title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄序
聖天子御極之三十有七年戊午
秋維大比之期天下士挾策
就試者所在雲集應天府府
尹臣鏜府丞臣時先期以考
試官
請迨閏七月戊寅
===
上命侍讀臣景淳臣僎往司試事時
臣鏜既晉南京大理寺卿臣
時職司提調乃繕垣宇飾供
具幣聘四方校官君教諭臣
奏臣金臣書臣育煦臣宗德臣朝恩
臣槐臣守齋俾同考試監試則
御史臣歩瀛臣宗舜廉內外各務
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序

聖天子御極之三十有七年戊午，秋，維大比之期，天下士挾策就試者，所在雲集。應天府府尹臣鏜、府丞臣時先期以考試官請。迨閏七月戊寅，上命侍讀臣景淳、臣僎往司試事。時，臣鏜既晉南京大理寺卿，臣時職司提調，乃繕垣宇，飾供具，幣聘四方校官君教諭臣奏、臣金、臣書、臣育煦、臣宗德、臣朝恩、臣槐、臣守齋，俾同考試。監試則御史臣歩瀛、臣宗舜廉內外，各務
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the thirty-seventh year of the sagely Son of Heaven’s reign, the wuwu year [1558], the time came for the triennial examination. Throughout the realm, scholars bearing their writings gathered like clouds wherever examinations were held. Your servants Tang, Prefect of Yingtian, and Shi, Vice Prefect, submitted a request in advance for the appointment of Examiners. On the wuyin day of the intercalary seventh month, His Majesty ordered your servants Jingchun and Zhuan, Readers-in-waiting, to go and direct the examination.

By this time, your servant Tang had been promoted to Minister of the Court of Judicial Review at Nanjing. Your servant Shi served as Proctor: he repaired the walls and buildings, put the requisite furnishings in order, and offered gifts to engage educational officials from various places—the Instructors, your servants Zou, Jin, Shu, Yuxu, Zongde, Chao’en, Huai, and Shouzhai—to serve as Associate Examiners. For oversight of the examination, the Censors, your servants Buying and Zongshun, inspected affairs within and outside the examination compound, each striving to…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
精白乃心慮慶祝舊加慶乃今
提學御史臣〔挐〕及六館諸生
所選士五千有奇三試之晝
夜繙閱遵
制額拔士百三十五人并錄其
文之優者以
獻臣〔景淳〕謹拜手稽首序其端臣
===
惟帝王之興雖神聖天縱其
臣莫及莫不以求士爲先務
取士之法雖代不相沿然要
在得賢輔治則一而已矣臣
�god奉
命而南下潞河涉大江見大木
之浮江而来也翩若游龍則
punctuated:
精白乃心，慮慶祝舊加慶。乃今提學御史臣〔挐〕及六館諸生所選士五千有奇，三試之晝夜繙閱，遵制額拔士百三十五人，并錄其文之優者以獻。臣〔景淳〕謹拜手稽首，序其端。
臣惟帝王之興，雖神聖天縱，其臣莫及，莫不以求士爲先務。取士之法，雖代不相沿，然要在得賢輔治，則一而已矣。臣�god奉命而南，下潞河，涉大江，見大木之浮江而来也，翩若游龍，則
translation_en:
…made their hearts pure and sincere [the following phrase, 慮慶祝舊加慶, is unclear]. Now the candidates selected by your servant 〔Na [?]〕, the Education Censor, together with students of the Six Colleges, numbered more than five thousand. We read their papers day and night through the three examination sessions and, following the quota prescribed by imperial regulation, selected 135 men. We also transcribed the best of their compositions for presentation to Your Majesty. Your servant 〔Jingchun〕 reverently bows with clasped hands and knocks his head to the ground, placing this preface at the beginning.
Your servant considers that, whenever emperors and kings have arisen, although Heaven endowed them with sagely wisdom beyond the reach of their ministers, they invariably made seeking worthy men their foremost task. Although methods of selecting men have varied from dynasty to dynasty, their essential purpose has been one and the same: to obtain worthy men to assist in government. Your servant [corrupt text: �god] received the command and traveled south, descending the Lu River and crossing the Great River. Seeing great timbers floating down the river, gliding like swimming dragons, I then…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
竊嘆曰嗟乎此真隆棟之材
其成非一二歲月之積也方
其隱於深山伏於遠方非假
左右爲之先容然人臣將
天子之命不遠數千里求之躬督
率而運致焉惟材之適用故
木無求于人而人求之也士
之大材晚成而耻於求售亦
何異于此詩曰周王壽考遐
不作人士固有待而興也
===
南畿在今猶周豐鎬鍾山石城
龍蟠虎踞巘業雲表長江渾
浩則西起岷蜀而東達於海
形勢之雄風氣之完固人材
punctuated:
竊嘆曰：「嗟乎！此真隆棟之材，其成非一二歲月之積也。方其隱於深山，伏於遠方，非假左右爲之先容，然人臣將天子之命，不遠數千里求之，躬督率而運致焉。惟材之適用，故木無求于人，而人求之也。士之大材晚成而耻於求售，亦何異于此？詩曰：『周王壽考，遐不作人。』士固有待而興也。」
南畿在今猶周豐鎬，鍾山石城，龍蟠虎踞，巘業雲表；長江渾浩，則西起岷蜀而東達於海。形勢之雄，風氣之完，固人材
translation_en:
…I privately exclaimed: “Ah! Here indeed is timber fit for a lofty ridgepole. Its growth is no mere accumulation of a year or two. While it lay hidden deep in the mountains, concealed in distant places, it did not rely on those close to the throne to recommend it beforehand. Yet an official, bearing the Son of Heaven’s command, thought nothing of traveling several thousand li to seek it, personally supervising its transport and delivery. It is solely because the timber is fit for use that the tree makes no appeal to men, but men seek it out. How are scholars of great ability, who mature late and feel ashamed to offer themselves for employment, any different? The Book of Odes says: ‘May the king of Zhou live long! Does he not nurture men of talent?’ Scholars indeed await the right occasion to rise.”
The Southern Metropolitan Region (Nanji) today is like Feng and Hao under the Zhou. Zhongshan and Shicheng stand like a coiling dragon and a crouching tiger, their peaks towering above the clouds [?]. The mighty, surging Yangzi River rises to the west in Min and Shu and reaches the sea to the east. With its commanding terrain and the fullness of its vital influences, it is surely a place where talented men…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之藪也我
聖天子一德格
天
壽考之隆且將遠邁周文則多士
之生此
纔服者寧不足以楨王國與周
士四休哉夫士不求則遺於
===
山林能求則增重廟堂臣故
於求大木者有感也既入鎖
院閱多士之文明辨者可以
觀識深醇者可以觀養雄剛
者可以觀才愽大者可以觀
器則相顧私喜庶幾隆棟之
材其在是乎昔人謂拔十得
punctuated:
之藪也。我聖天子一德格天，壽考之隆且將遠邁周文，則多士之生此纔服者，寧不足以楨王國，與周士四休哉？夫士不求則遺於山林，能求則增重廟堂。臣故於求大木者有感也。
既入鎖院，閱多士之文，明辨者可以觀識，深醇者可以觀養，雄剛者可以觀才，愽大者可以觀器，則相顧私喜：庶幾隆棟之材，其在是乎？昔人謂拔十得
translation_en:
…a gathering place for talent. Our sagely Son of Heaven, through his undivided virtue, reaches Heaven; the fullness of his longevity will far surpass even that of King Wen of Zhou. Could the many scholars born in this region [?] fail to serve as pillars of the royal realm and rival the glory of the scholars of Zhou [?]? If scholars are not sought out, they remain overlooked among the mountains and forests; if they are successfully sought out, they lend weight to the court. Thus your servant was moved by the search for great timber.
After entering the examination compound in confinement and reading the compositions of the many scholars, we could discern understanding in those that were clear and discriminating, cultivation in those that were profound and sound, talent in those that were vigorous and firm, and capacity in those that were broad and ample. We looked at one another with quiet delight: might the timber for lofty ridgepoles be found here? A man of old said, “Select ten and obtain…”

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
五臣不敢必即十得一焉亦
可以報
聖明逭後責矣然臣猶有懼焉竊
思一命之士皆勤簿書供職
守不敢無事而食以干曠官
之罰臣久塵侍從無所短長
獨玆校士可藉以報
===
國然力可勉而盡也知人之哲
不可强而能也今獨執一日
之文以求天下之士臣懼其
失之也夫江左自昔多才況
今爲首善之地重以
聖天子久道之化漸漬洋溢浹於
人心士生斯時沉潛六籍馳
punctuated: 五，臣不敢必，即十得一焉，亦可以報聖明、逭後責矣。然臣猶有懼焉。竊思一命之士，皆勤簿書，供職守，不敢無事而食，以干曠官之罰。臣久塵侍從，無所短長，獨玆校士，可藉以報國。然力可勉而盡也，知人之哲，不可强而能也。今獨執一日之文，以求天下之士，臣懼其失之也。夫江左自昔多才，況今爲首善之地，重以聖天子久道之化，漸漬洋溢，浹於人心。士生斯時，沉潛六籍，馳
translation_en:
…five out of ten, your servant dares not promise; yet even if one worthy man were found among ten, this would suffice to repay Your Majesty’s sagacity and avert later reproach. Still, your servant has misgivings. I reflect that even men holding the lowest official rank diligently attend to registers and documents and discharge their duties. They dare not draw their sustenance without doing any work and thereby incur punishment for neglect of office. Your servant has long unworthily served among Your Majesty’s attendants, without any accomplishment to speak of. Only this task of examining scholars offers a means of repaying the state. Yet while one can exert oneself to the utmost, the discernment needed to judge men cannot be attained by force of effort. Now, seeking worthy men throughout the realm solely on the evidence of a single day’s writing, your servant fears errors of judgment.
Jiangzuo has abounded in talent since antiquity. Moreover, it is now a place foremost in moral cultivation, further nurtured by the sagely Son of Heaven’s enduring rule: its transforming influence gradually permeates, spreads abundantly, and penetrates people’s hearts. Scholars born in this age immerse themselves deeply in the Six Classics and range…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
騁百家咸斐然有
帝臣之思其待舉有司者誠皆一
時之良顧器識傑然兼綜文
武堪以論思帷幄鎮定疆圉
者則代不數人耳
國家設科取士垂二百年每三
歲輒論士於鄉而賓興之雖
===
兼容博愛一藝益收亦冀有
傑然之材出是途可爲
社稷之衞也臣今殫竭心力庶幾
遇之乃或甄別不明有隆棟
之材棄而不收則臣罪大矣
臣嘗閲傳記見古来賢士適
不逢時雖有輔世之略亦沉
punctuated:
騁百家，咸斐然有帝臣之思。其待舉有司者，誠皆一時之良。顧器識傑然，兼綜文武，堪以論思帷幄、鎮定疆圉者，則代不數人耳。
國家設科取士，垂二百年，每三歲輒論士於鄉而賓興之。雖兼容博愛，一藝益收，亦冀有傑然之材出是途，可爲社稷之衞也。臣今殫竭心力，庶幾遇之。乃或甄別不明，有隆棟之材，棄而不收，則臣罪大矣。
臣嘗閲傳記，見古来賢士適不逢時，雖有輔世之略，亦沉
translation_en:
…range widely through the Hundred Schools, all displaying literary accomplishment and aspiring to serve as ministers of the Emperor. Those awaiting recommendation by the responsible officials are indeed all worthy men of their time. Yet men of outstanding capacity and discernment, versed in both civil and military affairs, fit to deliberate and counsel in the command tent and to secure the frontiers, number only a few in any generation.
The dynasty has maintained examinations to select officials for nearly two hundred years. Every three years, it assesses scholars in their home regions, honors them as guests, and advances them. Although it embraces men broadly and generously, accepting even those with a single accomplishment [?], it also hopes that outstanding talents will emerge through this route to defend the altars of soil and grain. Your servant now exhausts his energies in the hope of finding such men. Should my discrimination prove wanting, so that talent fit to serve as a great roof beam is discarded rather than selected, my culpability would be grave indeed.
Your servant has read historical accounts and biographies and seen how worthy scholars of antiquity, happening to live in unpropitious times, possessed strategies for aiding the age yet sank into…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
淪不克自見輒掩卷太息謂
士誠耻於自售縉紳之徒身
當其前不克推挽使國家收
得士之益賢士慰彚征之望
竊位之譏誠不可逭也臣今
謬當校士之任實當其前矣
乃不克推挽使奇偉倜儻之
===
士不獲進則何以謝天下今
多士之獲舉也亦有可以棟
明堂而任天下之重者乎記
曰夫學官先事士先志今多
士方與計偕雖未及試之政
事而志之所存不可謂不先
定也昔伊尹耕于有莘而堯
punctuated: 淪不克自見，輒掩卷太息，謂士誠耻於自售，縉紳之徒身當其前，不克推挽，使國家收得士之益，賢士慰彚征之望，竊位之譏誠不可逭也。臣今謬當校士之任，實當其前矣，乃不克推挽，使奇偉倜儻之士不獲進，則何以謝天下？今多士之獲舉也，亦有可以棟明堂而任天下之重者乎？記曰：「夫學，官先事，士先志。」今多士方與計偕，雖未及試之政事，而志之所存，不可謂不先定也。昔伊尹耕于有莘，而堯
translation_en:
…languished in obscurity, unable to make themselves known. I would close the book and sigh deeply, reflecting that worthy men indeed feel ashamed to promote themselves. If members of the official class, finding such men before them, fail to recommend and advance them—so that the state may benefit from obtaining worthy men and those men may fulfill their hope of advancing together—they truly cannot escape the reproach of occupying office without deserving it. Your servant has now been undeservedly entrusted with evaluating candidates and indeed stands in this very position. If I fail to recommend and advance them, leaving men of exceptional talent and unfettered spirit unable to rise, how could I answer to all under Heaven?
Among the many scholars now selected, are there men capable of serving as ridgepoles of the Hall of Enlightenment and bearing the weight of the realm? The Record of Rites says: “In learning, officials give priority to their duties, and scholars to their aspirations.” These scholars are now about to travel to the capital with the tribute delegation. Although they have not yet been tested in government affairs, their aspirations must already be firmly settled. In former times, Yi Yin tilled the fields at Youshen, yet Yao…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
舜君民之略已定於中此真
能尚志者也其次則諸葛孔
明之於漢范希文之於宋皆
篤於道義卓然不以成敗利
鈍貳其心亦伊尹之流亞也
今多士豈無志伊尹之志者
乎使平居而志不先定臨事
===
而氣隨以奪即才敏過人俾
當大任必有棟撓之虞復何
取焉臣令校士期於自盡復
以定志勗多士庶多士以古
人自期則亦不負斯舉也
翰林院侍讀瞿景淳謹序
punctuated:
舜君民之略已定於中，此真能尚志者也。其次，則諸葛孔明之於漢、范希文之於宋，皆篤於道義，卓然不以成敗利鈍貳其心，亦伊尹之流亞也。今多士豈無志伊尹之志者乎？使平居而志不先定，臨事而氣隨以奪，即才敏過人，俾當大任，必有棟撓之虞，復何取焉？臣令校士，期於自盡，復以定志勗多士。庶多士以古人自期，則亦不負斯舉也。
翰林院侍讀瞿景淳謹序。
translation_en:
…the plan to make his ruler and people like Yao and Shun was already settled within his heart. Here was someone truly able to exalt his aspirations. Next come Zhuge Kongming in his service to the Han and Fan Xiwen in his service to the Song. Both were steadfast in the Way and righteousness, standing firm without allowing success or failure, favorable or adverse circumstances, to divide their resolve. They, too, belonged among the worthy successors of Yi Yin. Among the many candidates today, surely there are some who aspire to Yi Yin’s aspirations? If a man has not settled his resolve beforehand in ordinary life, and his courage consequently fails when affairs confront him, then even if his ability and intelligence surpass others, entrusting him with great responsibilities will inevitably risk the bending of the ridgepole. What use would he then be?
Your servant, charged with examining the candidates [?], has sought to exert himself to the utmost, and further exhorts them to settle their resolve. I hope that they will take the men of antiquity as their standard, and thus prove worthy of their selection in this examination.
Preface respectfully composed by Qu Jingchun, Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:

南京河南道監察御史祝堯煥〔德徵山東濮州人癸丑進士〕
南京湖廣道監察御史王宗舜〔用中山西聞喜縣人癸丑進士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖叄拾柒年應天府鄉試。

提調官：
中順大夫、應天府府丞喻　時〔中甫，河南光州籍，江西豐城縣人，戊戌進士〕。

考試官：
翰林院侍讀瞿景淳〔師道，直隸常熟縣人，甲辰進士〕。
翰林院侍讀陳　陞〔晉甫，浙江餘姚縣人，辛丑進士〕。

同考試官：
河南汝寧府西平縣儒學教諭周士宏〔仲仁，廣東順德縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
福建泉州府同安縣儒學教諭吳　金〔礪伯，江西豐城縣人，丙午貢士〕。
河南開封府通許縣儒學教諭邵　書〔君詒，福建閩縣人，丙午貢士〕。

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
君子貞而不諒
上天之載無聲無臭至矣
爲人臣者懷仁義以事其君
易
乾始能以美利利天下不言所利大矣哉
觀乎人文以化成天下
天地設位而易行乎其中矣成性存存道
義之門
===
聖人南面而聽天下嚮明而治蓋取諸此
也
書
德惟善政政在養民
王懋昭大德建中于民以義制事以禮制
心
天子作民父母以爲天下王
凡人未見聖若不克見既見聖亦不克由
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
君子貞而不諒。
上天之載，無聲無臭，至矣。
爲人臣者，懷仁義以事其君。

易
乾始，能以美利利天下，不言所利，大矣哉！
觀乎人文，以化成天下。
天地設位，而易行乎其中矣。成性存存，道義之門。
聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此也。

書
德惟善政，政在養民。
王懋昭大德，建中于民，以義制事，以禮制心。
天子作民父母，以爲天下王。
凡人未見聖，若不克見；既見聖，亦不克由
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
The gentleman is steadfast in principle, but not inflexibly bound to his word.
The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor scent: this is the utmost perfection.
Those who serve as ministers cherish benevolence and righteousness in serving their ruler.

Book of Changes (Yijing)
Qian, the Creative, initiates things and can benefit all under Heaven with its excellent bounty, without speaking of the benefits it confers. Great indeed is it!
Observe human culture, thereby transforming and perfecting all under Heaven.
Heaven and Earth take their positions, and change operates between them. Continually preserving one's fully realized nature is the gateway to the Way and righteousness.
The sage faces south to hear the affairs of all under Heaven, turning toward the light to govern; this is presumably where he takes his model.

Book of Documents (Shujing)
Virtue consists in good government, and government lies in nourishing the people.
Let the king strive to manifest great virtue and establish the mean among the people, regulating affairs through righteousness and regulating the heart through ritual propriety.
The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother to the people, thereby becoming king of all under Heaven.
People, before seeing a sage, seem afraid that they will not manage to see him; once they have seen him, they still cannot follow …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖
詩
九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍稷重穋禾麻
菽麥嗟我農夫我稼既同上入執宮功
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋其始播
百穀
他山之石可以攻玉
虎拜稽首天子萬年
命于下國封建厥福
===
春秋
荊人來聘〔莊公二十有三年〕冬楚子使椒
來聘〔文公九年〕
夏公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯伐鄭圍
新城　秋楚人圍許諸侯遂救許　冬
公至自伐鄭〔俱僖公六年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕
夏叔孫豹會晉趙武楚屈建蔡公孫歸生
衛石惡陳孔奐鄭良霄許人曹人于宋
punctuated:
聖。

詩
九月築場圃，十月納禾稼：黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。嗟我農夫！我稼既同，上入執宮功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。
他山之石，可以攻玉。
虎拜稽首，天子萬年。
命于下國，封建厥福。

春秋
荊人來聘〔莊公二十有三年〕。冬，楚子使椒來聘〔文公九年〕。
夏，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。秋，楚人圍許，諸侯遂救許。冬，公至自伐鄭〔俱僖公六年〕。
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕。
夏，叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚屈建、蔡公孫歸生、衛石惡、陳孔奐、鄭良霄、許人、曹人于宋。
translation_en:
…the sage.

Book of Odes
In the ninth month we prepare the threshing grounds; in the tenth month we bring in the crops: broomcorn millet and foxtail millet, late-ripening and early-ripening grain, grain stalks, hemp, beans, and wheat. Ah, we farmers! Once our crops are gathered, we go up to undertake work on the buildings. By day you gather thatch; by night you twist ropes. Hurry up onto the roofs to repair them, for soon you must begin sowing the hundred grains.
Stones from other mountains can be used to polish jade.
Hu bows and knocks his head to the ground: may the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!
He gave his command to the states below, firmly establishing their blessings.

Spring and Autumn Annals
An envoy from Jing came on a diplomatic visit. 〔Twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang〕 In winter, the Viscount of Chu sent Jiao on a diplomatic visit. 〔Ninth year of Duke Wen〕
In summer, the Duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng; they besieged Xincheng. In autumn, the men of Chu besieged Xu, and the assembled lords thereupon went to Xu’s aid. In winter, the Duke returned from the campaign against Zheng. 〔All in the sixth year of Duke Xi〕
Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng〕
In summer, Shusun Bao met at Song with Zhao Wu of Jin, Qu Jian of Chu, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Shi E of Wei, Kong Huan of Chen, Liang Xiao of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao.

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
秋七月辛巳豹及諸侯之大夫盟于宋〔襄公二十有七年〕十有一月公如楚〔襄
公二十有八年〕夏楚子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯
許男徐子滕子頓子胡子沈子小邾子
宋世子佐淮夷會于申　秋七月楚子
蔡侯陳侯許男頓子胡子沈子淮夷伐
吳　遂滅頼〔俱昭公四年〕
禮記
天子之六府曰司土司木司水司草司器
司貨典司六職天子之六工曰土工金
工石工木工獸工草工典制六材
所以達天道順人情之大竇也
然則先王之爲樂也以法治也善則行象
德矣
和寧禮之用也此君臣上下之大義也
===
第貳場
論
孔子登太山而小天下
punctuated:
秋七月辛巳，豹及諸侯之大夫盟于宋〔襄公二十有七年〕。十有一月，公如楚〔襄公二十有八年〕。夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申。秋七月，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、許男、頓子、胡子、沈子、淮夷伐吳，遂滅頼〔俱昭公四年〕。

禮記
天子之六府，曰司土、司木、司水、司草、司器、司貨，典司六職。天子之六工，曰土工、金工、石工、木工、獸工、草工，典制六材。
所以達天道、順人情之大竇也。
然則先王之爲樂也，以法治也；善則行象德矣。
和寧，禮之用也；此君臣上下之大義也。

第貳場
論
孔子登太山而小天下
translation_en:
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the xinsi day, Bao and the high officers of the feudal lords concluded a covenant at Song. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xiang.〕 In the eleventh month, the duke went to Chu. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu 許, the Viscount of Xu 徐, the Viscount of Teng, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Shen 沈, the Viscount of Xiaozhu, Zuo, heir apparent of Song, and the Huai Yi met at Shen 申. In autumn, in the seventh month, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Baron of Xu 許, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Shen 沈, and the Huai Yi attacked Wu. They then destroyed Lai. 〔Both entries are from the fourth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Book of Rites
The Son of Heaven’s six offices are those responsible for land, wood, water, vegetation, implements, and valuables; they administer these six functions. The Son of Heaven’s six groups of craftsmen are workers in earth, metal, stone, wood, animal materials, and plant materials; they oversee the working of these six materials.
It is the great channel through which the Way of Heaven is realized and human feelings are followed.
Thus, the former kings made music to provide a model for good government; when it is good, its performance embodies virtue [?].
Harmony and tranquillity are the effects of ritual; this is the great principle governing ruler and minister, superior and subordinate.

Second Session
Discourse
Confucius ascended Mount Tai and found all under Heaven small.

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢定振窮養老之令詔〔文帝元年〕
擬唐以姚元之兼紫微令誥〔開元二年〕
擬
大朝門等成羣臣賀表
判語〔五條〕
舉用有過官吏
人戶以籍爲定
邊境申索軍需
軍民約會詞訟
修理橋梁道路
===
第叄場
策〔五道〕
問堯舜禹湯文武典謨訓誥之文不可尚
巳嗣是漢唐宋亦多英君誼辟而以文
見稱者何寡也獨唐太宗文至成帙論
者乃謂其雕奇鏤怪徒與騷人韻士爭
巧亦不足尚則文豈易言哉洪惟我
punctuated:
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢定振窮養老之令詔〔文帝元年〕。
擬唐以姚元之兼紫微令誥〔開元二年〕。
擬大朝門等成，羣臣賀表。

判語〔五條〕
舉用有過官吏。
人戶以籍爲定。
邊境申索軍需。
軍民約會詞訟。
修理橋梁道路。

第叄場
策〔五道〕
問：堯舜禹湯文武典謨訓誥之文，不可尚巳。嗣是漢唐宋亦多英君誼辟，而以文見稱者何寡也？獨唐太宗文至成帙，論者乃謂其雕奇鏤怪，徒與騷人韻士爭巧，亦不足尚。則文豈易言哉！洪惟我
translation_en:
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One question within this category [?].〕
Compose an edict in the name of the Han emperor establishing an ordinance to relieve the poor and support the aged. 〔First year of Emperor Wen’s reign.〕
Compose a proclamation in the name of the Tang emperor appointing Yao Yuanzhi concurrently as Director of the Secretariat. 〔Second year of the Kaiyuan reign.〕
Compose a congratulatory memorial from the assembled officials on the completion of Dachao Gate and other structures.

Legal judgments 〔Five items.〕
Recommending and appointing officials and clerks with previous offenses.
Determining household status by the registers.
Requests from the frontier for military supplies.
Arranging joint hearings of lawsuits involving military personnel and civilians.
Repairing bridges and roads.

Third Session
Policy questions 〔Five questions.〕
Question: The canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, and Kings Wen and Wu cannot be surpassed. Subsequently, the Han, Tang, and Song also had many outstanding sovereigns and righteous rulers; why, then, were so few renowned for their writings? The writings of Emperor Taizong of the Tang alone amounted to collected volumes, yet critics say that he carved out the unusual and embellished the bizarre, merely competing in ingenuity with poets and men of verse, and that his writings likewise do not merit esteem. Can writing, then, be discussed lightly? We reverently reflect upon our …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝躬提一旅不十年而成大業其武
功固獨高萬古矣然且
萬幾之暇
親灑宸翰凡大
詔令大
制勑大樂章大祝辭皆運心神以宣道妙莫不
震曜萬國懷柔百神至於記序之文詩
歌之作亦莫不根理致極體要而昭垂
訓典助宣聲教焉經天緯地之文直與帝王相
===
輝映於千古矣可得而陳其略歟當時
詹同樂韶鳳等
請而集之劉基宋濂郭傳又從而恭題其後
所以贊揚休美者至矣可得而舉其槩
歟逮我
聖上聖神文武雋古帝王而同符
聖祖
宸章睿藻炳若日星簡冊森嚴難以殫述可得
而鋪張其一二歟
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝躬提一旅，不十年而成大業，其武功固獨高萬古矣。然且萬幾之暇，親灑宸翰，凡大詔令、大制勑、大樂章、大祝辭，皆運心神以宣道妙，莫不震曜萬國，懷柔百神。至於記序之文、詩歌之作，亦莫不根理致、極體要，而昭垂訓典，助宣聲教焉。經天緯地之文，直與帝王相輝映於千古矣，可得而陳其略歟？當時詹同、樂韶鳳等請而集之，劉基、宋濂、郭傳又從而恭題其後，所以贊揚休美者至矣，可得而舉其槩歟？逮我聖上，聖神文武，雋古帝王而同符聖祖，宸章睿藻，炳若日星，簡冊森嚴，難以殫述，可得而鋪張其一二歟？
translation_en:
…Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, personally led a single brigade and in fewer than ten years accomplished the great enterprise of founding the dynasty. His martial achievements indeed stand unrivaled through all ages. Yet amid the countless affairs of government, he personally wielded the imperial brush. His great edicts and commands, proclamations and mandates, ceremonial musical compositions, and sacrificial prayers all drew upon his mind and spirit to reveal the mysteries of the Way. Without exception, they shed their brilliance upon the myriad states and conciliated the hundred spirits. His records and prefaces, poems and songs likewise were all rooted in principle and meaning and fully expressed essential substance. They illustriously bequeathed exemplary teachings and helped spread his moral influence. His writings, encompassing Heaven and Earth, shine alongside those of the ancient emperors and kings for all time. Can you set forth their principal features?
At the time, Zhan Tong, Yue Shaofeng, and others requested permission to compile these writings. Liu Ji, Song Lian, and Guo Chuan subsequently and reverently appended inscriptions, praising their excellence to the utmost. Can you give an outline of these appreciations?
Coming down to our present sovereign, sagely and divine, accomplished in civil and military affairs, he surpasses [?] the emperors and kings of antiquity and accords with the Sagely Ancestor. His imperial compositions and discerning literary expressions shine like the sun and stars; their collected volumes are imposing in their dignity, and it is difficult to describe them exhaustively. Can you expound upon one or two examples?

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇帝嘗諭侍臣以人心虛靈操而存之爲難
聖上心學之統乃見於
欽一之箴何其先後一揆也則文固有本歟
頃伏覩
聖上拳拳修攘之略文謨武烈於
聖祖赫然宣重光矣諸士服膺
聖訓有年必能識其大者敬悉心以對
問記稱禮之所尊尊其義也失其義陳其
數祝史之事也然隆古之時禮教明習
===
故雖祝史能知其數後世禮教衰缺禮
之義儒者猶能言之數則鮮有知者矣
是可以不素講歟今古禮之存於世者
惟三禮是孰講而孰傳之歟或謂聖經
不亡於秦火而大壞於漢儒然則漢儒
傳經之功可盡泯歟宋元諸儒有作古
禮經傳通解者有作三禮考註者亦有
愈於漢儒否歟漢時有古禮經出於魯
淹中漢儒無能傳者班孟堅獨深取之
punctuated:
皇帝嘗諭侍臣，以人心虛靈，操而存之爲難。聖上心學之統，乃見於《欽一之箴》，何其先後一揆也！則文固有本歟？頃伏覩聖上拳拳修攘之略，文謨武烈，於聖祖赫然宣重光矣。諸士服膺聖訓有年，必能識其大者，敬悉心以對。
問：記稱：「禮之所尊，尊其義也。失其義，陳其數，祝史之事也。」然隆古之時，禮教明習，故雖祝史能知其數。後世禮教衰缺，禮之義，儒者猶能言之；數則鮮有知者矣。是可以不素講歟？今古禮之存於世者，惟三禮，是孰講而孰傳之歟？或謂聖經不亡於秦火，而大壞於漢儒，然則漢儒傳經之功可盡泯歟？宋元諸儒有作《古禮經傳通解》者，有作《三禮考註》者，亦有愈於漢儒否歟？漢時有古禮經出於魯淹中，漢儒無能傳者，班孟堅獨深取之。
translation_en:
The Emperor once instructed his attendant officials that the human mind is empty and numinous, but that holding fast to it and preserving it is difficult. His Majesty’s succession to the tradition of learning concerning the mind is evident in the Admonition on Reverent Oneness (Qin yi zhi zhen). How perfectly the earlier and later sovereigns conform to a single standard! Does literary composition, then, indeed have a fundamental source? Recently, we have reverently witnessed His Majesty’s devoted attention to strategies for strengthening internal government and repelling external threats. His civil plans and martial achievements have splendidly renewed the brilliance of the Sagely Progenitor. You candidates have cherished the imperial teachings for years and must surely be able to discern their greater import. Apply your minds fully and reverently in answering.
Question: The Record of Rites states: “What is honored in ritual is its meaning. To lose its meaning and merely set out its particulars is the business of invocators and scribes.” Yet in high antiquity, ritual teachings were clearly understood and well practiced, so that even invocators and scribes knew their particulars. In later ages, ritual teachings declined and became incomplete. Confucian scholars could still discuss the meaning of ritual, but few knew its particulars. Can these be left without sustained study? Of the writings on ancient ritual surviving today, there are only the Three Ritual Classics. Who expounded them, and who transmitted them? Some say that the sages’ classics were not destroyed by the Qin fires but were gravely corrupted by Han Confucian scholars. Can the Han scholars’ merit in transmitting the classics therefore be entirely effaced? Among the Confucian scholars of the Song and Yuan, some composed the Comprehensive Explanation of the Classic and Commentaries on Ancient Ritual (Gu li jing zhuan tong jie), and others the Examination and Annotation of the Three Ritual Classics (San li kao zhu). Did any of them surpass the Han scholars? During the Han, an ancient Ritual Classic emerged from Yanzhong in Lu. None of the Han scholars could transmit it, but Ban Mengjian alone esteemed it highly …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
謂愈愛答等推士禮而致於天子然則十
七篇皆士禮歟非皆士禮孟堅何以云
爾歟作通解者欲取周禮禮記所載有
及於天子之事者以備儀禮之闕儻亦
孟堅之意歟今之言儀禮者既病其殘
闕而疑周禮者爲尤甚惟馬端臨之說
差得其中亦謂古今異宜而難行然則
諸儒之纂輯亦好古之過歟昔孔子嘗
思虞夏之質雖宋儒亦謂後聖有作必
===
不一如古禮之繁則好古者似亦不必
徒守其數也然諸儒愛禮之意則深矣
幸相與推明之□□□□當年不能究也
問作史者論事從□□□而立法欲嚴核故足
以信後世嚴故足以懲姦慝古之良史
未有不慎諸此者也春秋以來世之言
正統者何紛紛也正統之論始於歐陽
子蘇氏宗之而其論復有異同朱子作
資治通鑑綱目蓋宗乎溫公而復有異
punctuated:
謂愈愛答等推士禮而致於天子。然則十七篇皆士禮歟？非皆士禮，孟堅何以云爾歟？作《通解》者欲取《周禮》《禮記》所載有及於天子之事者，以備《儀禮》之闕，儻亦孟堅之意歟？今之言《儀禮》者既病其殘闕，而疑《周禮》者爲尤甚，惟馬端臨之說差得其中，亦謂古今異宜而難行。然則諸儒之纂輯亦好古之過歟？昔孔子嘗思虞夏之質，雖宋儒亦謂後聖有作，必不一如古禮之繁，則好古者似亦不必徒守其數也。然諸儒愛禮之意則深矣，幸相與推明之。□□□□當年不能究也。

問：作史者論事從□□□，而立法欲嚴。核故足以信後世，嚴故足以懲姦慝。古之良史，未有不慎諸此者也。《春秋》以來，世之言正統者何紛紛也？正統之論始於歐陽子，蘇氏宗之，而其論復有異同。朱子作《資治通鑑綱目》，蓋宗乎溫公，而復有異
translation_en:
…held it superior to the extrapolation of the rites for ordinary officers to the Son of Heaven by Ai Da and others [?]. Were all seventeen chapters, then, rites for ordinary officers? If they were not all such rites, why did Mengjian say this? The author of the Comprehensive Explanation wished to draw upon matters concerning the Son of Heaven recorded in the Rites of Zhou and the Record of Rites to supply what was missing from the Ceremonies and Rites. Might this also have been Mengjian’s intention? Those who discuss the Ceremonies and Rites today already deplore its fragmentary condition, while doubts concerning the Rites of Zhou are still greater. Only Ma Duanlin’s account comes somewhat close to a balanced judgment; yet he too says that circumstances in antiquity and the present differ, making these rites difficult to practice. Were the compilations of the various scholars, then, also the result of an excessive fondness for antiquity? Confucius once yearned for the simplicity of Yu and Xia. Even the Song scholars said that, should another sage arise, his arrangements would certainly not reproduce all the complexity of ancient ritual. It would thus seem that admirers of antiquity need not merely adhere to its prescribed particulars. Nevertheless, these scholars’ devotion to ritual was profound. Please work together to elucidate this. [Four illegible characters] could not fully investigate it at the time [?].

Question: Those who write history, in discussing events, follow [three illegible characters], while seeking rigor in establishing their principles. Accuracy makes their work trustworthy for later generations; rigor enables it to chastise the wicked and depraved. No good historian of antiquity failed to exercise care in these matters. Since the Spring and Autumn Annals, why have discussions of legitimate succession been so numerous and divergent? The discussion of legitimate succession began with Master Ouyang. Master Su followed him, but their arguments nevertheless contained points of agreement and disagreement. When Master Zhu compiled the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, he presumably followed the Duke of Wen, yet again there were differences…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同近世方氏著論復謂朱子猶有未盡
亦可舉其說而折衷之歟夫以秦爲閏
以梁爲僞私東晉者訴後魏爲虜私後
魏者訴東晉爲夷歐陽子嘗辨之矣然
進秦續周以周秦漢晉隋唐爲正統則
其得國果若是班歟如徒以其一天下
而予之則胡元亦將予之否歟朱子之
叙正統蓋本之歐陽子不得已而予之
者也故雖予之正統而書法之嚴亦有
===
與方氏所論相出入者亦可舉而言歟
夫知方氏之言雖異於朱子而實與朱
子相出入則方氏非徒好異矣請言之
以觀稽古之學
問賢才國之所恃以致理也必知之明而
後用之當故宋臣王君援劉邵人物志
進說蓋以邵之書主於詳察人物於任
官擇材之法有可觀焉其言曰人之質
量中和最貴中和之質必平淡無味故
punctuated:
同。近世方氏著論，復謂朱子猶有未盡，亦可舉其說而折衷之歟？夫以秦爲閏，以梁爲僞，私東晉者訴後魏爲虜，私後魏者訴東晉爲夷，歐陽子嘗辨之矣。然進秦續周，以周秦漢晉隋唐爲正統，則其得國果若是班歟？如徒以其一天下而予之，則胡元亦將予之否歟？朱子之叙正統，蓋本之歐陽子，不得已而予之者也。故雖予之正統，而書法之嚴，亦有與方氏所論相出入者，亦可舉而言歟？夫知方氏之言雖異於朱子，而實與朱子相出入，則方氏非徒好異矣。請言之，以觀稽古之學。

問：賢才，國之所恃以致理也。必知之明，而後用之當。故宋臣王君援劉邵《人物志》進說，蓋以邵之書主於詳察人物，於任官擇材之法有可觀焉。其言曰：「人之質量，中和最貴。中和之質，必平淡無味，故
translation_en:
…differences. In recent times, Master Fang has written a treatise arguing further that Master Zhu’s account still leaves some matters unresolved. Can you set out his arguments and weigh them to arrive at a balanced judgment? As for treating Qin as an intercalary dynasty and Liang as illegitimate, those partial to the Eastern Jin denounce the Later Wei as northern barbarians, while those partial to the Later Wei denounce the Eastern Jin as barbarians. Master Ouyang has already examined these claims. Yet if Qin is advanced to succeed Zhou, and Zhou, Qin, Han, Jin, Sui, and Tang are treated as the legitimate succession, did their acquisition of the realm truly warrant such ranking [?]? If this status is granted merely because they unified All under Heaven, should it also be granted to the Mongol Yuan? Master Zhu’s account of the legitimate succession was based on Master Ouyang’s; he granted this status because he had no alternative. Thus, although he accorded them legitimacy, the rigor of his historical wording also shows points of agreement and disagreement with Master Fang’s arguments. Can you cite and discuss these? If one understands that, although Master Fang’s statements differ from Master Zhu’s, they actually overlap with them as well as diverge, then Master Fang was not merely seeking novelty. Explain this, so that we may assess your learning in the study of antiquity.

Question: Worthy and talented men are what the state relies upon to achieve good government. Only after their qualities are clearly understood can they be employed appropriately. Thus Master Wang, a minister of the Song, drew upon Liu Shao’s Treatise on Human Character (Renwu zhi) when presenting his views. This was presumably because Shao’s book concentrates on examining people’s characteristics in detail and offers insights into methods of appointing officials and selecting talent. It says: “Among people’s inherent qualities and capacities, balance and harmony are most prized. A balanced and harmonious disposition must be bland and without distinctive flavor; thus …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
能調成五材變化應節是故觀人察質
必先察其平淡而後求其聰明但天之
生人兼材常少而偏材實多今考其志
流業十二而其人其任各有專指可得
而詳言歟其所謂國體一流果亦同於
衆流歟其亦有可指而議者歟其曰偏
材之人長於辦一官而短於爲一國又
曰能識同體之善而或失異量之美論
果當歟否歟其他分英雄於二用混直
===
訐於一塗謂偏材之性不可移轉謂慈
而不仁而不恤謂觀其感變以知常
度謂觀其所短以知所長謂察譽有偏
頗之謬謂接物有愛惡之惑言雖不同
而同於詳察人物第不知有合於聖賢
之論否耶其時散騎侍郎盛稱劭材史
臣亦曰邵該覽學籍文質周洽則其論
似有足多者然則用才者果可據是歟
抑別有其道歟願究言之以備官人之
punctuated: 能調成五材，變化應節。是故觀人察質，必先察其平淡，而後求其聰明。但天之生人，兼材常少，而偏材實多。今考其志，流業十二，而其人其任各有專指，可得而詳言歟？其所謂國體一流，果亦同於衆流歟？其亦有可指而議者歟？其曰：「偏材之人，長於辦一官，而短於爲一國。」又曰：「能識同體之善，而或失異量之美。」論果當歟，否歟？其他分英雄於二用，混直訐於一塗，謂偏材之性不可移轉，謂慈而不仁而不恤，謂觀其感變以知常度，謂觀其所短以知所長，謂察譽有偏頗之謬，謂接物有愛惡之惑，言雖不同，而同於詳察人物。第不知有合於聖賢之論否耶？其時散騎侍郎盛稱劭材，史臣亦曰：「邵該覽學籍，文質周洽。」則其論似有足多者。然則用才者果可據是歟？抑別有其道歟？願究言之，以備官人之
translation_en: …can harmonize the five kinds of talent and adapt to changing circumstances as occasion demands. Thus, when observing people and examining their qualities, one must first examine their evenness and lack of distinctive flavor, and only then seek out their intelligence and discernment. Yet among those born under Heaven, people combining several talents are always few, while those with specialized talents are indeed numerous. Now, examining his Treatise on Personalities (Renwu zhi), we find twelve categories of vocational aptitude, each referring to particular kinds of people and particular responsibilities. Can these be explained in detail? Is his category of “capacity for national leadership” really on the same footing as the other categories? Are there also points here that can be singled out for discussion? He says: “People with specialized talents excel at discharging the duties of a single office but fall short in governing an entire state.” He also says: “They can recognize the merits of those of the same disposition, yet may overlook the excellence of those with different capacities.” Are these judgments sound or not? Elsewhere, he distinguishes ying and xiong—outstanding intellect and outstanding valor—as two kinds of capability, but places forthrightness and accusatory faultfinding on the same path. He says that the nature of specialized talent cannot be changed; speaks of being “kind yet not benevolent and not compassionate” [?]; advocates observing people’s responses to change to discern their constant standards, and observing their shortcomings to discern their strengths; and speaks of errors of partiality in assessing praise and the confusion caused by likes and dislikes in dealings with others. Though these statements differ, they all concern the close examination of people’s character and abilities. But do they accord with the teachings of the sages and worthies? A Cavalier Attendant of his time highly praised Liu Shao’s talents, and the historian also said: “Shao read widely in scholarly writings; his literary accomplishments and substantive qualities were comprehensive and well integrated.” His judgments would therefore seem to have much to commend them. Can those who employ talented people truly rely on this work, then? Or is there another way? Please discuss this thoroughly, to assist in appointing men to office…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
助
問鹽筴之征非古也蓋自管仲始嗣後若
漢之桑弘羊孔僅唐之劉晏皆祖之以
裕國更數世而不廢豈其法亦不可廢
歟大夫文學之議元𢇁甄琛之言人持
一端將安所取衷歟我
國家富有天下鹽筴所入不當常賦百一然
法凡幾變而議之者亦凡幾人矣今之
餘鹽與正課並行誠非
===
國初之舊也或欲變通斂法或欲盡復正課
議雖美而難行者何歟夫擁山澤之利
而可以寬農民之征誠經國之所當講
者然君子恒有不盡利之慮不知如之
何而可以善其後歟
國初之征商蓋甚薄而用常有餘今之征商
蓋已厚而用猶不足何歟夫糜財之大
者莫大於吏兵之冗自多事以來吏兵
之增置者亦多矣不知亦可裁省歟抑
punctuated:
助。

問：鹽筴之征，非古也，蓋自管仲始。嗣後若漢之桑弘羊、孔僅，唐之劉晏，皆祖之以裕國。更數世而不廢，豈其法亦不可廢歟？大夫、文學之議，元𢇁、甄琛之言，人持一端，將安所取衷歟？我國家富有天下，鹽筴所入不當常賦百一，然法凡幾變，而議之者亦凡幾人矣。今之餘鹽與正課並行，誠非國初之舊也。或欲變通斂法，或欲盡復正課，議雖美而難行者何歟？夫擁山澤之利，而可以寬農民之征，誠經國之所當講者。然君子恒有不盡利之慮，不知如之何而可以善其後歟？

國初之征商，蓋甚薄，而用常有餘；今之征商，蓋已厚，而用猶不足，何歟？夫糜財之大者，莫大於吏兵之冗。自多事以來，吏兵之增置者亦多矣。不知亦可裁省歟？抑
translation_en:
…assistance.

Question: The levy arising from the salt monopoly was not an institution of antiquity; it began with Guan Zhong. Subsequently, men such as Sang Hongyang and Kong Jin of the Han and Liu Yan of the Tang all followed his example to enrich the state. It has endured through successive ages without abolition. Could it be that this system cannot be abolished? In the arguments of the grandee and the learned scholars, and in the statements of Yuan Si [?] and Zhen Chen, each upheld one side. Where should we seek a balanced judgment? Our dynasty possesses the wealth of all under Heaven, and salt-monopoly receipts do not amount to one hundredth of regular tax revenues. Yet how many times has the system changed, and how many people have debated it! The present practice of levying on surplus salt alongside the regular salt quota is certainly not the system established at the dynasty’s founding. Some wish to modify the methods of collection; others wish to restore the regular quota system in full. Why are these proposals, though admirable, difficult to implement? To command the profits of mountains and marshes and thereby lighten the levies on farmers is certainly something that those who govern the state ought to consider. Yet the gentleman is always concerned to avoid extracting every last profit. How, then, can the system be brought to a satisfactory outcome?

At the dynasty’s founding, taxes on commerce were very light, yet revenues regularly exceeded expenditure. Today, taxes on commerce are already heavy, yet revenues still fall short of expenditure. Why is this? Among the great sources of wasted funds, none is greater than supernumerary officials and soldiers. Since troubled times began, many additional officials and soldiers have been appointed or recruited. Could their numbers also be reduced? Or …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
可裁省而無鉠於事則財不可勝用非
特鹽筴可寛也頗詳著於篇將採而
獻焉
punctuated: 可裁省而無鉠於事，則財不可勝用，非特鹽筴可寛也。頗詳著於篇，將採而獻焉。
translation_en: …if these can be reduced without impairing affairs [?], then financial resources will be inexhaustible, and it will be possible to ease more than just the salt levies. Set out your views in some detail in your essay; they will be selected and presented to the throne.

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子貞而不諒
余簃中
同考試官教諭潘　批〔題本難作類多勦竊〕
〔陳言未見真切此篇獨得語意錄之〕
同考試官教諭陳　批〔貞諒二字分别明悉〕
〔而詞復精雅蔚發佳士也〕
考試官侍讀陳　批〔詞徹意沖〕
===
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔簡當〕
聖人論君子之守惟其正而無容心焉甚矣君
子大居正也容心焉則害於正矣亦何貴於守
之固哉夫子蓋慮夫執小信者之害道也故曰
人之守一也有見於理而守之必固者謂之貞
無見於理而守之必固者謂之諒貞雖有似於
諒而害貞者必諒也君子之於天下吾見其貞
而不諒焉幾微之際辨之已審而所以爲制事
之本者恒運之以理而不流素履之往養之已

聖人論君子之守，惟其正而無容心焉。甚矣，君子大居正也！容心焉，則害於正矣，亦何貴於守之固哉？夫子蓋慮夫執小信者之害道也，故曰：人之守一也，有見於理而守之必固者謂之貞，無見於理而守之必固者謂之諒。貞雖有似於諒，而害貞者必諒也。君子之於天下，吾見其貞而不諒焉。幾微之際，辨之已審，而所以爲制事之本者，恒運之以理而不流；素履之往，養之已
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“The gentleman is steadfast in righteousness, but not rigidly faithful to his word.”
Yu Yizhong 余簃中

Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: “The topic is inherently difficult to handle. Most essays plagiarize stale expressions and fail to convey its meaning truly and precisely. This essay alone captures the sense of the saying; it is selected for inclusion.”

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The distinction between ‘steadfastness in righteousness’ and ‘rigid fidelity to one’s word’ is explained clearly and fully. The language is also refined, elegant, and richly expressive. This is a fine scholar.”

Examiner Chen, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: “The language is lucid, the meaning deep and tranquil.”

Examiner Qu, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: “Concise and apt.”

In discussing what the gentleman holds fast to, the Sage requires only that it be right, with no place for private preconceptions. How greatly the gentleman prizes abiding in what is right! If private preconceptions intrude, they impair rightness; what value, then, is there in holding fast so firmly? The Master was surely concerned that insistence on petty fidelity would harm the Way. Thus he said: People alike hold fast to something. To perceive principle and necessarily hold firmly to it is called steadfastness in righteousness; to lack insight into principle yet insist on holding firmly is called rigid fidelity to one’s word. Although steadfastness in righteousness may resemble rigid fidelity, what undermines such steadfastness is invariably rigid fidelity. In the gentleman’s dealings with the world, I see steadfastness in righteousness, without rigid fidelity to his word. At the point of the subtlest stirrings, his discernment is already exact; what serves as the basis for his handling of affairs he constantly applies according to principle, without drifting astray. In the course of his customary conduct, his cultivation has already …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
定而所以爲立身之要者恒一之以理而不亂
方其有所見而信之篤也蓋有卓乎不回而在
外之得失舉不足以易之者矣然惟信以理也
未始有成心也時之不齊則將與時偕行以求
夫理之所安而又何必焉方其有所得而執之
堅也蓋有確乎不拔而在外之榮辱舉不足以
奪之者矣然惟執夫理也未始有偏主也勢之
不一則將與勢推移以求夫理之至當而又何
固焉蓋將自其不變者觀之則堅凝之操未始
===
少渝所以立天下之坊而不至於失已者此也
自其至變者觀之則圓神之用未始少滯所以
通天下之故而不至於違時者亦此也此君子
之固守蓋貞也而非所以爲諒也雖不必於信
義以成信而信亦在其中者也若必於諒焉則
有非所信而信焉者矣叶此君子之道所以爲
無斁歟抑是貞也推其極雖孔子之時中亦不
外此孟子所以顯學孔子以其無可無不可而
□適於道之可也後之君子必明以察之健以
punctuated: 定，而所以爲立身之要者，恒一之以理而不亂。方其有所見而信之篤也，蓋有卓乎不回，而在外之得失舉不足以易之者矣。然惟信以理也，未始有成心也。時之不齊，則將與時偕行，以求夫理之所安，而又何必焉？方其有所得而執之堅也，蓋有確乎不拔，而在外之榮辱舉不足以奪之者矣。然惟執夫理也，未始有偏主也。勢之不一，則將與勢推移，以求夫理之至當，而又何固焉？蓋將自其不變者觀之，則堅凝之操未始少渝，所以立天下之坊而不至於失已者，此也。自其至變者觀之，則圓神之用未始少滯，所以通天下之故而不至於違時者，亦此也。此君子之固守，蓋貞也，而非所以爲諒也。雖不必於信，義以成信，而信亦在其中者也。若必於諒焉，則有非所信而信焉者矣。叶此君子之道所以爲無斁歟？抑是貞也，推其極，雖孔子之時中亦不外此。孟子所以顯學孔子，以其無可無不可，而□適於道之可也。後之君子必明以察之，健以
translation_en:
…is settled, and what constitutes the essential basis for establishing oneself is always unified through principle and never confused. When the gentleman perceives something and believes in it deeply, he stands firm and unyielding: external gains and losses are wholly insufficient to change him. Yet because his belief accords with principle, he has no preconceived commitment. As circumstances differ with the times, he moves along with the times, seeking what accords with principle. What, then, would he insist upon unconditionally? When he has attained an understanding and holds to it firmly, he is steadfast and immovable: external honors and disgraces are wholly insufficient to wrest it from him. Yet because it is principle that he holds to, he has no partial attachment. As situations vary, he adapts to their changes, seeking what is most fitting according to principle. What, then, would he cling to rigidly?
Viewed from the standpoint of what does not change in him, his steadfast integrity never wavers in the slightest. This is how he establishes a bulwark for the world without losing himself. Viewed from the standpoint of his utmost adaptability, his flexible and subtle responsiveness never suffers the slightest impediment. This, too, is how he responds to the affairs of the world without falling out of accord with the times. Such firm adherence by the gentleman is principled constancy, rather than rigid fidelity to one's word. Although he does not insist unconditionally on keeping his word, he fulfills good faith through righteousness, and good faith is thus contained within it. If, however, one insists on rigid fidelity, one may keep faith where faith ought not to be kept. Is this [?] why the gentleman's Way is inexhaustible?
Moreover, when this principled constancy is carried to its fullest extent, even Confucius's attainment of the mean as circumstances require does not lie beyond it. The reason Mengzi expressly took Confucius as his model was that Confucius held nothing unconditionally permissible or impermissible, but □ accorded with what the Way permitted [?]. Gentlemen of later ages must scrutinize this with clarity and, with strength, …

之時士多詭隨稍知自好者率硜硜焉矜小信
而忽大義然則夫子斯言其有所感也夫其有
所警也夫
上天之載無聲無臭至矣
張炳

君子與天合其德也然則不顯之妙非天道之
神其孰盡之子思自下學立心之始而推極於
此示人以聖修之極也蓋曰君子之學始於尚
絅之心而馴造於篤恭之盛則其德至矣吾嘗
擬之詩而不顯之妙未易言也必也如文王之

中庸引言君子之至德，惟天道之神盡之也。夫君子與天合其德也，然則不顯之妙，非天道之神，其孰盡之？子思自下學立心之始，而推極於此，示人以聖修之極也。蓋曰：君子之學，始於尚絅之心，而馴造於篤恭之盛，則其德至矣。吾嘗擬之詩，而不顯之妙未易言也。必也如文王之
translation_en:
…decide resolutely upon it; only then can one abide in steadfast rectitude. Otherwise, few avoid lapsing into mere insistence on keeping their word. In the Spring and Autumn period, many scholars followed others unscrupulously. Those who had some concern for their own integrity generally clung stubbornly to petty fidelity, taking pride in it while neglecting greater righteousness. These words of the Master must therefore have been prompted by something he observed! They must have been intended as a warning!

“The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell. This is perfection.”
Zhang Bing

Associate Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: 〔The reasoning is precise and thorough, and the writing fully brings it out.〕〔There are exceedingly few who write essays interpreting the Doctrine of the Mean as this author does.〕
Associate Examiner Zhou, an Instructor, comments: 〔The description of what is unmanifest is nearly exhaustive—a level that shallow learning cannot attain. I record this as a model for the many scholars.〕
Examiner Chen, a Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔The meaning of the topic is explained clearly and fully.〕
Examiner Qu, a Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔The writing shows thoughtful insight; it is no careless composition.〕

The Doctrine of the Mean quotes these words to explain that only the wondrous working of the Way of Heaven fully expresses the gentleman’s supreme virtue. The gentleman’s virtue accords with Heaven. Who, then, could fully express the subtlety of what is unmanifest, except through the wondrous working of the Way of Heaven? Zisi proceeds from the first establishment of purpose in elementary learning and carries his account to this ultimate point, showing people the highest attainment of sagely cultivation. His meaning is this: the gentleman’s learning begins with the disposition to wear a plain covering over his brocade and gradually reaches the fullness of profound reverence; then his virtue is consummate. I have sought to illustrate it through the Odes, but the subtlety of what is unmanifest is not easily expressed. Surely it must be something like the ode concerning King Wen’s …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
詩乎詩云上天之載無聲無臭夫物之可以形
求者皆顯也微之而至於聲臭則已入於無形
聲臭而猶曰無焉則淵乎其淵者也物之可以
象求者皆顯也微之而至於聲臭則已入於無
象聲臭而猶曰無焉則深乎其深者也詩之言
天如此以是言君子不顯篤恭之妙斯其至乎
蓋君子之篤恭也由人以合天而一敬之存存
者潛會其不言之真盡性以至命而一敬之亹
亹者默契其於穆之運存之爲中而大本立焉
===
一天之所以爲神也退藏之密雖未易窺觀天
之靜而無靜而聲臭之俱泯者則可以通其故
矣發之爲和而達道行焉一天之所以爲化也
精明之致雖未易測觀天之動而無動而聲臭
之俱寂者則可以觀其深矣此修德者必達諸
天而後有以凝純粹之精語德者必徵諸天而
後可以盡淵微之妙也彼所謂不大聲色德輶
如毛者則迹猶未融而未免於擬議之粗也惡
足以盡君子之不顯哉雖然君子之至此豈有
punctuated: 詩乎？詩云：「上天之載，無聲無臭。」夫物之可以形求者，皆顯也。微之而至於聲臭，則已入於無形；聲臭而猶曰無焉，則淵乎其淵者也。物之可以象求者，皆顯也。微之而至於聲臭，則已入於無象；聲臭而猶曰無焉，則深乎其深者也。詩之言天如此，以是言君子不顯篤恭之妙，斯其至乎！蓋君子之篤恭也，由人以合天，而一敬之存存者，潛會其不言之真；盡性以至命，而一敬之亹亹者，默契其於穆之運。存之爲中，而大本立焉，一天之所以爲神也。退藏之密，雖未易窺，觀天之靜而無靜，而聲臭之俱泯者，則可以通其故矣。發之爲和，而達道行焉，一天之所以爲化也。精明之致，雖未易測，觀天之動而無動，而聲臭之俱寂者，則可以觀其深矣。此修德者必達諸天，而後有以凝純粹之精；語德者必徵諸天，而後可以盡淵微之妙也。彼所謂不大聲色、德輶如毛者，則迹猶未融，而未免於擬議之粗也，惡足以盡君子之不顯哉！雖然，君子之至此，豈有
translation_en:
…the poem concerning King Wen? The Book of Odes says: “The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” Now, anything that can be sought through physical form is manifest. When one proceeds into subtlety as far as sound and smell, one has already entered the realm of the formless. Yet to say that even sound and smell are absent is to reach the profoundest depths. Anything that can be sought through an image is manifest. When one proceeds into subtlety as far as sound and smell, one has already entered the realm of the imageless. Yet to say that even sound and smell are absent is to reach the deepest depths. Such is the poem’s description of Heaven. If we use this to describe the subtlety of the gentleman’s unmanifest virtue and profound reverence, surely this is the ultimate expression!

For in his profound reverence, the gentleman proceeds from the human to accord with Heaven; through his constant preservation of undivided reverence, he inwardly apprehends the reality of Heaven’s wordlessness. He fully realizes his nature and thereby reaches Heaven’s mandate; through his unremitting practice of undivided reverence, he silently accords with Heaven’s profound and solemn workings. Preserved within, this becomes equilibrium, and the great foundation is established: it is one with that whereby Heaven is numinous. Though the secrecy of what lies withdrawn and hidden is not easily glimpsed, by contemplating Heaven’s stillness that is no stillness, in which sound and smell alike disappear, one can comprehend its underlying principle. Expressed outwardly, this becomes harmony, and the universally applicable Way proceeds: it is one with that whereby Heaven transforms. Though the utmost refinement of its lucid intelligence is not easily fathomed, by contemplating Heaven’s movement that is no movement, in which sound and smell alike are silent, one can perceive its depths.

Thus those who cultivate virtue must reach through to Heaven before they can consolidate the essence of utter purity; those who speak of virtue must seek verification in Heaven before they can fully express its profound and subtle marvel. As for such sayings as “not making a great display in voice and countenance” and “virtue is light as a hair,” traces still remain undissolved, and these expressions cannot escape the coarseness of comparison and deliberation. How could they adequately express the gentleman’s unmanifest virtue? Nevertheless, when the gentleman reaches this state, could there be anything…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
出於尚絅之初心哉蓋始之戒懼愼獨此心也
終之不顯篤恭亦此心也自始學至成德雖所
造不同其心之不求人知而惟無愧於天則一
而已矣昔楊子雲謂仲尼潛心文王顔子潛心
仲尼聖賢之道未有不潛而能至者也然則學
道者其必自尚絅之心始乎
爲人臣者懷仁義以事其君
王道立

人臣思以道而事君其有所感矣夫仁義之道
根於心也人臣懷此以事君詎非有所感而然
哉孟子黜宋牼言利而詔以崇王也蓋曰道莫
嚴於公私幾莫神於感應是故愼所以感之者
punctuated:
出於尚絅之初心哉？蓋始之戒懼愼獨，此心也；終之不顯篤恭，亦此心也。自始學至成德，雖所造不同，其心之不求人知而惟無愧於天，則一而已矣。昔楊子雲謂仲尼潛心文王，顔子潛心仲尼，聖賢之道未有不潛而能至者也。然則學道者，其必自尚絅之心始乎！
