人臣思以道而事君，其有所感矣。夫仁義之道，根於心也。人臣懷此以事君，詎非有所感而然哉？孟子黜宋牼言利，而詔以崇王也。蓋曰：道莫嚴於公私，幾莫神於感應。是故愼所以感之者，
translation_en:
…go beyond the original intention of wearing a plain outer garment over embroidered robes? For the vigilance, apprehension, and watchfulness over oneself when alone at the outset arise from this heart; the unostentatious virtue and profound reverence attained at the end also arise from this heart. From beginning study to perfecting virtue, although the levels attained differ, the heart remains one in seeking no recognition from others and wishing only to stand without shame before Heaven. Formerly, Yang Ziyun said that Zhongni immersed his heart in King Wen, and Master Yan immersed his heart in Zhongni. No one has ever attained the Way of the sages and worthies without such immersion. Must not those who study the Way, then, begin with the disposition expressed by wearing a plain outer garment over embroidered robes?
“Those who serve as ministers cherish benevolence and righteousness in serving their rulers.”
Wang Daoli
Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor, comments: 〔Reading your composition, I judge that you too have long cherished benevolence and righteousness.〕
Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor, comments: 〔Within its classical propriety lies inexhaustible meaning. These are surely words from the heart.〕
Examiner Chen, Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting, comments: 〔Lucid and elegant.〕
Examiner Qu, Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting, comments: 〔Loyalty and love overflow; worthy of recitation.〕
When a minister resolves to serve his ruler according to the Way, something has moved him to do so. The Way of benevolence and righteousness is rooted in the heart. When a minister cherishes these in serving his ruler, must this not be because something has moved him? Mencius rejected Song Keng’s talk of profit and instructed him to exalt the kingly Way. His meaning was this: in the Way, no distinction is more stringent than that between public and private interests; among subtle incipient workings, none is more wondrous than stimulus and response. Therefore one must be careful about that by which one moves others…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
牼以仁義遊將見爲人臣者向固知有利而不
知有仁義也兹則興起之有自而幸致君之有
術恍在於仁而仁主於愛愛莫切於愛君則攄
忠悃而引君以志仁固其愛之不容已者恍在
於義而義主於敬敬莫先於敬君則秉虔恭而
輔君以行義乃其敬之不可過者贊襄啓沃率
由中之忱悃凡可用吾之愛者無不爲也祗承
左右咸根心之寅畏凡可行吾之敬者無弗至
也所居雖不同而惓惓於是以罄夙懷之誠者
===
不因位而有異所處雖不一而皇皇於此以達
中心之願者殆易地而皆然居仁由義蓋嘗責
諸巳矣而移此𢿱成乎君德惟下不負所學巳
耳豈敢儌榮以貶其守乎戴仁抱義蓋嘗修之
家矣而由此對揚於王庭惟上不負吾君巳耳
豈徒干祿以枉其道乎斯則盡其在我而非由
於外假求之在君而非强其不能人臣無弗愛
且敬矣不然爲容恍爲象恭皆徇利以事君耳
而尚足以言臣哉吁牼也亦有仁義而巳矣何
punctuated: 牼以仁義遊，將見爲人臣者，向固知有利而不知有仁義也，兹則興起之有自，而幸致君之有術。恍在於仁，而仁主於愛，愛莫切於愛君，則攄忠悃而引君以志仁，固其愛之不容已者。恍在於義，而義主於敬，敬莫先於敬君，則秉虔恭而輔君以行義，乃其敬之不可過者。贊襄啓沃，率由中之忱悃，凡可用吾之愛者，無不爲也；祗承左右，咸根心之寅畏，凡可行吾之敬者，無弗至也。所居雖不同，而惓惓於是以罄夙懷之誠者，不因位而有異；所處雖不一，而皇皇於此以達中心之願者，殆易地而皆然。居仁由義，蓋嘗責諸巳矣，而移此𢿱成乎君德，惟下不負所學巳耳，豈敢儌榮以貶其守乎？戴仁抱義，蓋嘗修之家矣，而由此對揚於王庭，惟上不負吾君巳耳，豈徒干祿以枉其道乎？斯則盡其在我，而非由於外假；求之在君，而非强其不能。人臣無弗愛且敬矣。不然，爲容恍，爲象恭，皆徇利以事君耳，而尚足以言臣哉？吁！牼也，亦有仁義而巳矣，何
translation_en:
…Keng, if you travel about advocating benevolence and righteousness, you will see that ministers who formerly knew only profit and knew nothing of benevolence and righteousness now have a source of inspiration and rejoice that they have a means of guiding their ruler. Intent upon benevolence [?], they recognize that benevolence centers on love, and that no love is more urgent than love for the ruler. Thus they express their heartfelt loyalty and guide the ruler to set his purpose upon benevolence: their love simply cannot cease. Intent upon righteousness [?], they recognize that righteousness centers on reverence, and that no reverence takes precedence over reverence for the ruler. Thus they maintain devout respect and assist the ruler in practicing righteousness: in this, their reverence cannot be excessive. In assisting and enlightening him, they act entirely from heartfelt sincerity; whatever can give effect to their love, they do. In respectfully attending him at his side, their actions all spring from the heart’s reverent awe; whatever can express their reverence, they carry to the utmost. Though their offices differ, their devoted efforts to exhaust the sincerity they have long cherished do not vary with their rank. Though their circumstances differ, their anxious efforts to fulfill their hearts’ wishes would surely remain the same if they exchanged places.

They have already demanded of themselves that they dwell in benevolence and follow righteousness; extending this to bring the ruler’s virtue to fulfillment [?], they seek only, in their subordinate position, not to betray what they have learned. How would they dare seek glory at the expense of their integrity? They have already cultivated the honoring of benevolence and the embracing of righteousness within their households; through these they respond to and proclaim the sovereign’s beneficence at court, seeking only not to fail their ruler above. How could they merely seek official emoluments and bend their Way? Thus they fully realize what lies within themselves, rather than borrow it from outside; they seek its realization in their ruler, rather than force him to do what he cannot. No minister would fail to love and revere him. Otherwise, putting on an outward appearance [?] and a semblance of respect would merely be serving the ruler in pursuit of profit. Could such people still deserve to be called ministers? Ah, Keng! There are only benevolence and righteousness. Why …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
必曰利奈其時胥溺於功利而性道不明於天
下孟子不得不因宋牼以悟之也然傑士豈必
待感而後興哉固有心乎爲君而强於仁義者
矣雖然聖學無所爲而爲有所爲而爲即仁義
亦利也義利之辨其嚴乎知此庶可語純臣已
易
觀乎人文以化成天下　　　　　俵見家
同考試官教諭吳　批〔剖析詳盡而詞藻蔚〕
===
同考試官教諭周　批〔莊重不浮時義中亦〕
然可以爲文矣
得文明以止之意
考試官侍讀陳　批〔簡勁〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔典雅〕
君子有見於人道之真而因以善天下之治焉
蓋文明以止人道之真也觀於此而化成天下
何有哉彖傳言此以盡其蘊也意謂賁之爲道
貴其義固具諸易卦而可稽推其用實達諸天
punctuated:
必曰利？奈其時胥溺於功利，而性道不明於天下，孟子不得不因宋牼以悟之也。然傑士豈必待感而後興哉？固有心乎爲君而强於仁義者矣。雖然，聖學無所爲而爲，有所爲而爲，即仁義亦利也。義利之辨，其嚴乎！知此，庶可語純臣已。
易
觀乎人文，以化成天下。俵見家
同考試官教諭吳，批〔剖析詳盡，而詞藻蔚〕
同考試官教諭周，批〔莊重不浮，時義中亦〕然可以爲文矣。得文明以止之意。
考試官侍讀陳，批〔簡勁〕
考試官侍讀瞿，批〔典雅〕
君子有見於人道之真，而因以善天下之治焉。蓋文明以止，人道之真也。觀於此而化成天下，何有哉？彖傳言此以盡其蘊也。意謂賁之爲道，貴其義，固具諸易卦而可稽；推其用，實達諸天
translation_en:
…why must you speak of profit? Yet in those days everyone was immersed in achievement and profit, and human nature and the Way were not understood throughout the world. Mencius therefore had to use Song Keng to awaken them. But must outstanding men wait to be stirred before rising to action? There certainly are men intent upon serving their ruler who exert themselves in benevolence and righteousness. Nevertheless, the learning of the sages consists in acting without an ulterior purpose. If one acts with an ulterior purpose, even benevolence and righteousness become profit-seeking. How strict is the distinction between righteousness and profit! Those who understand this may perhaps be addressed concerning what it means to be a minister of unsullied integrity.

Book of Changes
“Observe human culture, and thereby transform and perfect all under Heaven.” — Biao Jianjia

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “The analysis is thorough and exhaustive, and the language richly adorned: this can indeed be called literary composition.” [?]
Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “Dignified and free of frivolity; within an exposition of the topic’s contemporary significance, it also captures the meaning of ‘illumination restrained by limits.’” [?]
[The endings of these two comments appear displaced in the transcription.]
Examiner Chen, Reader-in-waiting, comments: “Concise and forceful.”
Examiner Qu, Reader-in-waiting, comments: “Classical and elegant.”

The gentleman perceives the true essence of the human Way and thereby improves the governance of all under Heaven. For illumination restrained by limits is the true essence of the human Way. By observing this, what difficulty could there be in transforming and perfecting all under Heaven? The Commentary on the Judgments says this to bring out its full significance. Its meaning is that, as for the way of the hexagram Bi, Adornment, its significance is to be prized: it is fully embodied in the hexagrams of the Changes and can be examined there. Extend its application, and it truly reaches Heaven…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人而無間時變之察有得於天文矣而觀乎人
文則豈不足以化成天下哉彼道在天下其燦
然者謂之文其截然者謂之止一於文則情勝
而無實君子以爲濫矣一於止則志睽而不通
君子以爲隘矣惟是人文也先之以離明則盡
飾煥天下之文旣不蹈夫徑情直行之弊繼之
以艮止則至序秩天下之異又不失於越禮犯
分之愆雍睦加於體統之嚴和樂而不流固有
相濟以弘其化物采章於等威之辨成文而不
===
亂殆有交錯以臻其休以正百官濟濟如也而
文陳於朝廷之上焉以正萬民熙熙如也而文
見於邦國之間焉有禮以相接有分以相守文
命之誕敷四達而不悖矣合愛以統同立敬以
辨異人紀之聿修萬世以爲準矣夫以天下之
大而化成之效不外於人文焉吾觀於賁而知
王道之易易也抑物不可以苟合故受之以賁
尚文非聖人之得已也及其後也僭越生焉歌
雍詩舞八佾似於文明之盛可觀而名分之止
punctuated: 人而無間。時變之察，有得於天文矣，而觀乎人文，則豈不足以化成天下哉？彼道在天下，其燦然者謂之文，其截然者謂之止。一於文，則情勝而無實，君子以爲濫矣；一於止，則志睽而不通，君子以爲隘矣。惟是人文也，先之以離明，則盡飾煥天下之文，旣不蹈夫徑情直行之弊；繼之以艮止，則至序秩天下之異，又不失於越禮犯分之愆。雍睦加於體統之嚴，和樂而不流，固有相濟以弘其化；物采章於等威之辨，成文而不亂，殆有交錯以臻其休。以正百官，濟濟如也，而文陳於朝廷之上焉；以正萬民，熙熙如也，而文見於邦國之間焉。有禮以相接，有分以相守，文命之誕敷，四達而不悖矣；合愛以統同，立敬以辨異，人紀之聿修，萬世以爲準矣。夫以天下之大，而化成之效不外於人文焉。吾觀於賁，而知王道之易易也。抑物不可以苟合，故受之以賁，尚文非聖人之得已也。及其後也，僭越生焉，歌雍詩，舞八佾，似於文明之盛可觀，而名分之止
translation_en: …and humanity without any separation. By discerning changes in the seasons, one gains an understanding of the patterns of Heaven; could observing human patterns, then, be insufficient to transform and perfect all under Heaven? Of the Way as it exists throughout the world, its resplendent aspect is called refinement, and its clearly delimited aspect is called restraint. If one attends exclusively to refinement, feelings prevail without substance: the gentleman considers this excessive. If one attends exclusively to restraint, purposes diverge and fail to communicate: the gentleman considers this restrictive. Human patterns, however, begin with the illumination of Li: through full adornment, they make the world's refinement shine, avoiding the fault of acting directly upon unchecked feelings. They follow this with the restraint of Gen: through consummate ordering [?], they arrange the world's distinctions, avoiding the transgression of overstepping ritual and violating one's allotted station. Concord and affection supplement the strictness of the hierarchical order, producing harmony and joy without abandon; these surely complement one another to extend their transforming influence. The colors and decorations of ceremonial objects make distinctions of rank and dignity manifest, producing patterned refinement without disorder; their interweaving thus brings about excellence. Applied to rectifying the hundred officials, this produces dignified concord, and refinement is displayed at court. Applied to rectifying the myriad people, it produces joyful harmony, and refinement appears throughout the realm. There are rites by which people engage with one another and distinctions of station that they mutually uphold: the civilizing commands are widely promulgated, reaching in all directions without contradiction. Bringing affection together unites what is shared; establishing reverence distinguishes what differs. The ordering principles of human relations are thereby cultivated, becoming a standard for ten thousand generations. Vast though the world is, the efficacy of its transformation and perfection does not extend beyond human patterns. In contemplating Bi, the hexagram Adornment, I recognize how very easy the kingly Way is to practice. Yet things cannot be joined together carelessly; hence Adornment follows. The sages had no choice but to value refinement. Later, however, usurpation and transgression arose: people sang the Yong hymn and performed the dance in eight ranks. These seemed to offer a spectacle of flourishing cultural refinement, yet the restraint imposed by distinctions of status…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
步在乎故賁之後有剝亦勢之所趨耳其曰白
賁無咎則惇本尚素又聖人補偏救弊之善也
是故與其文也寧質
天地設位而易行乎其中矣成性存存道
義之門
張克家
同考試官教諭吳　批〔說理明盡而詞復典〕
雅非苟作者
同考試官教諭周　批〔發明詳盡殆深於性〕
學者佳士佳士
===
考試官侍讀陳　批〔精邃〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔得聖人作易之意〕
大傳即造化以明聖學之所至見聖人與造化
準也夫易理散於造化而統於吾性者也聖人
得之則其用不與造化準耶夫子之意蓋曰易
之作也聖人所以盡三才之道而崇德廣業之
所必資者也學易而智崇禮卑焉則其用豈微
也哉蓋自卑高陳而天地位易之行乎其中者
punctuated:
步在乎，故賁之後有剝，亦勢之所趨耳。其曰「白賁無咎」，則惇本尚素，又聖人補偏救弊之善也。是故與其文也寧質。
「天地設位，而易行乎其中矣；成性存存，道義之門。」
張克家
同考試官教諭吳，批〔說理明盡，而詞復典〕雅，非苟作者。
同考試官教諭周，批〔發明詳盡，殆深於性〕學者。佳士！佳士！
考試官侍讀陳，批〔精邃〕。
考試官侍讀瞿，批〔得聖人作易之意〕。
大傳即造化以明聖學之所至，見聖人與造化準也。夫易理散於造化，而統於吾性者也。聖人得之，則其用不與造化準耶？夫子之意蓋曰：易之作也，聖人所以盡三才之道，而崇德廣業之所必資者也。學易而智崇禮卑焉，則其用豈微也哉？蓋自卑高陳而天地位，易之行乎其中者
translation_en:
…[the bounds] remain therein [?]. Thus, that Stripping Away (Bo) follows Adornment (Bi) is simply the inevitable course of things. The statement, “White adornment: no blame,” commends strengthening the foundations and esteeming simplicity; this, too, shows the sage’s skill in correcting imbalances and remedying abuses. Hence, rather than ornament, prefer substance.
“Heaven and Earth take their appointed positions, and change operates between them. Preserving and continually sustaining one’s fully realized nature is the gateway to the Way and righteousness.”
Zhang Kejia
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of principle is clear and exhaustive, and the language is also classical and elegant. This is no careless writer.”
Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The exposition is detailed and exhaustive; he seems deeply versed in the learning of human nature. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!”
Examiner Chen, Reader-in-waiting, comments: “Refined and profound.”
Examiner Qu, Reader-in-waiting, comments: “He grasps the sage’s intention in composing the Changes.”
The Great Commentary draws upon the workings of creation to illuminate the ultimate attainment of sagely learning, showing that the sage accords with creation. The principles of change are dispersed throughout creation but united within our nature. When the sage grasps them, does his application of them not accord with creation? The Master’s meaning is, presumably, this: the composition of the Changes was the sage’s means of fully encompassing the Way of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and it is indispensable for exalting virtue and broadening achievement. If, through studying the Changes, one’s wisdom becomes lofty and one’s ritual conduct humble, how could its efficacy be slight? Ever since the low and the high were arrayed and Heaven and Earth took their positions, change has operated between them…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
久矣天以倡乎地而一陰一陽恒相推而不窮
不必求之蓍策而確然示人者皆此理之流行
也地以和乎天而一剛一柔恒相摩而不已不
必求之卦象而隤然示人者皆此理之散見也
易之在天地有如此者其在於人成性之所存
即道義之所出與天地之易相似者也人惟智
之未至而不知存斯無以爲致用之本今智崇
如天則思慮未起而凡可以存其未發之真者
涵泳之不已矣亦惟禮之未至而不能存斯無
===
以豫時出之原今禮卑如地則物感未交而凡
可以存其固有之良者敦篤之不忘矣由是率
之斯爲道而所以通天下之故者胥此出焉吉
凶消長各以貞勝而莫究其端蓋同歸而殊途
也由是行之斯爲義而所以制天下之宜者胥
此出焉出處語默各以時行而不可爲典蓋一
致而百慮也此則聖人之易與天地之易竝行
者也語其初則有得於易者深矣易非聖人之
所以崇德而廣業者哉雖然易非心外物也成
punctuated: 久矣！天以倡乎地，而一陰一陽恒相推而不窮，不必求之蓍策，而確然示人者，皆此理之流行也。地以和乎天，而一剛一柔恒相摩而不已，不必求之卦象，而隤然示人者，皆此理之散見也。易之在天地有如此者，其在於人，成性之所存，即道義之所出，與天地之易相似者也。人惟智之未至而不知存，斯無以爲致用之本。今智崇如天，則思慮未起，而凡可以存其未發之真者，涵泳之不已矣。亦惟禮之未至而不能存，斯無以豫時出之原。今禮卑如地，則物感未交，而凡可以存其固有之良者，敦篤之不忘矣。由是率之，斯爲道，而所以通天下之故者，胥此出焉。吉凶消長，各以貞勝，而莫究其端，蓋同歸而殊途也。由是行之，斯爲義，而所以制天下之宜者，胥此出焉。出處語默，各以時行，而不可爲典，蓋一致而百慮也。此則聖人之易與天地之易竝行者也。語其初，則有得於易者深矣。易非聖人之所以崇德而廣業者哉？雖然，易非心外物也。成
translation_en:
…has long been so! Heaven takes the lead over Earth, and yin and yang continually impel one another without exhaustion. There is no need to seek this in the milfoil stalks used in divination: all that Heaven firmly displays to humankind is the flowing operation of this principle. Earth responds harmoniously to Heaven, and the firm and yielding continually interact without cease. There is no need to seek this in the images of the hexagrams: all that Earth compliantly displays to humankind is this principle manifesting itself in diverse forms. Such is the Changes as it exists in Heaven and Earth. Within human beings, the abiding place of the perfected nature is precisely the source of the Way and righteousness; it corresponds to the Changes of Heaven and Earth.

It is only because people's wisdom has not reached its utmost that they do not know how to preserve this nature, and thus lack a foundation for putting it into practice. Now, when wisdom is lofty like Heaven, before thoughts and deliberations arise, they ceaselessly immerse themselves in everything that can preserve the authenticity of their nature before it is aroused. Likewise, it is only because their ritual propriety has not reached its utmost that they cannot preserve this nature, and thus cannot prepare the source from which it emerges at the appropriate time. Now, when ritual propriety is lowly like Earth, before contact with external things stirs them, they steadfastly cultivate, without neglect, everything that can preserve their inherent goodness.

Following this nature constitutes the Way, and everything by which one comprehends the affairs of the world issues from it. Good fortune and ill fortune, decline and growth, each prevail through constancy, yet none can fathom their beginnings: they reach the same destination by different paths. Acting upon this nature constitutes righteousness, and everything by which one determines what is fitting in the world issues from it. Taking office or withdrawing, speaking or remaining silent—each proceeds according to its proper time and cannot be made into a fixed rule: a hundred deliberations converge upon a single end. Thus the Changes of the sage operates alongside the Changes of Heaven and Earth. To speak of its origin, the sage's understanding of the Changes is indeed profound. Is the Changes not that by which the sage exalts his virtue and extends his undertakings? Nevertheless, the Changes is not something external to the mind. The perfected …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
性者即易之太極吾人受之天地以爲心者也
天地得之而變化行聖人得之而道義出所謂
三極之道天地人之心也聖人之學易亦惟以
易之理証吾心耳否則洗心退藏神明其德何
爲者哉學易者試思之
書
德惟善政政在養民
張明正
同考試官教諭魏　批〔此作以德爲善政養民之本蓋知本者錄之〕
同考試官教諭邵　批〔講善政養民處甚充蔚可以觀素養矣〕
===
考試官侍讀陳　批〔精粹〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔整贍〕
大臣言人君推德於政而當務其大者焉蓋治
道莫大於養民也以德行政者盡亦是務乎禹
欲帝念益之言而告之及此意謂天之立君以
爲民也而所以養民者存乎政所以立政者存
punctuated:
性者，即易之太極，吾人受之天地以爲心者也。天地得之而變化行，聖人得之而道義出，所謂三極之道，天地人之心也。聖人之學易，亦惟以易之理証吾心耳。否則洗心退藏，神明其德，何爲者哉？學易者試思之。
書
德惟善政，政在養民。
張明正
同考試官教諭魏批〔此作以德爲善政養民之本，蓋知本者，錄之。〕
同考試官教諭邵批〔講善政養民處甚充蔚，可以觀素養矣。〕
考試官侍讀陳批〔精粹。〕
考試官侍讀瞿批〔整贍。〕
大臣言人君推德於政，而當務其大者焉。蓋治道莫大於養民也，以德行政者盡亦是務乎！禹欲帝念益之言，而告之及此，意謂天之立君以爲民也，而所以養民者存乎政，所以立政者存
translation_en:
…the perfected nature is precisely the Supreme Ultimate of the Changes, which we receive from Heaven and Earth as our heart-mind. Heaven and Earth obtain it, and transformation proceeds; the sage obtains it, and the Way and righteousness emerge. What is called the Way of the Three Ultimates is the heart-mind of Heaven, Earth, and humanity. In studying the Changes, the sage merely uses its principles to verify his own heart-mind. Otherwise, what purpose would be served by cleansing the heart-mind, withdrawing into concealment, and making one’s virtue spiritually luminous? Let those who study the Changes ponder this.

Book of Documents

“Virtue consists in good government; government lies in nourishing the people.”

Zhang Mingzheng

Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor, comments: 〔This composition takes virtue as the foundation of good government and nourishing the people. The author evidently understands the foundation; I select it.〕

Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of good government and nourishing the people is exceptionally full and rich, revealing the author’s accumulated cultivation.〕

Examiner Chen, Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔Refined and pure.〕

Examiner Qu, Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔Well ordered and ample.〕

The great minister states that when a ruler extends his virtue into government, he should attend to what is most important. For nothing in the way of governing is greater than nourishing the people. Should not all who apply virtue in government devote themselves to this? Yu wished the emperor to heed Yi’s words, and so his admonition reached this point. His meaning was that Heaven establishes rulers for the sake of the people; the means of nourishing the people lies in government, and the means of establishing government lies…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
乎德故君天下者不徒有其德而已惟當有以
善其政焉蓋德者其立本也政者其致用也有
其德無其政則經綸之迹無所見而其德亦徒
善耳是必以精神心術之藴而施爲裁成輔相
之方議諸朝廷而紀法於是昭焉頒諸邦國而
制度於是立焉擴仁心于仁政開物成務者一
公平正大之體也溢美意于良法因時作則者
皆明通公溥之用也是所貴乎德者惟其有善
政而已矣不然則亦何取於德哉又不徒善其
===
政而已惟在有以養其民焉蓋德政者其大體
也養民者其實用也行其政弗養其民則致理
之術有所乖而其政亦徒法耳是必因天地自
然之利而布爲生養安全之澤鼓舞盡神而容
保無疆焉通變盡利而厚下安宅焉致事用而
品式備非以示法也法立而利亦興與民共之
者也本德行而區畫詳非以盡制也制定而惠
斯溥與民安之者也是所貴乎政者在乎能養
民而已矣不然則亦何取於政哉夫養道得而
punctuated: 乎德。故君天下者，不徒有其德而已，惟當有以善其政焉。蓋德者，其立本也；政者，其致用也。有其德，無其政，則經綸之迹無所見，而其德亦徒善耳。是必以精神心術之藴，而施爲裁成輔相之方：議諸朝廷，而紀法於是昭焉；頒諸邦國，而制度於是立焉。擴仁心于仁政，開物成務者，一公平正大之體也；溢美意于良法，因時作則者，皆明通公溥之用也。是所貴乎德者，惟其有善政而已矣。不然，則亦何取於德哉？又不徒善其政而已，惟在有以養其民焉。蓋德政者，其大體也；養民者，其實用也。行其政，弗養其民，則致理之術有所乖，而其政亦徒法耳。是必因天地自然之利，而布爲生養安全之澤：鼓舞盡神，而容保無疆焉；通變盡利，而厚下安宅焉。致事用而品式備，非以示法也，法立而利亦興，與民共之者也；本德行而區畫詳，非以盡制也，制定而惠斯溥，與民安之者也。是所貴乎政者，在乎能養民而已矣。不然，則亦何取於政哉？夫養道得而
translation_en:
…upon virtue. Thus, one who rules all under Heaven must not merely possess virtue; he must put it to work in making his government good. Virtue establishes the foundation; government puts it into practice. If he possesses virtue but does not express it in government, no achievements of ordering the realm will be evident, and his virtue will amount only to goodness without practical effect. He must therefore draw upon the resources of his spirit and mind to devise ways of ordering and assisting the processes of Heaven and Earth. When these are deliberated at court, rules and laws become clear; when they are promulgated throughout the realm, institutions are established. Extending a benevolent heart into benevolent government, opening up the potential of things and bringing affairs to completion—all embody a single impartial, fair, upright, and magnanimous substance. Pouring good intentions into sound laws and establishing standards suited to the times—all put into practice an enlightened, adaptable, impartial, and far-reaching capacity. What makes virtue valuable is simply that it produces good government. Otherwise, what use would virtue be?

Nor is it enough merely to make government good: it must provide for the people. Virtue and government constitute the general framework; nourishing the people is their practical application. If one carries out government without nourishing the people, the methods for achieving good order go astray, and government amounts only to laws without practical effect. One must therefore draw upon the benefits naturally afforded by Heaven and Earth and distribute them as blessings that sustain life and ensure security. By inspiring the people and fully exercising this wondrous efficacy, one embraces and protects them without limit; by adapting to changing circumstances and fully realizing their benefits, one enriches those below and makes their dwelling secure. Attending to practical affairs and providing a complete array of standards and forms is not merely a display of laws: once laws are established, benefits also arise, to be shared with the people. Taking virtuous conduct as the foundation and making detailed arrangements is not merely a matter of elaborating every regulation: once institutions are settled, beneficence spreads widely, enabling the people to enjoy security through them. What makes government valuable is simply its ability to nourish the people. Otherwise, what use would government be? Now, only when the proper way of nourishing the people has been attained…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
後可以語政善政行而後可以語德要之德者
立政之原而養民者行政之實君人者當知所
務矣抑禹因伯益陳儆戒無虞而中重於養民
寔制治保邦之要道也蓋民者邦之本不養則
民散而邦本不固其何以爲國故禹獨以養民
爲言而下文復詳六府三事惓惓爲邦本慮也
夫亦廣益之旨欲帝深念而保之於無窮乎噫
虞帝弗可及也已
天子作民父母以爲天下王
金世卭
===
同考試官教諭魏 批 〔讀子之文蓋亦今之有感於斯言者〕
同考試官教諭邵 批 〔講尊親意甚切書義若此亦難得矣〕
考試官侍讀陳 批 〔得頌君體〕
考試官侍讀瞿 批 〔規切有味〕
庶民頌君而親且尊焉斯言之感也甚矣王化
感人之妙也民於建極之君而以尊親頌之豈
punctuated:
後可以語政，善政行而後可以語德。要之，德者立政之原，而養民者行政之實，君人者當知所務矣。抑禹因伯益陳儆戒無虞，而中重於養民，寔制治保邦之要道也。蓋民者邦之本，不養則民散，而邦本不固，其何以爲國？故禹獨以養民爲言，而下文復詳六府三事，惓惓爲邦本慮也。夫亦廣益之旨，欲帝深念而保之於無窮乎？噫！虞帝弗可及也已。
天子作民父母，以爲天下王。
金世卭
同考試官教諭魏批〔讀子之文，蓋亦今之有感於斯言者。〕
同考試官教諭邵批〔講尊親意甚切，書義若此，亦難得矣。〕
考試官侍讀陳批〔得頌君體。〕
考試官侍讀瞿批〔規切有味。〕
庶民頌君而親且尊焉，斯言之感也甚矣！王化感人之妙也！民於建極之君而以尊親頌之，豈
translation_en:
…only then can one speak of government; only after good government is put into practice can one speak of virtue. In sum, virtue is the source of establishing government, while nourishing the people is the substance of administering it. A ruler of men should know where to direct his efforts. Moreover, when Yu responded to Boyi’s admonition to remain vigilant even when there was no cause for anxiety, he placed particular emphasis [?] on nourishing the people. This is indeed the essential way to establish order and preserve the state. The people are the foundation of the state: if they are not nourished, they disperse, and the state’s foundation becomes insecure. How, then, can a state be maintained? Thus Yu spoke specifically of nourishing the people, and the following passage further elaborates the Six Treasuries and Three Affairs, showing his earnest concern for the foundation of the state. Was he also expanding upon Yi’s meaning, wishing the emperor to ponder it deeply and preserve the state forever? Ah! The emperor of Yu cannot be equaled!
“The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother to the people, thereby becoming king of all under Heaven.”
Jin Shiqiong 金世卭
Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor: 〔Reading your essay, I see that you too are among those today who are moved by these words.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor: 〔The exposition of reverence and affection is most apt. An interpretation of the Book of Documents like this is indeed hard to come by.〕
Comment by Examiner Chen, Reader-in-Waiting: 〔It captures the proper form for praising the ruler.〕
Comment by Examiner Qu, Reader-in-Waiting: 〔The admonition is pointed and rich in meaning.〕
The common people praise their ruler, cherishing and revering him. How deeply moving these words are! Such is the wondrous power of kingly transformation to move people! When the people praise the ruler who establishes the supreme standard with reverence and affection, could it be that …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
非深得其心者哉昔箕子衍皇極之疇至此蓋
曰皇極之理君訓之而民同有之者也民於敷
言旣訓行以近光矣而所以頌之者何如哉但
見涵泳於服習之久而天機爲之發揚踊躍於
觀感之深而頌聲以之洋溢莫不曰明明天子
其作民父母乎蓋父母之於子善有教不善有
沮惟子之克肖焉耳天子敷言之訓使我協於
極而不罹於咎則是教之以義方通天下爲一
家愛之而知勞視萬民爲一體提撕而警覺焉
===
非徒以正率也念切而保之至也感發而興起
焉非徒以言教也心誠而求之篤也是殆父母
之而不忍納於邪矣吾何幸而爲之子哉又莫
不曰明明天子其爲天下王乎蓋王者之於民
善則勸不善則懲惟民之斂德焉耳天子敷言
之訓使民戒以私而會歸於極則是約人心以
至當不易之理而寵綏已及於四方示天下以
大中至正之矩而具瞻無愧於元后修道以設
教舉一世而甄陶之大君之臨允宜也繼天以
punctuated: 非深得其心者哉？昔箕子衍皇極之疇，至此蓋曰：皇極之理，君訓之而民同有之者也。民於敷言旣訓，行以近光矣，而所以頌之者何如哉？但見涵泳於服習之久，而天機爲之發揚；踊躍於觀感之深，而頌聲以之洋溢。莫不曰：「明明天子，其作民父母乎！」蓋父母之於子，善有教，不善有沮，惟子之克肖焉耳。天子敷言之訓，使我協於極而不罹於咎，則是教之以義方，通天下爲一家；愛之而知勞，視萬民爲一體。提撕而警覺焉，非徒以正率也，念切而保之至也；感發而興起焉，非徒以言教也，心誠而求之篤也。是殆父母之而不忍納於邪矣，吾何幸而爲之子哉！又莫不曰：「明明天子，其爲天下王乎！」蓋王者之於民，善則勸，不善則懲，惟民之斂德焉耳。天子敷言之訓，使民戒以私而會歸於極，則是約人心以至當不易之理，而寵綏已及於四方；示天下以大中至正之矩，而具瞻無愧於元后。修道以設教，舉一世而甄陶之，大君之臨允宜也；繼天以
translation_en:
…does this not show that he has profoundly won their hearts? Long ago, when Jizi elaborated the section on the August Ultimate, at this point he was, in effect, saying: the principle of the August Ultimate is something the ruler teaches and the people all possess. Having followed his widely proclaimed teachings, the people conduct themselves so as to draw near his radiance. How, then, do they praise him? Immersed in long practice and habituation, their innate moral impulses unfold; stirred to exultation by the depth of what they witness and feel, they overflow with songs of praise. All say: “May the illustrious Son of Heaven act as father and mother to the people!” Parents teach their children what is good and restrain what is bad, wishing only that their children may truly resemble them. Through his widely proclaimed teachings, the Son of Heaven enables us to accord with the Ultimate and avoid wrongdoing. Thus he teaches us the ways of righteousness, treating all under Heaven as one family; loving us and knowing that he must set us to work, he regards the myriad people as one body. He instructs and awakens us: this is more than leading through rectitude; his concern is earnest and his protection complete. He moves and rouses us: this is more than teaching through words; his heart is sincere and his solicitude profound. Surely he acts as our father and mother, unable to bear allowing us to fall into evil. How fortunate we are to be his children!

All likewise say: “May the illustrious Son of Heaven be king of all under Heaven!” A king encourages what is good in his people and punishes what is bad, wishing only that they may gather virtue within themselves. Through his widely proclaimed teachings, the Son of Heaven warns the people against selfishness [?] and brings them together in returning to the Ultimate. Thus he disciplines human hearts by principles supremely fitting and unchanging, and his favor and pacification already extend to the four quarters. He shows all under Heaven the standard of perfect centrality and utmost rectitude; as the one to whom all look, he is worthy of being their sovereign. Cultivating the Way to establish instruction, he molds an entire age: most fitting indeed is the great ruler’s governance. Continuing Heaven’s work in order to…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
立極盡斯民而範圍之帝位之履不疚也是蓋
司牧之而勿使失其性矣吾何幸而爲之民哉
夫曰父母則親之至矣曰天下王則尊之至矣
親之而愛以情通尊之而敬由心立敷言感人
之妙一至是夫抑王者之感人豈徒於言語之
末哉皇極之建敷錫庶民則化導之本固自有
在而敷言之訓特特此以爲感動之機而已若
曰聖人之感人也以言庶民之頌德也亦以言
則無本之教不足以率人而豈王者忘言之治
至神之化哉噫此固箕子衍疇意也
===
詩
九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍稷重穋禾麻
菽麥嗟我農夫我稼既同上入執宮功
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋其始播
百穀
劉廷對
同考試官教諭潘 批〔通篇力去陳言而意〕
〔婉詞切蓋深於詩者〕
punctuated:
立極，盡斯民而範圍之，帝位之履不疚也。是蓋司牧之而勿使失其性矣，吾何幸而爲之民哉！夫曰父母，則親之至矣；曰天下王，則尊之至矣。親之而愛以情通，尊之而敬由心立，敷言感人之妙一至是夫！抑王者之感人，豈徒於言語之末哉？皇極之建，敷錫庶民，則化導之本固自有在，而敷言之訓特特此以爲感動之機而已。若曰聖人之感人也以言，庶民之頌德也亦以言，則無本之教不足以率人，而豈王者忘言之治、至神之化哉？噫！此固箕子衍疇意也。

詩

九月築場圃，十月納禾稼，黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。嗟我農夫！我稼既同，上入執宮功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。

劉廷對

同考試官教諭潘，批〔通篇力去陳言而意〕〔婉詞切蓋深於詩者〕
translation_en:
…establishing the ultimate standard and bringing all these people within its compass, he occupies the imperial throne without fault. Thus he shepherds them and does not allow them to lose their inherent nature. How fortunate we are to be his people!

To call him “father and mother” expresses the utmost closeness; to call him “king of all under Heaven” expresses the utmost reverence. Through closeness, love communicates through feeling; through reverence, respect takes root in the heart. Such is the marvelous power of his proclaimed words to move people! Yet does a king move people merely through the superficial means of speech? When the August Standard is established and its blessings are bestowed broadly upon the common people, the foundation of transformative guidance assuredly already exists. Instruction through proclaimed words merely uses this as the occasion for moving them—the wording here is doubtful [?]. If one were to say that the sage moves people through words, and that the common people likewise praise his virtue through words, then teaching without a foundation would be insufficient to lead people. How could this be the king’s governance that transcends words, his supremely wondrous transformation? Ah! This indeed was Jizi’s meaning in expounding the categories of the Great Plan.

Book of Poetry

“In the ninth month we prepare the threshing ground in the garden;
in the tenth month we bring in the crops:
millet and panicled millet, late- and early-ripening grain,
grain and hemp, beans and wheat.
Ah, we farmers!
Our crops have all been gathered;
we go up to undertake work on the lord’s buildings.
By day you gather thatch;
by night you twist ropes.
Hasten to climb onto the roofs and repair them,
for soon you must begin sowing the hundred grains.”

Liu Tingdui

Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: “Throughout the piece he strives to avoid hackneyed expressions; his meaning is delicately conveyed and his language apt. He is surely one who understands the Book of Poetry deeply.”

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陳　批〔寓精彩於沖淡文之〕
佳者錄之
考試官侍讀陳　批〔傳永〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔得旨〕
觀豳人于農事之終始可以知憂勤之心矣夫
民事不可緩也豳人於其終而即慮其始焉是
何其念之深也哉周公作此以諷成王蓋曰國
之所恃以立者民民之所賴以生者食王知豳
人之于農乎時乎九月而場圃築焉蓋自禾之
===
未納而先爲之所矣時乎十月而禾稼納焉蓋
自場之旣築而早爲之登矣有黍稷有重穋而
無一之不入昔之于耜舉趾而親其勞者于今
得以享其成也有禾麻有菽麥而無一之不備
昔之同我婦子而勞于事者于今得以食其實
也夫以三時之勤而享百穀之入雖少休焉亦
不爲過維我豳人則相戒以爲我稼之同固吾
人之慶而邑居之治亦吾人之事也今可以入
都邑而執宮功矣葺所需也爾其晝往取焉綯
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陳，批〔寓精彩於沖淡，文之〕佳者，錄之。
考試官侍讀陳，批〔傳永〕。
考試官侍讀瞿，批〔得旨〕。
觀豳人于農事之終始，可以知憂勤之心矣。夫民事不可緩也，豳人於其終而即慮其始焉，是何其念之深也哉！周公作此以諷成王，蓋曰：國之所恃以立者民，民之所賴以生者食。王知豳人之于農乎？時乎九月而場圃築焉，蓋自禾之未納而先爲之所矣。時乎十月而禾稼納焉，蓋自場之旣築而早爲之登矣。有黍稷，有重穋，而無一之不入。昔之于耜舉趾而親其勞者，于今得以享其成也。有禾麻，有菽麥，而無一之不備。昔之同我婦子而勞于事者，于今得以食其實也。夫以三時之勤而享百穀之入，雖少休焉，亦不爲過。維我豳人則相戒以爲：我稼之同，固吾人之慶，而邑居之治，亦吾人之事也。今可以入都邑而執宮功矣。葺所需也，爾其晝往取焉；綯
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Excellence resides within its quiet simplicity. This is a fine composition; include it.”
Examiner Chen, Reader-in-waiting, comments: “To be transmitted enduringly [?].”
Examiner Qu, Reader-in-waiting, comments: “Grasps the essential meaning.”
By observing the people of Bin at the ending and beginning of their agricultural work, one can understand their anxious diligence. The people’s work cannot be delayed. At its conclusion, the people of Bin immediately considered its next beginning. How deeply they thought about it! The Duke of Zhou composed this poem to admonish King Cheng, saying, in effect: What sustains a state is its people; what sustains the people’s lives is food. Does Your Majesty understand how the people of Bin attend to farming? In the ninth month they prepare the threshing grounds in their garden plots: even before the grain is brought in, they have already made a place for it. In the tenth month they bring in the crops: once the threshing grounds are prepared, they promptly gather the harvest. There are millets, both glutinous and non-glutinous, and late- and early-ripening grain; none goes ungathered. Those who formerly readied their ploughs and set their feet to work, personally undertaking the toil, can now enjoy its accomplishment. There are grain and hemp, beans and wheat; nothing is lacking. Those who formerly labored at the work together with their wives and children can now eat its fruits.
Having toiled through three seasons and received the harvest of all the grains, they would not be at fault even if they rested a little. Yet our people of Bin admonish one another, saying: “The gathering of our crops is indeed cause for celebration, but putting our dwellings in order is also our responsibility. Now we may enter the town and undertake work on our houses. Thatching material is needed; go and fetch it by day. As for rope …”

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
所當也爾其夜絞治焉夜以繼日各勤其事而
亟爲乘屋之圖者非徒棘其欲也蓋居可懷也
而時不可失也食所重也而備不可忘也屋今
不治而東作屆期將復始事于百穀之播而于
此不暇矣吾人于農每慮夫日之不給也敢以
歲稅而自逸哉夫不以田功之成而忘嗣歲之
計不待田畯之督而懷先事之圖此可以知稼
穡之艱難與小人之依矣此成王之所當念也
雖然以周公之忠豈他無可以告君而惓惓獨
===
以農事爲言者何也王業之本固在此也夫創
業之初民情之得達于君也難其居使之然也使成王能知
民事之艱而以先公之心爲心則民之不獲自
盡者鮮矣其後成王爲守成令王至今誦德不
衰焉則成王之賢與周公輔導之力不皆可見
也哉
虎拜稽首天子萬年
水思中
punctuated:
所當也，爾其夜絞治焉。夜以繼日，各勤其事，而亟爲乘屋之圖者，非徒棘其欲也。蓋居可懷也，而時不可失也；食所重也，而備不可忘也。屋今不治，而東作屆期，將復始事于百穀之播，而于此不暇矣。吾人于農，每慮夫日之不給也，敢以歲稅而自逸哉？夫不以田功之成而忘嗣歲之計，不待田畯之督而懷先事之圖，此可以知稼穡之艱難與小人之依矣。此成王之所當念也。雖然，以周公之忠，豈他無可以告君，而惓惓獨以農事爲言者，何也？王業之本固在此也。夫創業之初，民情之得達于君也難，其居使之然也。使成王能知民事之艱，而以先公之心爲心，則民之不獲自盡者鮮矣。其後成王爲守成令王，至今誦德不衰焉，則成王之賢與周公輔導之力，不皆可見也哉？

虎拜稽首，天子萬年。

水思中
translation_en:
…is what is called for; you should twist and prepare it at night. Continuing by night the work of the day, each diligently attends to his tasks and hastens to make plans for repairing the roofs. This is not merely eagerness to satisfy their wishes. A dwelling is something to cherish, but the proper season must not be missed; food is essential, but preparations must not be forgotten. If the houses are not repaired now, when the season for spring cultivation arrives they will again begin sowing the various grains and have no leisure for this work. In farming, we constantly fear that the days will not suffice. Dare we take our ease once the year's taxes are paid [?]?

They do not forget their plans for the coming year merely because the work in the fields is complete; nor do they wait for the agricultural overseer's supervision before thinking ahead. From this one can understand the hardships of sowing and reaping and what the common people depend upon. This is what King Cheng ought to keep in mind. Yet, with the Duke of Zhou's loyalty, could there have been nothing else about which he might advise his ruler? Why did he speak so earnestly of farming alone? Because the foundation of kingly rule assuredly lies here. At the founding of a dynasty, it is difficult for the people's circumstances to reach their ruler's attention: his position makes it so. If King Cheng could understand the hardships of the people's work and take the heart of his forebears as his own, few among the people would be unable to exert themselves to the full. Subsequently, King Cheng became an excellent king who preserved the achievements he inherited, and praise of his virtue continues unabated to this day. Does this not reveal both King Cheng's worthiness and the efficacy of the Duke of Zhou's assistance and guidance?

“Hu bowed and knocked his head to the ground: ‘May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!’”

Shui Sizhong

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭潘　批〔臣子受恩對揚之情形容殆盡〕
同考試官教諭陳　批〔讀此召虎忠愛君父之情藹然可掬〕
考試官侍讀陳　批〔警切〕
考試官侍讀體　批〔召公之忠愛蓋如此〕
大臣敬受乎君賜而因祈以無疆之壽焉夫臣
之愛君必圖其久也大臣受君賜而以萬壽祝
之忠愛寧有窮乎宣王命召穆公平淮南之夷
===
詩人叙其事以美之至此蓋曰王之有召虎也
蓋天之所以資中興也王之策命召虎者至矣
虎將何以承之哉思天寵之優渥而抑畏彌深
拜稽首者如將弗勝而不敢以紓也仰天威之
伊邇而齋慄彌至拜稽首者如將失之而不敢
以忽也維時召公所稱以報天子者將何以哉
惟願天子之萬年耳蓋臣之願于君者不惟有
一時之功而惟其有長裕之澤不惟有一時之
治而惟其有不匱之仁其在于今經營之就緒
punctuated:
同考試官教諭潘　批〔臣子受恩對揚之情，形容殆盡。〕
同考試官教諭陳　批〔讀此，召虎忠愛君父之情，藹然可掬。〕
考試官侍讀陳　批〔警切。〕
考試官侍讀體　批〔召公之忠愛，蓋如此。〕
大臣敬受乎君賜，而因祈以無疆之壽焉。夫臣之愛君，必圖其久也。大臣受君賜，而以萬壽祝之，忠愛寧有窮乎？宣王命召穆公平淮南之夷，詩人叙其事以美之。至此，蓋曰：王之有召虎也，蓋天之所以資中興也。王之策命召虎者至矣，虎將何以承之哉？思天寵之優渥，而抑畏彌深，拜稽首者，如將弗勝，而不敢以紓也；仰天威之伊邇，而齋慄彌至，拜稽首者，如將失之，而不敢以忽也。維時召公所稱以報天子者，將何以哉？惟願天子之萬年耳。蓋臣之願于君者，不惟有一時之功，而惟其有長裕之澤；不惟有一時之治，而惟其有不匱之仁。其在于今，經營之就緒……
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: 〔The feelings of a subject receiving favor and responding by extolling it are portrayed almost exhaustively.〕
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔Reading this, one can almost grasp the abundant warmth of Shao Hu’s loyalty and love for his sovereign and father.〕
Examiner Chen, Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔Admonitory and incisive.〕
Examiner Ti [?], Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔Such indeed was the Duke of Shao’s loyalty and love.〕
A great minister reverently receives his sovereign’s gifts and thereupon prays that his sovereign’s life may be without limit. A subject who loves his sovereign must surely seek his longevity. When a great minister receives his sovereign’s gifts and wishes him ten thousand years of life, can such loyalty and love ever have an end? King Xuan commanded Duke Mu of Shao to pacify the Yi peoples south of the Huai River, and the poet recounted the events to praise him. At this point, the meaning is: the king’s possession of Shao Hu was Heaven’s means of supporting the dynastic restoration. The king had bestowed the fullest honors upon Shao Hu through his written investiture; how, then, would Hu receive them? Reflecting on the abundance of the royal favor, his humility and awe grew ever deeper. He bowed and touched his forehead to the ground as though unable to bear its weight, not daring to relax. Looking up to the royal majesty so close at hand, his reverence and trembling grew ever more intense. He bowed and touched his forehead to the ground as though fearing to lose that favor, not daring to be heedless. At that moment, what words could the Duke of Shao utter in recompense to the Son of Heaven? He could only wish the Son of Heaven ten thousand years of life. For what a subject desires for his sovereign is not merely achievement for a single age, but beneficence that enriches the people enduringly; not merely good government for a single age, but benevolence that never runs dry. As for the present, his endeavors have been brought into order…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而土宇版章既有以增文武之光烈矣引之萬
年而恒逢夫康強之吉則道久化成當益有以
奠不基而垂永世之慶也其在于今疆理之告
成而聲教大同既有以紹成康之盛美矣延之
萬年而恒荷夫保定之休則道洽政治當益有
以利後人而綿卜年之歷也此則召公之願於
王者也公之愛王豈其淺哉吁此周之君臣相
與所以爲至而共成有道之長也昔周之始興
也化行江漢而天下歸是文王之德也而康公
===
實布之者也其中興也威行江漢而天下服是
宣王之烈也而穆公實與有功者也創守異時
得臣之助一也然宣王以召祖勉其臣而穆公
亦以文德勸其君則所以衍萬年之祚者豈徒
在於武功哉詩可以觀其此類矣
春秋
荆人來聘〔莊公二十有三年冬楚子使椒〕
來聘〔文公九年〕
王錫爵
punctuated:
而土宇版章，既有以增文武之光烈矣。引之萬年，而恒逢夫康強之吉，則道久化成，當益有以奠不基，而垂永世之慶也。其在于今，疆理之告成，而聲教大同，既有以紹成康之盛美矣。延之萬年，而恒荷夫保定之休，則道洽政治，當益有以利後人，而綿卜年之歷也。此則召公之願於王者也。公之愛王，豈其淺哉！吁！此周之君臣相與所以爲至，而共成有道之長也。昔周之始興也，化行江漢而天下歸，是文王之德也，而康公實布之者也。其中興也，威行江漢而天下服，是宣王之烈也，而穆公實與有功者也。創守異時，得臣之助一也。然宣王以召祖勉其臣，而穆公亦以文德勸其君，則所以衍萬年之祚者，豈徒在於武功哉！詩可以觀，其此類矣。

春秋

荆人來聘〔莊公二十有三年冬，楚子使椒〕來聘〔文公九年〕

王錫爵
translation_en:
…and the territories and their registers are manifestly established [?], already adding to the brilliant achievements of Kings Wen and Wu. Extend this for ten thousand years, continually enjoying the blessing of health and strength: as the Way endures and its transforming influence reaches fulfillment, this should further secure an enduring foundation [?] and transmit blessings to all future ages. At present, the ordering of the boundaries has been completed, and the civilizing influence of royal instruction prevails everywhere alike, already carrying forward the splendid accomplishments of Kings Cheng and Kang. Prolong this for ten thousand years, continually receiving the blessing of protection and stability: as the Way spreads everywhere and government becomes well ordered, this should bring further benefit to later generations and prolong the span of years foretold by divination. Such was the Duke of Shao’s wish for his king. Could the duke’s love for his king have been shallow? Ah! This is how the ruler and ministers of Zhou brought their mutual relations to perfection and together achieved the enduring rule of a dynasty possessed of the Way.

When Zhou first arose, its transforming influence spread through the Jiang and Han river regions, and all under Heaven gave it their allegiance. This was King Wen’s virtue, but it was Duke Kang who actually disseminated it. During Zhou’s restoration, its might spread through the Jiang and Han regions, and all under Heaven submitted. This was King Xuan’s achievement, but Duke Mu indeed shared in the accomplishment. Founding and maintaining a dynasty belonged to different times; receiving the assistance of ministers was the same in both. Yet King Xuan exhorted his minister by invoking the ancestor of the house of Shao, while Duke Mu likewise urged his ruler to cultivate civil virtue. Could the means of extending the dynasty’s allotted blessings for ten thousand years, then, have lain solely in military achievements? That the Book of Odes may be used for observation and understanding is exemplified by passages such as this.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“The men of Jing came on a diplomatic visit.” 〔Winter, the twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang. The Viscount of Chu sent Jiao〕 “to pay a diplomatic visit.” 〔The ninth year of Duke Wen.〕

Wang Xijue

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭戴 批〔議論精切筆力俊健〕
是公殺之餘也可式
考試官侍讀陳 批〔簡嚴〕
考試官侍讀瞿 批〔典則〕
春秋于遠人之慕義而漸進之于中國也夫聖
人重絕人也楚而慕義不已則可進之于中國
矣又何過求之有哉且楚之始見于經敗蔡伐
鄭聖人蓋常以夷狄擯之矣其始聘于魯則進
而稱人蓋別之于夷狄也及其再聘于魯復進
===
而稱子且名其臣蓋等之于中國也夫別之于
夷狄則漸進之矣等之于中國則遂進之矣然
則安在其爲謹華夷之辨哉蓋春秋立法之嚴
所以存尊王之義而與人之恕所以廣自新之
門有如楚人彼之慕我也爲益勤則吾之與彼
也當益進雖其前此而剪我諸姬圖我北方猾
夏之罪不可縱也今能息其猾夏之謀而爲講
信修睦之舉則一念之善亦有可與者矣固不
必追其既往也雖其後此而伐我同盟加我兵
punctuated:
同考試官教諭戴批〔議論精切，筆力俊健〕。是公殺之餘也，可式。
考試官侍讀陳批〔簡嚴〕。
考試官侍讀瞿批〔典則〕。
春秋于遠人之慕義，而漸進之于中國也。夫聖人重絕人也，楚而慕義不已，則可進之于中國矣，又何過求之有哉？且楚之始見于經，敗蔡伐鄭，聖人蓋常以夷狄擯之矣。其始聘于魯，則進而稱人，蓋別之于夷狄也；及其再聘于魯，復進而稱子，且名其臣，蓋等之于中國也。夫別之于夷狄，則漸進之矣；等之于中國，則遂進之矣。然則安在其爲謹華夷之辨哉？蓋春秋立法之嚴，所以存尊王之義；而與人之恕，所以廣自新之門。有如楚人，彼之慕我也爲益勤，則吾之與彼也當益進。雖其前此而剪我諸姬，圖我北方，猾夏之罪不可縱也，今能息其猾夏之謀，而爲講信修睦之舉，則一念之善，亦有可與者矣，固不必追其既往也。雖其後此而伐我同盟，加我兵
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor, comments: 〔The argument is incisive and exact; the writing is distinguished and vigorous.〕 This is a surviving trace of gongsha [?]; it may serve as a model.
Examiner Chen, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: 〔Concise and rigorous.〕
Examiner Qu, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: 〔Exemplary and conforming to established standards.〕
The Spring and Autumn Annals gradually admits distant peoples who admire righteousness into the central states. The Sage is reluctant to reject others utterly. If Chu persists in admiring righteousness, it can be admitted into the central states. Why demand too much of it? When Chu first appeared in the Classic, defeating Cai and attacking Zheng, the Sage indeed excluded it as barbarian. When it first sent an envoy to Lu, he advanced its standing by calling it “men,” thereby distinguishing it from the barbarians. When it again sent an envoy to Lu, he further advanced its standing by calling its ruler “Viscount” and naming his minister, thereby placing it on an equal footing with the central states. Distinguishing it from the barbarians meant gradually advancing it; placing it on an equal footing with the central states meant admitting it fully. Where, then, is the careful maintenance of the distinction between the civilized and the barbarian?
The strictness with which the Spring and Autumn Annals establishes its rules preserves the principle of honoring the king; its generosity in recognizing others opens wide the door to self-renewal. In the case of the people of Chu, the more earnestly they admire us, the further we should advance our recognition of them. Although they previously cut down our states of the Ji lineage and coveted our northern lands, offenses of disturbing the Xia states that cannot be condoned, if they can now abandon their schemes to disturb the Xia and undertake to uphold good faith and cultivate amity, even a single good intention deserves recognition. There is certainly no need to pursue their past offenses. Although afterward they might attack our allies and bring arms against us…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
亂稔禍之罪不可長也今能蓋其稔禍之衍尋
尋徼福同好之約則一日之善亦有可嘉者矣
固不必逆其將來也誠使玉帛之使交乎天下
而兵革之禍不及生民則聖人待衰世之心亦
慰矣楚固神明之後先王封國非純于夷者亦
何過絶之有哉此義明則春秋謹華夷之辨者
亦不必攘斥之過矣雖然魯于是時可晏然而
遂已乎蓋恤小事大者邦交之常而任賢圖治
者自強之道魯之于楚報其聘可也乞師報怨
不可也屈千乘之尊而會于宋盟于蜀甚至如
楚焉不可也孔子一用而齊人章章歸其侵疆
使能終用之又何楚之畏而不能自立乎夫子
之進楚蓋與楚之慕中國未及言中國自強之
道也嚴于自治而薄于責人固聖人經世之略
也
===
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕
楊于世
同考試官教諭戴　批〔善發明經傳本意可〕
punctuated:
亂，稔禍之罪不可長也。今能蓋其稔禍之衍尋，尋徼福同好之約，則一日之善亦有可嘉者矣，固不必逆其將來也。誠使玉帛之使交乎天下，而兵革之禍不及生民，則聖人待衰世之心亦慰矣。楚固神明之後、先王封國，非純于夷者，亦何過絶之有哉？此義明，則《春秋》謹華夷之辨者，亦不必攘斥之過矣。雖然，魯于是時可晏然而遂已乎？蓋恤小事大者，邦交之常；而任賢圖治者，自強之道。魯之于楚，報其聘可也，乞師報怨不可也。屈千乘之尊，而會于宋、盟于蜀，甚至如楚焉，不可也。孔子一用，而齊人章章歸其侵疆，使能終用之，又何楚之畏而不能自立乎？夫子之進楚，蓋與楚之慕中國，未及言中國自強之道也。嚴于自治而薄于責人，固聖人經世之略也。

晉欒書帥師救鄭。〔成公六年〕
楊于世
同考試官教諭戴，批〔善發明經傳本意，可〕
translation_en:
…disorder: the offense of fomenting calamity must not be allowed to persist. If Chu can now put aside its course of fomenting calamity [?] and renew an agreement to seek blessings and share friendly relations, then even a single day’s goodness deserves praise. There is certainly no need to prejudge its future conduct. If envoys bearing jade and silk truly exchanged visits throughout the realm, and the calamities of warfare did not reach the people, then the sage’s hopes for an age of decline would also be consoled. Chu was, after all, descended from divine ancestors and was a state enfeoffed by the former kings; it was not wholly barbarian. Why, then, reject it excessively? Once this principle is understood, it becomes clear that the Spring and Autumn Annals, in carefully maintaining the distinction between the Chinese and the barbarians, need not carry exclusion and rejection to excess.

Nevertheless, could Lu at this time simply rest content and do nothing further? Showing concern for small states and serving great ones are the ordinary practices of interstate relations; employing worthy men and striving for good government are the means of strengthening oneself. In its dealings with Chu, Lu could properly reciprocate a diplomatic visit, but it could not properly beg for troops to avenge a grievance. To abase the dignity of a state of a thousand chariots by attending a meeting at Song, entering a covenant at Shu, or even going to Chu was unacceptable. As soon as Confucius was employed, the people of Qi openly returned the territory they had seized. Had Lu been able to employ him to the end, why would it have feared Chu and been unable to stand on its own? In advancing Chu’s standing, the Master was approving Chu’s admiration for the Central States; he had not yet addressed how the Central States should strengthen themselves. To be exacting in governing oneself and restrained in reproaching others was indeed the sage’s strategy for ordering the world.

“Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng.” 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng.〕
Yang Yushi
Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor, comments: 〔“It ably elucidates the original meaning of the classic and its commentary and can …”〕

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
以式多士矣
考試官侍讀陳　批〔約而盡〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔得聖人慎戰意〕
春秋于伯臣深予其恤患之善焉夫善師者不
以戰爲功也欒書之救鄭有之此春秋所以予
之歟且晉楚爭鄭久矣夷夏盛衰之幾固决于
鄭之向背也自鄭與蟲牢之盟而楚有嬰齊之
伐晉欒書之救義之不可已者也在春秋時觀
之亦兵爭之常耳而君子以書救爲善之者何
===
也蓋寇不可玩而禦之者期于解紛武不可黷
而用之者期于靖亂書之帥師也初以謀勝遇
繞角而楚師潰旣以利進至桑隧而楚師出使
徒以倖勝爲常而不以遷戮爲戒其何以稱有
制之師乎書也知進知退而不冒昧以倖功能
剛能柔而不貪獲以怒敵以持重爲勇而寧避
二邑之衆以易夫小者不可與慮敵也以從善
爲衆而寧違帥之言以覺于勇者不可與定
功也一舉而鄭人紓圍逼之危晉師免傷夷之
punctuated:
以式多士矣。
考試官侍讀陳，批〔約而盡〕。
考試官侍讀瞿，批〔得聖人慎戰意〕。
春秋于伯臣，深予其恤患之善焉。夫善師者，不以戰爲功也。欒書之救鄭有之，此春秋所以予之歟？且晉楚爭鄭久矣，夷夏盛衰之幾，固决于鄭之向背也。自鄭與蟲牢之盟，而楚有嬰齊之伐，晉欒書之救，義之不可已者也。在春秋時觀之，亦兵爭之常耳，而君子以書救爲善之者，何也？蓋寇不可玩，而禦之者期于解紛；武不可黷，而用之者期于靖亂。書之帥師也，初以謀勝，遇繞角而楚師潰；旣以利進，至桑隧而楚師出。使徒以倖勝爲常，而不以遷戮爲戒，其何以稱有制之師乎？書也知進知退，而不冒昧以倖功；能剛能柔，而不貪獲以怒敵。以持重爲勇，而寧避二邑之衆，以易夫小者不可與慮敵也；以從善爲衆，而寧違帥之言，以覺于勇者不可與定功也。一舉而鄭人紓圍逼之危，晉師免傷夷之
translation_en:
…thereby serving as a model for the many candidates.

Examiner Chen, Reader-in-waiting, comments: “Concise yet comprehensive.”

Examiner Qu, Reader-in-waiting, comments: “Captures the sage’s intention to exercise caution in warfare.”

In its treatment of ministers serving hegemons, the Spring and Autumn Annals strongly commends the virtue of relieving distress. Those skilled in commanding armies do not regard fighting itself as an achievement. Luan Shu’s relief of Zheng exemplified this. Was this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals commended him? Jin and Chu had long contended for Zheng. The critical balance between the flourishing and decline of the non-Chinese and the Chinese states surely depended upon where Zheng’s allegiance lay. After Zheng joined the covenant at Chonglao, Yingqi of Chu attacked it. Luan Shu of Jin was therefore bound by righteousness to come to its relief. Viewed in the circumstances of the Spring and Autumn period, this was merely an ordinary instance of military rivalry. Why, then, do gentlemen regard the Annals’ recording of his relief expedition as praise?

Invaders must not be taken lightly, but those who resist them should aim to resolve conflict. Armed force must not be used wantonly, and those who employ it should aim to quell disorder. When Shu commanded the army, he initially prevailed through strategy: at the encounter at Raojiao, Chu’s army collapsed. He then advanced to exploit his advantage, reaching Sangsui, where Chu’s army came out. Had he merely treated fortunate victory as something assured, without guarding against bringing slaughter upon himself [?], how could his force have been called a disciplined army? Shu knew when to advance and when to retreat; he did not recklessly gamble on success. He could be firm or yielding; he did not provoke the enemy through greed for gains. He regarded steadiness as courage and preferred to avoid the forces of the two towns, because those who disdain small forces cannot be partners in assessing an enemy. He regarded following sound counsel as strength in numbers and preferred to disregard his commanders’ words, because those preoccupied with bravery [?] cannot be partners in securing success. In a single operation, the people of Zheng were relieved of the peril of siege and pressure, and Jin’s army escaped the injuries and losses of…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
則雖不迨帝王之師而所全亦多矣□□
□世之中而見書此役能無予乎故曰晋欒書
□師救鄭若曰慎如欒書庶無負師師之任矣
蓋取節焉者也邲之役羣帥多不欲戰荀林父
不能斷以從善而奪于先縠遂敗晋師故聖人
慎戰以勝不可必而殃民之罪大也此欒武子
之所以可予也然鄢陵之役復貪一時之捷而
忽范文子內憂之忠言則其智亦末矣噫安得
如范文子者而與之謀國乎
===
禮記
所以達天道順人情之大竇也
王之翰
同考試官教諭安　批〔以典雅之辭析精微之理其可以式矣〕
考試官侍讀陳　批〔以性情立說良是〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔精確〕
記者於禮義而喻其甚切於性情焉夫禮義所
以通達乎性情也其所係爲甚切者而容可去
punctuated:
則雖不迨帝王之師，而所全亦多矣。□□□世之中，而見書此役，能無予乎？故曰：「晋欒書□師救鄭。」若曰：「慎如欒書，庶無負師師之任矣。」蓋取節焉者也。邲之役，羣帥多不欲戰，荀林父不能斷以從善，而奪于先縠，遂敗晋師。故聖人慎戰，以勝不可必，而殃民之罪大也。此欒武子之所以可予也。然鄢陵之役，復貪一時之捷，而忽范文子內憂之忠言，則其智亦末矣。噫！安得如范文子者而與之謀國乎？

禮記
所以達天道順人情之大竇也。
王之翰
同考試官教諭安，批〔以典雅之辭析精微之理，其可以式矣。〕
考試官侍讀陳，批〔以性情立說，良是。〕
考試官侍讀瞿，批〔精確。〕
記者於禮義而喻其甚切於性情焉。夫禮義所以通達乎性情也，其所係爲甚切者，而容可去
translation_en:
…then, although they did not equal the armies of the sage emperors and kings, they nevertheless preserved much. Amid an age of [illegible text], seeing this campaign of Luan Shu, could one withhold approval? Thus the text says: “Luan Shu of Jin [illegible character] the army to relieve Zheng.” It is as though it said: “With caution such as Luan Shu’s, one might hope not to fail in the responsibility of commanding an army.” It thus approves a particular aspect of his conduct. At the battle of Bi, most of the commanders did not wish to fight. Xun Linfu could not resolve to follow sound counsel, but yielded to Xian Hu, and consequently brought defeat upon Jin’s army. Thus the Sage was cautious about warfare, because victory cannot be assured, while the guilt of bringing calamity upon the people is great. This is why Luan Wuzi deserves approval. Yet at the battle of Yanling, he again coveted a momentary victory and disregarded Fan Wenzi’s loyal warning about troubles within the state. His wisdom, then, was limited after all. Alas! Where could one find someone like Fan Wenzi with whom to deliberate on affairs of state?

Record of Rites (Liji)
“The great channel through which the Way of Heaven is realized and human feelings are accorded their proper course.”
Wang Zhihan
Associate Examiner An, Instructor, comments: 〔“With elegant language, he analyzes subtle principles. This may serve as a model.”〕
Examiner Chen, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: 〔“Basing the argument on human nature and feelings is indeed correct.”〕
Examiner Qu, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: 〔“Precise and sound.”〕
The author of the Record uses a comparison to show how intimately ritual and rightness concern human nature and feelings. Ritual and rightness are the means by which human nature and feelings find full expression. Since what depends upon them is so vital, how could they be dispensed with…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
哉宜記者取譬以示人也蓋謂禮義之用大矣
哉以益身心以合幽明而天道人情亦不能違
之矣彼天道具於人蔽於物欲則湮矣惟禮義
擴其未發之中則不息者純其體明覺者昭其
用成性存存而胥此立天下之有焉是禮義天
道所不能免也人情動於內一有乖戾則逆矣
惟禮義養其中節之和則未應之先無取必旣
感之後無凝滯物至知知而胥此通天下之故
焉是禮義人情所不能免也禮義從違而天道
===
通塞係之則靜虛之地非此無以彰其微猶之
竇焉夫人所共由而不可須臾離也其殆達天
道之大竇乎禮義用舍而人情順逆因之則應
感之常非此無以得其正猶之竇焉夫人所共
履而不可頃刻違也其殆順人情之大竇乎是
天道不自達也而所以達者禮義之功不容誣
也人情不自順也而所以順者禮義之用不可
揜也蓋未有人而不由夫竇則亦未有違天道
順人情而不以禮義者矣不然猶欲其出入而
punctuated: 哉！宜記者取譬以示人也。蓋謂禮義之用大矣哉！以益身心，以合幽明，而天道人情亦不能違之矣。彼天道具於人，蔽於物欲則湮矣。惟禮義擴其未發之中，則不息者純其體，明覺者昭其用，成性存存，而胥此立天下之有焉。是禮義，天道所不能免也。人情動於內，一有乖戾則逆矣。惟禮義養其中節之和，則未應之先無取必，旣感之後無凝滯，物至知知，而胥此通天下之故焉。是禮義，人情所不能免也。禮義從違而天道通塞係之，則靜虛之地，非此無以彰其微。猶之竇焉，夫人所共由而不可須臾離也，其殆達天道之大竇乎！禮義用舍而人情順逆因之，則應感之常，非此無以得其正。猶之竇焉，夫人所共履而不可頃刻違也，其殆順人情之大竇乎！是天道不自達也，而所以達者，禮義之功不容誣也；人情不自順也，而所以順者，禮義之用不可揜也。蓋未有人而不由夫竇，則亦未有違天道順人情而不以禮義者矣。不然，猶欲其出入而
translation_en:
…could they be dispensed with? It is fitting that the recorder should use an analogy to instruct people. Surely the efficacy of ritual and rightness is great! They benefit body and mind and unite the hidden and the manifest; neither the Way of Heaven nor human feelings can depart from them. The Way of Heaven is inherent in human beings, but when obscured by desires for material things, it becomes submerged. Only ritual and rightness enlarge the equilibrium that exists before feelings arise. Then unceasing activity makes its substance pure, and luminous awareness makes its functioning manifest. One’s perfected nature is continually preserved, and through this all that exists under Heaven is established. Thus ritual and rightness are indispensable to the Way of Heaven. Human feelings stir within; once any discord arises, they become disordered. Only ritual and rightness nurture the harmony in which feelings attain their proper measure. Then, before responding, one insists on no predetermined outcome; after being moved, one remains free of obstruction. As things arrive, understanding apprehends them, and through this one comprehends the affairs of the world. Thus ritual and rightness are indispensable to human feelings.

Whether the Way of Heaven flows freely or is obstructed depends on whether ritual and rightness are followed or violated. Within the realm of stillness and emptiness, their aid is necessary to reveal its subtleties. They are like an opening through which everyone passes and from which no one can depart even for an instant. Are they not indeed the great opening through which the Way of Heaven is given free passage? Whether human feelings are ordered or disordered depends on whether ritual and rightness are employed or discarded. In the regular course of stimulus and response, their aid is necessary to attain correctness. They are like an opening through which everyone proceeds and from which no one can deviate even momentarily. Are they not indeed the great opening through which human feelings are brought into accord? Thus the Way of Heaven does not attain free passage of itself: the achievement of ritual and rightness in giving it passage cannot be denied. Human feelings do not become ordered of themselves: the efficacy of ritual and rightness in ordering them cannot be concealed. Since no one can avoid passing through such an opening, neither has anyone ever ‘contravened the Way of Heaven and brought human feelings into accord’ [?] without employing ritual and rightness. Otherwise, it would be like wishing to go out and come in while…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
樂之實也噫誰能出入而不由實哉至於禮義
獨昧之是故舍之而不由者衆也唯聖人全備
乎此有以建中和之極性由此立情由此出而
萬事萬化舉不外是焉故致中和則天地位萬
物育而達順之實亦惟禮義焉盡之信非人之
大端矣乎是聖人之能事也
然則先王之爲樂也以法治也善則行象
德矣
諸鐈
===
同考試官教諭安　批〔紆徐容與即其文亦深於樂者〕
考試官侍讀陳　批〔明潔〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔醇雅〕
記者原先王作樂有本而因以感乎人也夫民
行象德則樂化之感人亦深矣非本於天地而
能然哉今夫天人異形而同理君民有感而即
應治無所法者固傷世無功矣然則先王之爲
樂也何如哉盖樂以成教而教非强爲也盖取
punctuated:
樂之實也。噫！誰能出入而不由實哉？至於禮義，獨昧之，是故舍之而不由者衆也。唯聖人全備乎此，有以建中和之極，性由此立，情由此出，而萬事萬化舉不外是焉。故致中和，則天地位、萬物育，而達順之實亦惟禮義焉盡之。信非人之大端矣乎？是聖人之能事也。
然則先王之爲樂也，以法治也，善則行象德矣。
諸鐈
同考試官教諭安　批〔紆徐容與，即其文亦深於樂者。〕
考試官侍讀陳　批〔明潔。〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔醇雅。〕
記者原先王作樂有本，而因以感乎人也。夫民行象德，則樂化之感人亦深矣，非本於天地而能然哉？今夫天人異形而同理，君民有感而即應，治無所法者，固傷世無功矣。然則先王之爲樂也，何如哉？盖樂以成教，而教非强爲也，盖取
translation_en:
…the substance of music [?]. Alas! Who can enter and leave without passing through the substance [?; the context suggests a doorway]? Yet when it comes to ritual and rightness, people alone remain ignorant of them; thus many abandon them and do not follow them. Only the sage possesses these in their entirety and can thereby establish the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony. Through these, human nature is established and feelings issue forth; none of the myriad affairs and transformations falls outside them. Thus, when equilibrium and harmony are fully realized, Heaven and Earth take their proper places and the myriad things flourish. The full realization of giving passage to Heaven’s Way and bringing human feelings into accord likewise rests entirely upon ritual and rightness. Are these not indeed the great essentials of human life? This is what the sage can accomplish.
“Thus, in making music, the former kings took it as their model for governance. When it was good, conduct reflected virtue.” [?]
Zhu Qiao 諸鐈
Associate Examiner An, Instructor, comments: 〔“Unhurried and at ease: his writing itself shows someone with a deep understanding of music.”〕
Examiner Chen, Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔“Clear and clean.”〕
Examiner Qu, Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔“Pure and elegant.”〕
The author of the Record traces how the former kings’ creation of music had a foundation, through which they moved people. When the people’s conduct reflects virtue, music’s transforming influence has indeed moved them deeply. Could this occur unless it were rooted in Heaven and Earth? Now Heaven and humanity differ in form but share the same principle; when the ruler exerts an influence, the people respond at once. Governance that has no model to follow certainly harms the world and achieves nothing. How, then, did the former kings make music? Music serves to complete moral instruction, and instruction is not something imposed by force: rather, it draws upon …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
諸寒暑焉因事以作樂而事非任智也蓋取諸
風雨焉求端於不已而治功之旁達一化工之
默運所以立之學等而作新天下者殆體其撰
而不過宣會於合同而有心之成能實無心之
妙用所以比諸節奏而乖範斯民者殆玩其樂
而不違夫然則教焉以時而鼓舞自妙於宜民
事焉以節而推行適協於當可是惟天下至德
能之而治莫善於此矣民之行不有以象君之
德哉蓋君民之分不同而從善之心則一樂行
===
而感既以啓其好德之情機觸而應自能神其
敏德之化下上乎弌而則君自治者近天子之
光矣四國攸順而觀化自淑者歸維皇之極矣
奚有於教之傷世而事之無功也耶是則法天
地而樂之本所由立感人心而樂之化所由行
先王作樂之善孰有加於此哉抑季札觀樂於
魯而曰如天地之無不覆載蓋與此章之旨互
相發明然寒暑有時而愆候風雨有時而失節
則參贊之責固有攸在是以聖人必先法天地
punctuated: 諸寒暑焉。因事以作樂，而事非任智也，蓋取諸風雨焉。求端於不已，而治功之旁達，一化工之默運，所以立之學等而作新天下者，殆體其撰而不過。宣會於合同，而有心之成能，實無心之妙用，所以比諸節奏而乖範斯民者，殆玩其樂而不違。夫然則教焉以時，而鼓舞自妙於宜民；事焉以節，而推行適協於當可。是惟天下至德能之，而治莫善於此矣。民之行不有以象君之德哉？蓋君民之分不同，而從善之心則一。樂行而感，既以啓其好德之情；機觸而應，自能神其敏德之化。下上乎弌，而則君自治者，近天子之光矣；四國攸順，而觀化自淑者，歸維皇之極矣。奚有於教之傷世而事之無功也耶？是則法天地而樂之本所由立，感人心而樂之化所由行。先王作樂之善，孰有加於此哉？抑季札觀樂於魯，而曰：「如天地之無不覆載。」蓋與此章之旨互相發明。然寒暑有時而愆候，風雨有時而失節，則參贊之責固有攸在。是以聖人必先法天地
translation_en:
…from cold and heat. They created music in accordance with affairs, yet their conduct of affairs did not rely on cleverness: they took their model from wind and rain. They sought its source in ceaseless activity; the far-reaching accomplishments of their government were one with the silent workings of nature’s creative power. Thus, in establishing it at the various levels of schooling [?] and renewing all under Heaven, they embodied nature’s operations without exceeding them. They gave expression to convergence in harmony and unity; what conscious effort accomplished was in truth the wondrous working of that which acts without conscious intent. Thus, in arranging it into measured rhythms and providing a model for the people [?], they savored its music without departing from it.

Accordingly, instruction followed the seasons, and its power to inspire and animate was wondrously suited to the people; affairs followed their proper measures, and their execution accorded precisely with what was fitting. Only one possessing the utmost virtue under Heaven could accomplish this, and no government could surpass it. Would not the people’s conduct then reflect their ruler’s virtue? Although ruler and people differ in station, their hearts are one in following goodness. When music is performed and moves them, it awakens their love of virtue; when the impulse touches them and they respond, it gives wondrous efficacy to their transformation toward diligence in virtue. Those above and below are united: those who model themselves on the ruler and govern themselves draw near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven. All the lands in the four directions submit: those who observe this transforming influence and improve themselves return to the sovereign’s supreme standard. How could instruction then harm the age, or affairs fail to bear fruit?

Thus, by taking Heaven and Earth as their model, they established the foundation of music; by moving human hearts, they brought music’s transforming influence into effect. Who could surpass the former kings in their excellence at creating music? Moreover, when Ji Zha witnessed the music of Lu, he said: “It is like Heaven and Earth, which leave nothing uncovered or unsupported.” This and the meaning of the present chapter illuminate one another. Yet cold and heat sometimes depart from their proper seasons, and wind and rain sometimes lose their due measure. The responsibility for participating in and assisting the work of Heaven and Earth therefore surely rests somewhere. Hence the sage must first take as his model Heaven and Earth…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之和以作樂及樂作而天地之和應焉此天人
相須之妙裁成輔相之功不容諉者樂之爲用
大矣哉噫吾心一天地也必豫養聲氣之元而
後可
第貳塲
論
孔子登太山而小天下
余毅中

同考試官教諭陳　批〔力醇雅雄勁讀之令人竦然〕
===
〔理學精邃而詞藻蔚〕
〔然宿擅塲之作〕
考試官侍讀陳　批〔得孟子狀聖道本意〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔說理之文〕
聖人之道非有加於天下也人自小之而聖人
之道始大於天下矣夫道之在天下非小也自
人之學焉者各因其性之所近得其一偏一曲
而不適於道之全是故見其小也聖人之道雖
punctuated:
之和以作樂，及樂作而天地之和應焉。此天人相須之妙，裁成輔相之功不容諉者。樂之爲用大矣哉！噫！吾心一天地也，必豫養聲氣之元而後可。

第貳塲
論
孔子登太山而小天下
余毅中
同考試官教諭潘　批〔認理真切而議論揮〕
同考試官教諭陳　批〔力醇雅雄勁，讀之令人竦然。〕
〔理學精邃而詞藻蔚〕
〔然宿擅塲之作。〕
考試官侍讀陳　批〔得孟子狀聖道本意。〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔說理之文。〕

聖人之道非有加於天下也，人自小之，而聖人之道始大於天下矣。夫道之在天下非小也，自人之學焉者各因其性之所近，得其一偏一曲，而不適於道之全，是故見其小也。聖人之道雖
translation_en:
…the harmony of Heaven and Earth in making music; once the music is made, the harmony of Heaven and Earth responds to it. Such is the subtle mutual dependence of Heaven and humanity: the work of regulating and assisting their operations cannot be shirked. Great indeed is the efficacy of music! Ah! My own mind is itself a Heaven and Earth; one must first nurture the source of sound and vital energy before this can be accomplished.

Second Session
Discourse
“Confucius Ascended Mount Tai and Considered All under Heaven Small”
Yu Yizhong

Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: 〔The understanding of principle is true and precise, and the argument unfolds [?].〕
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔Its force is pure, elegant, vigorous, and strong; reading it inspires awe.〕
〔The learning of principle is profound and refined, and the literary embellishment luxuriant …〕

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
非有異于人而獨會其全造其極故聖人自視
亦惟自盡吾道自人望之則見聖人之道大而
天下之言道術者皆小而不足爲矣然則求道
者固以聖爲至而聖道亦豈有加于天下哉孔
子登太山而小天下夫天下非小物也往哲之
所經綸後賢之所稱述其爲道術非小數也而
謂孔子小之者孟子非徒尊孔子蓋示人以吾
道之至使之不安于偏而與端之徒亦不得以
小吾道也夫物各有至道亦有至太山者高之
===
至也聖人者道之至也人惟無見于太山則步
仞之丘亦足以爲高觀太山而後知吾所履之
卑也人惟無見于聖人則一善之得亦足以爲
多觀聖人而後知吾所得之狹也此孟子覺天
下之意也易曰地中有山謙夫以山之高而縕
于地之卑此山之所以安其基也聖人雖道高
天下豈知其所至之若此哉故有卑以自牧而
已矣未始自尚其事而居天下于卑也有小心
翼翼而已矣未始自多其能而居天下于狹也
punctuated:
非有異于人，而獨會其全、造其極，故聖人自視，亦惟自盡吾道；自人望之，則見聖人之道大，而天下之言道術者皆小而不足爲矣。然則求道者固以聖爲至，而聖道亦豈有加于天下哉？孔子登太山而小天下。夫天下非小物也，往哲之所經綸、後賢之所稱述，其爲道術非小數也。而謂孔子小之者，孟子非徒尊孔子，蓋示人以吾道之至，使之不安于偏，而與端之徒亦不得以小吾道也。夫物各有至，道亦有至。太山者，高之至也；聖人者，道之至也。人惟無見于太山，則步仞之丘亦足以爲高；觀太山而後知吾所履之卑也。人惟無見于聖人，則一善之得亦足以爲多；觀聖人而後知吾所得之狹也。此孟子覺天下之意也。

《易》曰：「地中有山，謙。」夫以山之高而縕于地之卑，此山之所以安其基也。聖人雖道高天下，豈知其所至之若此哉？故有卑以自牧而已矣，未始自尚其事而居天下于卑也；有小心翼翼而已矣，未始自多其能而居天下于狹也。
translation_en:
…is no different from that of other people, yet the sage alone comprehends it in its entirety and attains its utmost reach. Thus, in his own eyes, the sage merely fulfills our Way to the utmost. Viewed by others, however, the sage’s Way appears great, while all the teachings about the Way and its practice offered by others throughout the world appear small and insufficient to pursue. Those who seek the Way certainly regard sagehood as the highest attainment; yet how could the sage’s Way add anything to what is already present in the world?

Confucius ascended Mount Tai and regarded the world as small. Now, the world is no small thing. What the wise men of antiquity ordered and governed, and what later worthies praised and expounded, were no petty methods in the realm of the Way and its practice. In saying that Confucius regarded these as small, Mencius was not merely honoring Confucius. He was showing people the utmost reach of our Way, so that they would not rest content with a partial understanding, and so that adherents of deviant teachings [?] could not belittle our Way either. Things each have their highest attainment, and the Way likewise has its highest attainment. Mount Tai represents the utmost in height; the sage represents the utmost in the Way. Only because people have never seen Mount Tai can a hill a few paces or fathoms high seem sufficiently lofty to them. Only after viewing Mount Tai do they realize how low the ground on which they stand is. Only because people have never seen a sage can the attainment of a single good quality seem ample to them. Only after viewing a sage do they realize how narrow their own attainments are. This is Mencius’s purpose in awakening the world.

The Book of Changes says: “Within the earth is a mountain: Modesty.” A mountain, despite its height, is enfolded within the lowliness of the earth: this is how it secures its foundation. Although the sage’s Way towers above the world, how could he be conscious that his attainment has reached such a height? Thus he merely nurtures himself through humility; he has never exalted his own deeds and assigned the rest of the world a lowly place. He is merely cautious and reverent; he has never vaunted his own abilities and deemed the rest of the world narrow in its attainments.

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
然心愈卑而道愈高心彌小而道彌大此孔子
所以超乎天下而天下之言道術者皆小也夫
孔子之道亦天下共由之道猶之太山然人皆
得登之而未始沮人之進也然人之不至于道
者其失有二志之不立也功之不繼也志之不
立者則以聖道爲不可幾及而自棄不爲猶之
畏太山之高却立而不肯登者也功之不繼者
雖知聖道之可及少有得焉而自畫不進猶之
慕太山之高登之而不果至者也由志之不立
===
功之不繼而吾道之至始獨歸于聖人故孔子
之小天下非直優入聖域者不足以與知也今
夫太山有登其麓者矣有至其半者矣有至其
巔者矣登其麓者視人之在平地者所見則有
間矣而未遠也至其半則加遠矣至其巔則又
遠矣夫所履益進則所至益高所至益高則所
見益遠所見益遠則視下益小孔子之小天下
葢至爲實至見爲實見非可以料想測度求也
吾獨于孔子之學不厭者而觀其深也夫道之
punctuated: 然心愈卑而道愈高，心彌小而道彌大。此孔子所以超乎天下，而天下之言道術者皆小也。夫孔子之道，亦天下共由之道，猶之太山然，人皆得登之，而未始沮人之進也。然人之不至于道者，其失有二：志之不立也，功之不繼也。志之不立者，則以聖道爲不可幾及，而自棄不爲，猶之畏太山之高，却立而不肯登者也。功之不繼者，雖知聖道之可及，少有得焉，而自畫不進，猶之慕太山之高，登之而不果至者也。由志之不立、功之不繼，而吾道之至始獨歸于聖人。故孔子之小天下，非直優入聖域者，不足以與知也。今夫太山，有登其麓者矣，有至其半者矣，有至其巔者矣。登其麓者，視人之在平地者，所見則有間矣，而未遠也；至其半則加遠矣，至其巔則又遠矣。夫所履益進，則所至益高；所至益高，則所見益遠；所見益遠，則視下益小。孔子之小天下，葢至爲實至，見爲實見，非可以料想測度求也。吾獨于孔子之學不厭者，而觀其深也。夫道之
translation_en:
Yet the humbler his heart, the loftier his Way; the more modest his heart, the greater his Way. This is why Kongzi rose above all under Heaven, and why all others who speak of the Way and its arts seem small. Kongzi’s Way is also the Way that all under Heaven may follow. It is like Mount Tai: everyone may climb it, and it has never obstructed anyone’s advance. Yet those who fail to attain the Way have two failings: they do not establish their resolve, or they do not sustain their effort. Those who do not establish their resolve consider the sages’ Way beyond reach and abandon themselves to inaction. They are like people who fear Mount Tai’s height and stand back, unwilling to climb. Those who do not sustain their effort know that the sages’ Way is attainable, but after gaining a little, they set limits upon themselves and advance no further. They are like people who admire Mount Tai’s height and begin to climb, but never reach the summit. It is because people fail to establish their resolve and sustain their effort that the highest attainment of our Way comes to belong to the sages alone. Thus, unless one has truly and fully entered the realm of sagehood, one cannot share in understanding how Kongzi regarded all under Heaven as small.

Now, among those who climb Mount Tai, some reach its foothills, some its midpoint, and some its summit. Those who reach its foothills already differ in what they see from people on level ground, but their view does not yet extend far. At the midpoint it extends farther, and at the summit farther still. The farther one advances, the higher one reaches; the higher one reaches, the farther one sees; and the farther one sees, the smaller what lies below appears. Kongzi’s regarding all under Heaven as small rested upon an actual attainment and an actual vision. It cannot be grasped through conjecture and estimation. I discern his depth particularly in his tireless learning. Now, the Way’s…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
全人得其一偏一曲猶挾之以自多而孔子孜
學之不厭不倦此殆其所以造道之至而天下
之道術不足以爲大者也夫吾道之體廣大配
天地變通配四時未始有偏也而仁者得之以
爲仁智者得之以爲智清者得之以爲清和者
得之以爲和任者得之以爲任又其次則禮樂
名物儀文度數亦皆執之以成名辨之以爲慱
非不皆有得于道然自孔子之集大成而時出
之者觀之蓋不啻太山之于丘垤矣孔子之聖
===
亦非有離于智也由志學以至耳順蓋智之至
而非一偏之智也亦非有離于仁也由志學以
至從心蓋仁之至而非一偏之仁也時清而清
則清其所兼而非一偏之清也時和而和則和
其所兼而非一偏之和也時任而任則任其所
兼而非一偏之任也祖述堯舜則兼堯舜憲章
文武則兼文武上律下襲則兼天地至如老聃
之于禮師襄之于琴郯子之于官無不兼而識
之由是知孔子之道其高如天而偏焉者皆不
punctuated: 全，人得其一偏一曲，猶挾之以自多，而孔子孜學之不厭不倦，此殆其所以造道之至，而天下之道術不足以爲大者也。夫吾道之體，廣大配天地，變通配四時，未始有偏也。而仁者得之以爲仁，智者得之以爲智，清者得之以爲清，和者得之以爲和，任者得之以爲任。又其次，則禮樂名物、儀文度數，亦皆執之以成名，辨之以爲慱。非不皆有得于道，然自孔子之集大成而時出之者觀之，蓋不啻太山之于丘垤矣。孔子之聖，亦非有離于智也。由志學以至耳順，蓋智之至，而非一偏之智也。亦非有離于仁也。由志學以至從心，蓋仁之至，而非一偏之仁也。時清而清，則清其所兼，而非一偏之清也；時和而和，則和其所兼，而非一偏之和也；時任而任，則任其所兼，而非一偏之任也。祖述堯舜，則兼堯舜；憲章文武，則兼文武；上律下襲，則兼天地。至如老聃之于禮，師襄之于琴，郯子之于官，無不兼而識之。由是知孔子之道，其高如天，而偏焉者皆不
translation_en:
…the wholeness of the Way: people who obtain just one aspect or one narrow portion of it still clutch it and pride themselves upon it. Yet Kongzi diligently pursued learning, never sated and never weary. This was probably how he attained the utmost reaches of the Way, beside which the teachings and practices of the world could not count as great. The substance of our Way matches Heaven and Earth in its vastness and the four seasons in its transformations; it has never been partial. Yet the benevolent grasp it as benevolence, the wise as wisdom, the pure as purity, the harmonious as harmony, and those who shoulder responsibility as responsibility. At a lower level, there are the names and objects of ritual and music, ceremonial forms, and measures and numerical rules: people likewise hold fast to these to establish their reputations, and distinguish their details to claim broad learning [?]. It is not that they have gained nothing of the Way. But viewed from the standpoint of Kongzi, who gathered its elements into a grand completion and manifested them as circumstances required, the difference is no less than that between Mount Tai and little mounds.

Kongzi’s sagehood was not separate from wisdom. From setting his heart on learning to attaining an ear attuned to what it heard, he reached the utmost wisdom, not wisdom confined to one aspect. Nor was it separate from benevolence. From setting his heart on learning to following his heart’s desires, he reached the utmost benevolence, not benevolence confined to one aspect. When circumstances called for purity, he was pure: purity was thus something he encompassed, not a purity confined to one aspect. When circumstances called for harmony, he was harmonious: harmony was thus something he encompassed, not a harmony confined to one aspect. When circumstances called for shouldering responsibility, he shouldered it: responsibility was thus something he encompassed, not a responsibility confined to one aspect. In transmitting the traditions of Yao and Shun, he encompassed Yao and Shun; in taking Kings Wen and Wu as his models, he encompassed Wen and Wu; in conforming above to Heaven and following below the patterns of Earth, he encompassed Heaven and Earth. Even such things as Lao Dan’s knowledge of ritual, Music Master Xiang’s knowledge of the qin, and the Viscount of Tan’s knowledge of official offices—he encompassed and understood them all. From this we know that Kongzi’s Way is as high as Heaven, while those confined to one aspect of it are all unable to …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
免于自卑也由是知孔子之道其廣如地而偏
焉者皆不免于自小也由是知孔子之道變通
如四時而偏焉者猶四時之各一其氣而不能
相通也夫是之謂孔子登太山而小天下其所
至者固宜有以小之也然豈孔子有加于吾性
哉吾性本全孔子特全之耳夫太山雖至高亦
土壤之積也孔子雖至聖亦衆善之積也人各
安于一偏一曲自卑自小以裂吾道而不覩天
地之全則孟子之尊孔子以尊吾道豈容已哉
===
戰國之時佛老未興而楊墨之徒則已鼓邪說
以惑世彼見吾儒之執其一偏一曲則曰儒之
道小也爲吾儒之徒者習見其然則亦曰吾儒
之道誠小也孟子憂之是故尊孔子以立極蓋
孔子之道尊則異端之說息亦其衛道之心不
得已者也不然孔子于仁聖自謂未能孟子之
賢豈不知孔子之心而顧爲是以尊之哉然則
求孔子之道當柰何昔曰若升高必自下言至
也以漸也曰無自廣以狹人言受之以虛也虛
punctuated:
免于自卑也。由是知孔子之道，其廣如地，而偏焉者皆不免于自小也。由是知孔子之道，變通如四時，而偏焉者猶四時之各一其氣而不能相通也。夫是之謂「孔子登太山而小天下」，其所至者固宜有以小之也。然豈孔子有加于吾性哉？吾性本全，孔子特全之耳。夫太山雖至高，亦土壤之積也；孔子雖至聖，亦衆善之積也。人各安于一偏一曲，自卑自小，以裂吾道，而不覩天地之全，則孟子之尊孔子以尊吾道，豈容已哉？

戰國之時，佛老未興，而楊墨之徒則已鼓邪說以惑世。彼見吾儒之執其一偏一曲，則曰：「儒之道小也。」爲吾儒之徒者，習見其然，則亦曰：「吾儒之道誠小也。」孟子憂之，是故尊孔子以立極。蓋孔子之道尊，則異端之說息，亦其衛道之心不得已者也。不然，孔子于仁聖自謂未能，孟子之賢豈不知孔子之心，而顧爲是以尊之哉？然則求孔子之道當柰何？昔曰：「若升高，必自下。」言至也以漸也。曰：「無自廣以狹人。」言受之以虛也。虛
translation_en:
…cannot avoid making themselves lowly. From this we know that the Way of Kongzi is as broad as the earth, while those confined to one aspect of it cannot avoid making themselves small. From this we know that the Way of Kongzi changes and adapts like the four seasons, while those confined to one aspect resemble the seasons each possessing its own vital force but unable to communicate with one another. This is what is meant by “Kongzi ascended Mount Tai and found all under Heaven small.” Given the heights he attained, he surely had grounds for seeing it as small. Yet did Kongzi add anything to our nature? Our nature is inherently complete; Kongzi merely realized its completeness. Though Mount Tai is supremely high, it too is an accumulation of earth; though Kongzi is supremely sagely, he too is an accumulation of all good qualities. If people each rest content with one partial aspect or narrow corner, making themselves lowly and small, fragmenting our Way and failing to behold the wholeness of Heaven and Earth, how could Mengzi refrain from honoring Kongzi in order to honor our Way?

In the Warring States period, the teachings of Fo and Lao—Buddhism and the teachings of Laozi—had not yet arisen, but the followers of Yang Zhu and Mo Di were already promoting pernicious doctrines to delude the world. Seeing our Confucian scholars cling to a single partial aspect or narrow corner, they said, “The Way of the Confucians is small.” Those belonging to our Confucian tradition, accustomed to seeing this, likewise said, “Our Confucian Way is indeed small.” Mengzi was troubled by this, and therefore honored Kongzi to establish the supreme standard. For when the Way of Kongzi is honored, heterodox doctrines subside. This, too, was something his determination to defend the Way compelled him to do. Otherwise, since Kongzi himself said that he had not attained benevolence and sagehood, how could someone as worthy as Mengzi have failed to understand Kongzi’s mind, and yet have honored him in this fashion? How, then, should one seek the Way of Kongzi? It was said of old, “If you would ascend to a height, you must begin below.” This means that one reaches it gradually. It was also said, “Do not consider yourself broad-minded and others narrow.” This means receiving it with an open mind. With an open mind…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
冑觀增崇聿啓萬年之運
晉臨赫奕茂延
五位之禧
玄穹申錫於無疆
華闕煥新於有象懽騰
朝野喜溢臣民恭惟
皇帝陛下
紹統承基
明倫建極
===
心涵太始
道格重玄
操三重以宅尊
秉一敬而作則

仁育義裁配乾坤覆載之德舉世荷
