punctuated:
冑觀增崇，聿啓萬年之運；晉臨赫奕，茂延五位之禧。玄穹申錫於無疆，華闕煥新於有象，懽騰朝野，喜溢臣民。
恭惟皇帝陛下，紹統承基，明倫建極，心涵太始，道格重玄，操三重以宅尊，秉一敬而作則。文經武緯，妙陰陽闔闢之機；仁育義裁，配乾坤覆載之德。舉世荷帡幪於無外，羣生樂怙冒以多年。乃當丁巳之秋，再卜大工之建，荷
translation_en:
…The towers [?] have been raised higher, opening an era of ten thousand years; Your Majesty’s approach shines resplendently, abundantly extending the blessings of the five positions [?]. Heaven above bestows anew its limitless gifts; the magnificent palace gates shine renewed in visible form. Jubilation rises throughout court and country, and joy overflows among officials and people.
We reverently reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor has continued the imperial succession and inherited its foundations, clarified human relationships and established the supreme standard. Your mind embraces the Great Beginning; your Way reaches the deepest mystery. You wield the three weighty prerogatives to occupy the exalted station, and hold fast to undivided reverence to set the example. With civil accomplishments as warp and military achievements as weft, you wondrously govern the workings of yin and yang as they close and open. Nurturing through benevolence and regulating through righteousness, you match the virtue of Heaven and Earth in sheltering and sustaining all. The whole world receives your protection, with none excluded; all living beings have rejoiced in your sustaining shelter for many years. Then, in the autumn of the dingsi year [1557], an auspicious time was again divined for undertaking the great construction project, receiving…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
上天之仁愛祗切
仰承監
文祖之規模載恢
堂構治欲宅中而圖大制惟因舊以爲新庶
民子來遐邇爭先趨事百神響答川谷競
爾效奇玉石出自
帝畿梗楠貢於侯服乃
使公輸削墨爰
命奚斯董成測用土圭營以城矩文礎屹立盤
===
厚地以奠基畫棟高驤摩層霄而承宇闢
閶闔于
天上聳閣道于雲中兩觀崔嵬門闕遂來乎賢
士五城縹緲樓居夙好於仙人璇題切紫
極以崢嶸朱栱茲廣寒而掩映雕文有燦
九龍獻彩於承明綺甍斯飛五鳳騰輝於
景福雖
今中勿亟
念每切於紓民而說以忘勞功遂成於不日際
punctuated: 上天之仁愛，祗切仰承；監文祖之規模，載恢堂構。治欲宅中而圖大，制惟因舊以爲新。庶民子來，遐邇爭先趨事；百神響答，川谷競爾效奇。玉石出自帝畿，梗楠貢於侯服。乃使公輸削墨，爰命奚斯董成。測用土圭，營以城矩。文礎屹立，盤厚地以奠基；畫棟高驤，摩層霄而承宇。闢閶闔于天上，聳閣道于雲中。兩觀崔嵬，門闕遂來乎賢士；五城縹緲，樓居夙好於仙人。璇題切紫極以崢嶸，朱栱茲廣寒而掩映。雕文有燦，九龍獻彩於承明；綺甍斯飛，五鳳騰輝於景福。雖今中勿亟，念每切於紓民，而說以忘勞，功遂成於不日。際
translation_en: …the benevolence of Heaven above is received with earnest reverence. Taking the pattern of the cultured ancestor as a model, the palace buildings are expanded anew. In governing, the aim is to occupy the center and plan on a grand scale; in construction, to make the new from the old. The common people come like children to their parent, those near and far vying to hasten to the work. The hundred spirits respond like an echo, and rivers and valleys compete to offer their marvels. Jade and stone come from the imperial domain; geng and nan timber [?] are presented as tribute from the feudatory regions. Thus Gongshu is set to wield the inked line and cutting tools, and Xi Si is commanded to oversee completion. Measurements are taken with the earthen sundial tablet, and construction is laid out with the builder’s square. Ornamented foundation stones stand firm, rooted in the deep earth to establish the base; painted ridge beams soar high, brushing the layered heavens and supporting the roofs. The gates of Heaven open on high, and elevated passageways tower among the clouds. The twin gate towers rise majestically, and worthy men accordingly come to the palace gates. The five cities shimmer in the distance: dwelling in lofty towers has long been the delight of immortals. Jade-adorned gable ends rise steeply toward the Purple Pole; vermilion brackets stand here amid the alternating light and shade of the Palace of Vast Cold [?]. Carved ornament gleams: nine dragons display their colors at Chengming. Splendid roof ridges take flight: five phoenixes spread their radiance over Jingfu. Although the injunction is to avoid haste [?], and the concern is always to ease the people’s burdens, they rejoice and forget their toil, so that the work is completed in scarcely any days. At a time when…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
二百載承平之後新億兆人心目之觀矧
當
萬壽之期誕受四方之賀人心永
戴儼衆拱於
北辰
天眷益申表
上壽於南極金莖承九霄之露玉液調
萬年之觴衣冠序列於兩階玉帛錯陳於萬
國瑞圖啓
===
聖集熒河溫洛之符重譯來
朝紛貢獒獻雉之侶聽簫韶而率同獸舞委環
佩而共效嵩呼濟濟蹌蹌與三千之禮樂
明明赫赫壯百二之山河陳王會而展國容
肅官聯而聽吏治日臨仙掌
九重遙醉春桃雲近蓬萊五色常浮曉仗
治隆一統
慶洽萬方效三祝於華封欣欣相告納八荒
於
punctuated: 二百載承平之後，新億兆人心目之觀。矧當萬壽之期，誕受四方之賀。人心永戴，儼衆拱於北辰；天眷益申，表上壽於南極。金莖承九霄之露，玉液調萬年之觴。衣冠序列於兩階，玉帛錯陳於萬國。瑞圖啓聖，集熒河溫洛之符；重譯來朝，紛貢獒獻雉之侶。聽簫韶而率同獸舞，委環佩而共效嵩呼。濟濟蹌蹌，與三千之禮樂；明明赫赫，壯百二之山河。陳王會而展國容，肅官聯而聽吏治。日臨仙掌，九重遙醉春桃；雲近蓬萊，五色常浮曉仗。治隆一統，慶洽萬方。效三祝於華封，欣欣相告；納八荒於
translation_en:
…after two hundred years of peace, renewing the spectacle presented to the eyes and minds of the countless millions. Moreover, on the occasion of Your Majesty’s birthday, you receive congratulations in abundance from every quarter. The people’s hearts uphold you forever, solemnly surrounding you as the stars surround the Northern Pole; Heaven’s favor is renewed and increased, and the Southern Pole Star signals supreme longevity. The bronze stalk catches dew from the highest heavens; the jade nectar is blended in the cup that pledges ten thousand years. Officials in cap and robe stand in ordered ranks beside the two stairways; jade and silk from the myriad states are displayed in rich array. Auspicious diagrams herald the sage, gathering the portents of the Ying River [?] and the warm Luo River. Through successive interpreters, visitors come to court in throngs, bringing tribute of mastiffs and pheasants. Hearing the Shao music of the pipes, all join in the dance of the beasts; letting their girdle pendants hang low as they bow, together they echo the acclamations from Mount Song. Dignified and moving in measured step, they participate in the three thousand rites and their music [?]; brilliant and resplendent, they magnify the grandeur of mountains and rivers whose strategic strength lets two withstand a hundred.

The assembly of rulers is arrayed to display the realm’s majesty; the ranks of officials are made solemn, and reports on administration are heard. The sun shines upon the immortal’s palm; deep within the ninefold palace, spring peaches bring distant intoxication. Clouds draw near Penglai; their five colors ever float above the ceremonial guard at dawn. Government flourishes in unified rule; rejoicing reaches every land. Emulating the three blessings offered by the border warden of Hua, all joyfully tell one another; bringing the eight farthest regions into…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
壽域蕩蕩難名寔
宗社無疆之休神人永賴之慶也臣某等職忝
瘝曠仰荷
大造之容事屬經營愧乏微勞之效幸値
告成之日恭逢
誕聖之辰功與運成百禮斯洽事與時竝萬福
攸同傾葵心而莫罄名言效雀躍而祇勤
頌禱伏願
繁祉駢集
===
景運彌昌
寶曆流光天錫維新之祚
金甌鞏固人詞有道之長
駿烈遠竝乎舞干
鴻恩覃被於比屋
參三才而
壽居四大
履百順而慶集
punctuated:
壽域，蕩蕩難名，寔宗社無疆之休、神人永賴之慶也。臣某等職忝瘝曠，仰荷大造之容；事屬經營，愧乏微勞之效。幸値告成之日，恭逢誕聖之辰。功與運成，百禮斯洽；事與時竝，萬福攸同。傾葵心而莫罄名言，效雀躍而祇勤頌禱。
伏願繁祉駢集，景運彌昌；寶曆流光，天錫維新之祚；金甌鞏固，人詞有道之長；駿烈遠竝乎舞干，鴻恩覃被於比屋；參三才而壽居四大，履百順而慶集
translation_en:
…the realm of longevity, whose boundless extent defies description. This is indeed an unending blessing for the ancestral temples and the altars of state, a cause for rejoicing upon which spirits and humankind may forever rely. We, your servants So-and-so and the others, unworthily occupy our offices and leave our duties unfulfilled, yet receive the forbearance of Your Majesty’s great, nurturing beneficence. Charged with planning and undertaking this work, we are ashamed to have rendered not even a small service. Fortunately, the day of its completion coincides with the sacred anniversary of Your Majesty’s birth. Achievement and auspicious fortune reach fulfillment together, and the hundred rites are harmoniously observed; the undertaking coincides with the fitting season, and myriad blessings converge. Our hearts turn toward you as sunflowers toward the sun, yet words cannot exhaust our feelings; we leap like sparrows for joy and can only devote ourselves to praise and prayer.
We humbly wish that abundant blessings may gather together and your glorious fortune flourish ever more; that your precious imperial reign may spread its radiance, and Heaven bestow blessings ever renewed; that the golden bowl of your realm may remain secure, and the people speak of the enduring rule of one who possesses the Way [?]; that your great achievements may equal those ancient victories won through the shield dance, and your vast grace extend to every household; that, taking your place among the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and Humanity—your longevity may rank among the Four Great Ones, and that, proceeding in accord with every favorable influence, blessings may gather…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
日升月恒茂衍箕疇之斂福
天長地久末邁周室之卜年臣某等無任瞻
天仰
聖忻躍慶戴之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第叁場
策五道
===
第一問
余毅中
同考試官教諭潘　批
聖製一策正欲觀士子誦法之素此作具悉
聖祖
聖上謨訓之大蓋仰
聖文之郁郁而觀其深者錄之
同考試官教諭陳　批
聖祖
punctuated:
日升月恒，茂衍箕疇之斂福；天長地久，末邁周室之卜年。臣某等無任瞻天仰聖、忻躍慶戴之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第叁場
策五道

第一問
余毅中

同考試官教諭潘批：
聖製一策，正欲觀士子誦法之素。此作具悉聖祖、聖上謨訓之大，蓋仰聖文之郁郁而觀其深者，錄之。

同考試官教諭陳批：
聖祖
translation_en:
…As the sun rises and the moon waxes, may the gathering of blessings described in Jizi’s Great Plan flourish and spread; enduring as Heaven and Earth, may the dynasty surpass [?] the years divined for the royal house of Zhou. We, your servants So-and-so and the others, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty with boundless joy, offering congratulations and devoted allegiance. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulations for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

First Question
Yu Yizhong

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor:
This imperially composed policy question expressly seeks to ascertain the grounding candidates have acquired through reciting and taking the imperial teachings as their model. This essay comprehensively understands the greatness of the plans and instructions of the Sagely Progenitor and His Majesty. Its author admires the rich splendor of the imperial writings and perceives their depth. Selected for inclusion.

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
□□□制作之盛天地爲昭誠非下土所能循覩而子能識其大其日
紀載
盛美以備金匱石室之藏當有望也
考試官侍讀陳　批　〔初場二場俱精練五策博洽此篇尤詳整可觀殆服習〕
聖訓而有槩於中者乎
考試官侍讀瞿　批　〔五策俱該洽此作尤鋪張得體錄此猶崑山積玉探得一焉亦知其爲珍異〕
也
===
帝王之文所以經緯天地光昭後先者豈
有他哉本之於心則大德立焉垂之於訓
則大業廣焉施之於邦國被之於後世則
大化神焉夫是以凝性命之精關經綸之
秘動天地感鬼神諧民人孚遠近天下萬
世悉囿於文明之治而不知其由也然則
我
聖祖之與
皇上文之炳煥與天地爲昭者豈易測哉夫天
punctuated:
□□□制作之盛，天地爲昭，誠非下土所能循覩，而子能識其大。其日紀載盛美，以備金匱石室之藏，當有望也。

考試官侍讀陳批：〔初場二場俱精練，五策博洽，此篇尤詳整可觀，殆服習〕聖訓而有槩於中者乎？

考試官侍讀瞿批：〔五策俱該洽，此作尤鋪張得體，錄此猶崑山積玉，探得一焉，亦知其爲珍異〕也。

帝王之文，所以經緯天地、光昭後先者，豈有他哉？本之於心，則大德立焉；垂之於訓，則大業廣焉；施之於邦國，被之於後世，則大化神焉。夫是以凝性命之精，關經綸之秘，動天地，感鬼神，諧民人，孚遠近，天下萬世悉囿於文明之治，而不知其由也。然則我聖祖之與皇上，文之炳煥，與天地爲昭者，豈易測哉？夫天
translation_en:
…□□□ The magnificence of these institutions and compositions shines together with Heaven and Earth; truly, it is beyond what those here below can survey, yet you can discern its greatness. There is reason to hope that you will someday [?] record these splendid achievements for preservation in golden coffers and stone chambers.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Reader-in-Waiting: 〔The work in both the first and second sessions is polished and accomplished. The five policy essays display broad and thorough learning; this essay is especially detailed, well ordered, and worthy of attention. Surely the writer has diligently studied〕 the imperial instructions and grasped their essentials in his heart?

Comment by Examiner Qu, Reader-in-Waiting: 〔All five policy essays are comprehensive and well informed. This composition is especially fitting in its expansive exposition. Selecting it is like drawing a single piece from the accumulated jade of Mount Kun: even from this one, its rarity and excellence can be recognized〕.

The writings of emperors and kings order Heaven and Earth and shed their light upon past and future. How could their source be anything else? Rooted in the heart, they establish great virtue; handed down as instructions, they extend great achievements; applied throughout the realm and transmitted to later generations, they make the great work of moral transformation wondrously efficacious. Thus they concentrate the essence of human nature and Heaven’s mandate, encompass the mysteries of ordering the world, move Heaven and Earth, stir ghosts and spirits, bring the people into harmony, and win the trust of those near and far. All beneath Heaven, through myriad generations, dwell within the bounds of enlightened rule without knowing how it comes about. Can the brilliant writings of our Sagely Progenitor and His Majesty, shining together with Heaven and Earth, then be readily fathomed? Now, Heaven…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
地之心不可得而見觀天地之文則天地
之心於穆不已者可識矣帝王之心不可
得而見觀帝王之文則帝王之心純粹以
精者亦可識矣堯之文思舜之文明禹之
文命文王之所以爲文皆是物也自今觀
之典謨訓誥之書垂之於經以憲萬世曷
故哉亦惟精一執中之傳列聖授受以爲
心法本之也漢祖起泗上以開基唐宗興
晉陽而化國宋祖由陳橋以踐祚皆䏿削
===
除羣雄混一四海卓哉武矣然而漢黜治
於詩書宋慙德於禪受故樸而不文有以
也唐太宗雖銳情經術刻意詞章然沿六
朝之風競四聲之巧而乏帝王之象則太
宗之穢德實爲之矣洪惟我
太祖高皇帝以天縱之資當羣雄之禍不忍民
之無主徐起而應之兼僞國而收其驅除
逬殘胡而還之沙漠取帝王所自立之地
而版章之拯腥羶所舊染之民而洗滌之
punctuated:
地之心不可得而見，觀天地之文，則天地之心於穆不已者可識矣。帝王之心不可得而見，觀帝王之文，則帝王之心純粹以精者亦可識矣。堯之文思，舜之文明，禹之文命，文王之所以爲文，皆是物也。自今觀之，典謨訓誥之書，垂之於經，以憲萬世，曷故哉？亦惟精一執中之傳，列聖授受以爲心法，本之也。漢祖起泗上以開基，唐宗興晉陽而化國，宋祖由陳橋以踐祚，皆䏿削除羣雄，混一四海，卓哉武矣！然而漢黜治於詩書，宋慙德於禪受，故樸而不文，有以也。唐太宗雖銳情經術，刻意詞章，然沿六朝之風，競四聲之巧，而乏帝王之象，則太宗之穢德實爲之矣。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，以天縱之資，當羣雄之禍，不忍民之無主，徐起而應之。兼僞國而收其驅除，逬殘胡而還之沙漠，取帝王所自立之地而版章之，拯腥羶所舊染之民而洗滌之。
translation_en:
…the heart of Heaven and Earth cannot be seen directly. Yet by observing their patterned manifestations, one can recognize the profound and unceasing workings of that heart. The hearts of emperors and kings cannot be seen directly. Yet by observing their writings, one can likewise recognize the purity and refinement of their hearts. Yao’s cultivated thought, Shun’s luminous cultivation, Yu’s cultured ordinances, and that which made King Wen worthy of the name “Cultured”—all embody this same thing. Viewed from our own day, why have the canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations been preserved in the Classics as models for ten thousand generations? It is because they are rooted in the transmission of refinement and single-mindedness and of holding fast to the mean, handed down from sage to sage as the method of the heart.
The founding emperor of Han arose in the region of the Si River to establish his dynasty’s foundations; the Tang emperor arose at Jinyang to transform the realm; and the founding emperor of Song came from Chenqiao to ascend the throne. All cut down and eliminated the contending warlords [?] and united all within the Four Seas. How outstanding was their martial achievement! Yet Han rule slighted the Odes and Documents [?], while Song’s virtue was compromised by the circumstances of its receiving the throne through abdication. There were thus reasons why they possessed unadorned substance but lacked cultural refinement. Although Tang Taizong devoted himself ardently to classical learning and applied himself painstakingly to literary composition, he followed the fashion of the Six Dynasties, competing in ingenious manipulation of the four tones while lacking the bearing of an emperor or king. It was Taizong’s sullied virtue that brought this about.
We reverently reflect upon our Emperor Taizu Gao. Endowed with Heaven-bestowed gifts, he encountered the calamities wrought by contending warlords. Unable to bear that the people should have no sovereign, he rose in due course to answer their need. He annexed the illegitimate states and reaped the benefit of their clearing away his opponents; he drove out the remaining Hu and sent them back to the desert. He took the lands where emperors and kings had established themselves and registered and demarcated them [?]; he rescued the people long tainted by the rank smell of meat and mutton and cleansed them.

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
怙冒極玄黄所覆載照臨同日月所出入
保大定功之武自開闢以來所未有也然
且干戈倥偬之時而不忘講藝
幾務經綸之暇而時發爲文矜恤黎元而
德音布
勑臣隣而大戒昭綏徠裔夷而文告行精禋
大祀而樂章奏奠告百神而祝辭具敷宣理道
而雜文述發攄性情而詩歌作
獨運睿藻
===
親灑奎翰一揮而數千百言立就代言之臣讋
服而登諸玉板紀言之史將述而藏諸金
匱其見於詹同樂韶鳳之所集與後臣之
所續者可伏覩矣猗歟盛哉敬陳其略
即位有
詔求言有
詔赦宥輕重有
詔興□學校有
□□□文稅秋糧有
punctuated: 怙冒極玄黄所覆載，照臨同日月所出入。保大定功之武，自開闢以來所未有也。然且干戈倥偬之時，而不忘講藝；幾務經綸之暇，而時發爲文。矜恤黎元而德音布，勑臣隣而大戒昭，綏徠裔夷而文告行，精禋大祀而樂章奏，奠告百神而祝辭具，敷宣理道而雜文述，發攄性情而詩歌作。獨運睿藻，親灑奎翰，一揮而數千百言立就。代言之臣讋服而登諸玉板，紀言之史將述而藏諸金匱。其見於詹同、樂韶鳳之所集與後臣之所續者，可伏覩矣。猗歟盛哉！敬陳其略：即位有詔，求言有詔，赦宥輕重有詔，興□學校有□□□文稅秋糧有
translation_en: …His sheltering protection extended throughout all that Heaven covers and Earth supports; his illumination reached wherever the sun and moon rise and set. His martial achievements in preserving greatness and securing lasting accomplishment were unprecedented since the beginning of the world. Yet even amid the press of warfare he did not forget to study the arts of learning; in intervals between managing the affairs of state, he would give expression to his thoughts in writing. In compassion for the common people, he issued gracious pronouncements; in admonishing his ministers, he made solemn warnings clear; in pacifying and attracting the distant peoples, he promulgated proclamations. For the great sacrifices performed with pure devotion, musical hymns were played; for offerings and announcements to the hundred spirits, invocations were provided. To expound the principles of good government, he composed miscellaneous writings; to express his nature and feelings, he wrote poems and songs. He alone fashioned these sagacious compositions, personally wielding the imperial brush: with one sweep, hundreds or thousands of words were completed on the spot. The ministers charged with drafting pronouncements on his behalf bowed in awed admiration and recorded them on jade tablets; the historians who recorded his words would transmit them and preserve them in golden coffers. These writings may reverently be viewed in the collections compiled by Zhan Tong and Yue Shaofeng, and in the continuations made by later ministers. Ah, how magnificent! I respectfully set forth their outlines: upon his accession there was an edict; to solicit frank counsel there was an edict; on pardons and leniency for offenses of varying gravity there was an edict; on establishing □ schools there was [illegible text; the following 文 is unclear, ?]; on levying the autumn grain tax there was…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
詔而稅糧之免蓋十餘舉而不靳
仁恩覃布至誠感孚而天下之民煦嫗以有生
安善良而革頑梗漢氏下山東之詔不得
而擬焉答
御殿上壽有
制除授百官有
勅中書政務有
勅天下有司有
勅欲羣臣務公去私有
===
勅枚舉其凡吏僕未可盡也著之話言引之藝
極而天下之臣莫不奔走率職無敢曠越
以速戾宋氏謹刑訓廉之頒不得而擬焉
詔諭暹羅國王而賜之印
詔諭安南國王而使之息兵養民
詔諭高麗國王而卻其美貢
書諭占城國王而使之修睦於安南
詔諭琉球國王而使之息戰育民
聖武布昭
punctuated:
詔。而稅糧之免，蓋十餘舉而不靳。仁恩覃布，至誠感孚，而天下之民煦嫗以有生，安善良而革頑梗，漢氏下山東之詔不得而擬焉。答御殿上壽有制，除授百官有勅，中書政務有勅，天下有司有勅，欲羣臣務公去私有勅。枚舉其凡，吏僕未可盡也。著之話言，引之藝極，而天下之臣莫不奔走率職，無敢曠越以速戾，宋氏謹刑訓廉之頒不得而擬焉。
詔諭暹羅國王而賜之印，詔諭安南國王而使之息兵養民，詔諭高麗國王而卻其美貢，書諭占城國王而使之修睦於安南，詔諭琉球國王而使之息戰育民。聖武布昭
translation_en:
…an edict. Remissions of the grain tax were granted more than ten times, without stint. Benevolent grace spread far and wide, and utmost sincerity inspired trust. The people throughout the realm were nurtured and sustained in life; the good were settled in peace, and the obstinate reformed. The Han dynasty’s edict to Shandong cannot compare with these. There was an imperial decree answering the birthday felicitations presented in the imperial hall; imperial commands concerning appointments to the various offices; commands concerning the governmental affairs of the Central Secretariat; commands to the responsible officials throughout the realm; and commands urging all ministers to serve the public interest and abandon private interests. Even an enumeration of their main categories could not exhaust them [? “clerks and servants”]. These were set forth in instructive pronouncements, guiding officials toward the highest standards. Thus all ministers throughout the realm hastened to discharge their duties; none dared neglect or exceed them and thereby incur punishment. The Song dynasty’s promulgations urging caution in punishment and inculcating incorruptibility cannot compare with these.
An edict instructed the king of Xianluo and bestowed a seal upon him. An edict instructed the king of Annan to cease hostilities and nurture his people. An edict instructed the king of Gaoli and declined his splendid tribute. A letter instructed the king of Zhancheng to cultivate amity with Annan. An edict instructed the king of Liuqiu to end warfare and foster his people. The sage sovereign’s martial might shone far and wide…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
天聲不殺邊方夷徼莫不輸琛奉藩席槀歸命
無敢干度以犯順者漢文賜南粤尉佗之
書不得而擬焉
而
祀天地則爲之樂府侑之以九奏申之以九歌
社稷帝王咸備焉肅雍和鳴情文兼至足以降
天神出地祇而禮人鬼矣於神則二儀三
光嶽鎭海瀆
宗廟諸神有奠告之文於人則勝國之君與其
===
諭祭之有文禮度辭肅義深情至足以使百神
受職而衆工咸勸矣至于雜文之作率多
關於世教是故觀七曜天體循環之論而
知天道之常也觀堯湯水旱之説而知天
人之際也觀設喻文而知好善惡惡之情
也觀省頑文而知修德善終之理也其詞
嚴其義正其博喻也曲而有章君君臣臣
之道盡於此矣至於詩賦之作尤有關於
舊臣與元勲死事之臣皆
punctuated:
天聲不殺，邊方夷徼莫不輸琛奉藩，席槀歸命，無敢干度以犯順者。漢文賜南粤尉佗之書，不得而擬焉。
而祀天地，則爲之樂府，侑之以九奏，申之以九歌，社稷帝王咸備焉。肅雍和鳴，情文兼至，足以降天神、出地祇而禮人鬼矣。於神，則二儀、三光、嶽鎭、海瀆、宗廟諸神，有奠告之文；於人，則勝國之君與其諭祭之有文，禮度辭肅，義深情至，足以使百神受職而衆工咸勸矣。
至于雜文之作，率多關於世教。是故觀七曜天體循環之論，而知天道之常也；觀堯湯水旱之説，而知天人之際也；觀設喻文，而知好善惡惡之情也；觀省頑文，而知修德善終之理也。其詞嚴，其義正，其博喻也曲而有章，君君臣臣之道盡於此矣。至於詩賦之作，尤有關於舊臣與元勲死事之臣皆
translation_en:
…His heavenly renown suffered no diminution. Throughout the borderlands and distant foreign territories, all offered precious objects and acknowledged their vassal status; seated upon straw in submission, they pledged allegiance. None dared transgress the established limits and defy the rightful order. Even Emperor Wen of Han’s letter to Tuo, Commandant of Nanyue, cannot compare with these writings.
For sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, he composed ritual music, accompanying the offerings with nine musical performances and further expressing their meaning through nine songs. Provision was likewise complete for sacrifices to the gods of soil and grain and to former emperors and kings. Solemn, harmonious, and concordant in sound, these works perfected both feeling and formal expression, sufficing to bring down the celestial spirits, call forth the earthly deities, and duly honor the spirits of the dead. For the divine powers—the Two Forces of Heaven and Earth, the Three Luminaries, the sacred peaks and guardian mountains, the seas and great rivers, and the spirits of the ancestral temple—there were texts for offerings and announcements. For human recipients, there were writings proclaiming sacrifices to the rulers of the preceding dynasty and their … [?]. Measured in ritual observance and solemn in diction, profound in meaning and consummate in feeling, they sufficed to ensure that the hundred spirits fulfilled their offices and that all officials were encouraged in their duties.
As for his miscellaneous prose, it mostly concerned moral instruction for the world. Thus, reading his discourse on the cyclical movements of the Seven Luminaries and celestial bodies, one understands the constancy of Heaven’s Way. Reading his explanation of the floods and droughts under Yao and Tang, one understands the relationship between Heaven and humanity. Reading his “Essay Setting Forth Analogies” (Sheyu wen), one understands the disposition to love goodness and hate evil. Reading his “Essay Admonishing the Obstinate” (Xingwan wen), one understands the principle of cultivating virtue and attaining a good end. His diction is rigorous and his meaning upright; his extensive analogies explore particulars while maintaining an orderly pattern. The Way by which rulers act as rulers and ministers as ministers is fully expressed here. As for his poetry and rhapsodies, these are especially concerned with …
Former officials and founding servants of outstanding merit, together with officials who died in the discharge of their duties, all … [This final fragment appears displaced in the transcription; it apparently belongs after “the rulers of the preceding dynasty and their” above.][?]

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
性情是故賦鴛囀皇州而感大化之循環
賦四瀆潦水而感二氣之姤和詠東風而
有春滿乾坤之句詠濟時而有寰中擊壤
之情達於天同於物其爲思也止乎禮義
樂樂利利之休盡於此矣故當時文學之
臣得於親炙者亦止能形容其
天葩睿藻之妙而已誠意伯劉基曰雄深宏偉
言雅而旨遠至于
詔諭遐方明燭萬里若洞見其肺肝眞所謂
===
天生神明可望而不可及者矣學士宋濂曰建
中于民寤寐弗忘則有虞阜財解愠之歌
也夙夜修省常如神明森列左右則湯武
盤杅几杖之銘也殷彝周鼎未足喻其古
也太山喬嶽未足喻其高也風霆流形未
足喻其變化也起居注郭傳曰去浮靡之
華惇淳古之本爛乎與日星同其耀也風
雲同其變也河嶽同其高深也大章韶頀
同其奏也浩乎與江漢同其波汀漫汪溢
punctuated: 性情。是故賦鴛囀皇州，而感大化之循環；賦四瀆潦水，而感二氣之姤和；詠東風，而有春滿乾坤之句；詠濟時，而有寰中擊壤之情。達於天，同於物，其爲思也止乎禮義，樂樂利利之休盡於此矣。故當時文學之臣，得於親炙者，亦止能形容其天葩睿藻之妙而已。誠意伯劉基曰：「雄深宏偉，言雅而旨遠。至于詔諭遐方，明燭萬里，若洞見其肺肝，眞所謂天生神明，可望而不可及者矣。」學士宋濂曰：「建中于民，寤寐弗忘，則有虞阜財解愠之歌也；夙夜修省，常如神明森列左右，則湯武盤杅几杖之銘也。殷彝周鼎，未足喻其古也；太山喬嶽，未足喻其高也；風霆流形，未足喻其變化也。」起居注郭傳曰：「去浮靡之華，惇淳古之本，爛乎與日星同其耀也，風雲同其變也，河嶽同其高深也，大章韶頀同其奏也。浩乎與江漢同其波，汀漫汪溢，
translation_en: …human nature and feelings. Thus, in composing a rhapsody on mandarin ducks warbling in the imperial capital [?], he was moved by the cycles of cosmic transformation; in composing a rhapsody on the floodwaters of the Four Waterways, he was moved by the meeting and harmony of the two vital forces, yin and yang. In singing of the east wind, he wrote of spring filling Heaven and Earth; in singing of bringing aid to his age, he expressed the feeling of people throughout the realm playing at striking the ground—a sign of peaceful contentment. Reaching to Heaven and attuned to all things, his thoughts remained within ritual propriety and righteousness. The blessings of rejoicing in what brings people joy and benefiting them in what benefits them were fully expressed here. Thus even the literary ministers of that time who received his personal instruction could do no more than describe the wonders of his heavenly blossoms and imperial compositions. Liu Ji, Earl of Chengyi, said: “Majestic and profound, expansive and grand: his language is elegant and his meaning far-reaching. When he issues edicts to distant regions, his insight illuminates ten thousand li, as though he could see directly into their innermost hearts. Truly, he possesses what is called Heaven-born spiritual understanding: one may gaze toward him, but cannot attain his heights.” Academician Song Lian said: “Establishing the mean among the people, never forgetting it whether waking or sleeping—these are the songs of the lord of Youyu, Shun, enriching the people's resources and relieving their resentment. Cultivating himself and examining his conduct morning and night, always as though spirits stood arrayed closely on either side—these are the inscriptions on the basin, bowl, armrest, and staff of Tang and Wu. The ritual vessels of Yin and the tripods of Zhou do not suffice to convey his writings' antiquity; Mount Tai and the lofty peaks do not suffice to convey their loftiness; wind and thunder taking visible form do not suffice to convey their transformations.” Imperial Diarist Guo Chuan said: “He casts aside superficial, extravagant ornament and strengthens the foundations of ancient simplicity. Resplendent, his writings share the brilliance of sun and stars, the transformations of wind and cloud, the height and depth of rivers and mountains, and the harmonies of the ancient musical works Dazhang, Shao, and Hu. Vast, they share the surging waves of the Yangzi and Han rivers, spreading and overflowing [?]…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
莫能窺其涯涘也冲乎與陽春同其和煦
而草木得以遂其生也可謂模寫得其似
矣要其所自則我
太祖之全德寔本之見於存心省躬精誠錄者
可考而知也故宋濂又曰
天德粹純無聲色之好無遊畋䟽樂之從聚精
會神凝思至道形於心聲功同造化非言
語形容可盡也郭傳又曰
天才英邁
===
聖體純穆涵養冲素蓄之厚者施必溥源之澄
者流必清故其發於外者光明正大有如
此恭惟我
聖上聖神文武駕古帝王而同符
聖祖
宸章睿藻簡冊森嚴固非草茅賤士所能窺測
也然於節
頒中外珎藏秘館者則嘗竊讀而仰識
皇極之敷言矣謹拜手稽首鋪張其一二可乎
punctuated:
莫能窺其涯涘也；冲乎與陽春同其和煦，而草木得以遂其生也。」可謂模寫得其似矣。要其所自，則我太祖之全德寔本之，見於《存心》《省躬》《精誠錄》者，可考而知也。故宋濂又曰：「天德粹純，無聲色之好，無遊畋䟽樂之從；聚精會神，凝思至道，形於心聲，功同造化，非言語形容可盡也。」郭傳又曰：「天才英邁，聖體純穆，涵養冲素。蓄之厚者施必溥，源之澄者流必清，故其發於外者光明正大有如此。」
恭惟我聖上，聖神文武，駕古帝王而同符聖祖。宸章睿藻，簡冊森嚴，固非草茅賤士所能窺測也。然於節頒中外、珎藏秘館者，則嘗竊讀而仰識皇極之敷言矣。謹拜手稽首，鋪張其一二，可乎？
translation_en:
…none can discern its bounds. Serene, it shares the genial warmth of spring, allowing plants and trees to fulfill their growth.” This may be called a portrayal that captures its likeness. If we seek its source, however, its true foundation is the perfect virtue of our Taizu. This can be ascertained by examining what appears in the Records of Preserving the Mind, Examining Oneself, and Perfect Sincerity. Thus Song Lian also said: “His heavenly virtue is pure and unalloyed. He has no fondness for music and sensual beauty, nor does he indulge in excursions, hunting, or idle pleasures [?]. Concentrating his energies and gathering his spirit, he meditates deeply upon the supreme Way. Expressed in the voice of his heart, his achievement equals that of creation itself; words and descriptions cannot exhaust it.” Guo Chuan also said: “His heaven-endowed talent is outstanding; his sagely nature is pure and reverent, nurtured in serenity and simplicity. Where accumulation is abundant, its benefits must spread widely; where the source is clear, the stream must be clear. Thus what he expresses outwardly possesses such brilliance, uprightness, grandeur, and rectitude.”
We reverently reflect that our present Sage Sovereign, sagely and divine, accomplished in civil and martial affairs, surpasses the emperors and kings of antiquity and accords with our Sagely Ancestor. His imperial compositions and discerning literary embellishments stand in solemn array in the written volumes. They are certainly beyond the capacity of a humble scholar of the countryside to fathom. Yet I have ventured to read those writings periodically promulgated at court and throughout the realm and treasured in the palace library, and have thereby reverently come to understand the pronouncements setting forth the sovereign standard. With hands respectfully joined and forehead bowed to the ground, may I expound upon one or two of them?

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
大敃元一
詔則重瞻日月之光明倫再宜則復覩綱常之
紀災變寛恤則氣合雨潤之滋祀儀釐正
則族嚴夷夏之辨謹時巡則
大狩龍飛有録重農事則無逸豳風有頌廣
聖謨則表尚書之三要揚
祖德則疏遺治之五事
續念農詩而成
先志
===
答賀雪吟而追喜起
郊禋有詠妙達於天人也
平臺有詞泰交於上下也
顯陵渡河之作以志感也
御製祭懽雨小賦以志喜也其諸
欽天有頌
翊學有詩
五箴有解
七陵有述
punctuated: 大敃元一詔，則重瞻日月之光；明倫再宜，則復覩綱常之紀；災變寛恤，則氣合雨潤之滋；祀儀釐正，則族嚴夷夏之辨。謹時巡，則大狩龍飛有録；重農事，則無逸豳風有頌；廣聖謨，則表尚書之三要；揚祖德，則疏遺治之五事。續念農詩而成先志，答賀雪吟而追喜起。郊禋有詠，妙達於天人也；平臺有詞，泰交於上下也；顯陵渡河之作，以志感也；御製祭懽雨小賦，以志喜也。其諸欽天有頌，翊學有詩，五箴有解，七陵有述，
translation_en: In the edict concerning the great inaugural act [?], we behold anew the radiance of sun and moon; in the renewed proclamation clarifying human relations [?], we again discern the ordering of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues. In extending relief amid disasters and anomalies, its spirit accords with the nourishing moisture of rain; in rectifying sacrificial rites, it rigorously maintains the distinction between the peoples beyond the civilized realm and those within it [?]. Care for the seasonal tours finds expression in records of the great royal hunt and the dragon’s ascent; attention to agriculture finds expression in eulogies invoking “Against Idleness” and the “Airs of Bin.” In expanding the sagely counsels, he sets forth the three essentials of the Book of Documents; in exalting his ancestor’s virtue, he expounds five matters of governance handed down to him. He continues the poem “Concern for Agriculture,” fulfilling his predecessor’s aspirations; he answers the verses congratulating him on snowfall, recalling the ancient song of ruler and ministers rejoicing and rising to their tasks. His verses on the suburban sacrifices wonderfully comprehend the relations between Heaven and humanity; his lyrics on the Platform express harmonious intercourse between those above and below. His composition on crossing the river on the journey to Xianling records his heartfelt emotion; his imperially composed short rhapsody on sacrifice and rejoicing in rain [?] records his delight. Among his other works are a eulogy on revering Heaven, a poem on supporting learning, explanations of the Five Admonitions, and an account of the Seven Imperial Mausoleums…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
除夕有作並誦
聖製豈能備觀而盡識哉日星燦爛雲漢昭回
誠與典謨訓誥同體而媲美
聖祖經天緯地之文有非漢唐宋諸君所能彷
彿其萬一者何也蓋由其有心法以爲之
本耳
聖祖嘗諭侍臣曰人心虛靈乘氣機出入操而
存之爲難
聖上亦嘗與輔臣討論理道作
===
敬一箴以自儆心學之純
聖上與
聖祖後先一揆也
聖上之敬一即
聖祖之操存皆統於精一者也心同則道同道
同則文同此
明聖鑒盛而
作述並隆歟然愚嘗謂創業者惟忠其文之不
足守成者惟恐其武之未振我
punctuated:
除夕有作，並誦聖製，豈能備觀而盡識哉？日星燦爛，雲漢昭回，誠與典謨訓誥同體，而媲美聖祖經天緯地之文，有非漢唐宋諸君所能彷彿其萬一者，何也？蓋由其有心法以爲之本耳。聖祖嘗諭侍臣曰：「人心虛靈，乘氣機出入，操而存之爲難。」聖上亦嘗與輔臣討論理道，作《敬一箴》以自儆。心學之純，聖上與聖祖後先一揆也。聖上之敬一，即聖祖之操存，皆統於精一者也。心同則道同，道同則文同。此明聖鑒盛，而作述並隆歟？

然愚嘗謂，創業者惟忠其文之不足，守成者惟恐其武之未振。我
translation_en:
…For New Year’s Eve there are compositions as well. Reciting these imperial writings together, how could one survey them fully and comprehend them all? They shine like the sun and stars, like the luminous sweep of the Milky Way. Truly, they share the character of the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements of the Book of Documents, and rival in beauty the Sagely Founder’s writings that ordered Heaven and Earth. Why do they possess qualities of which the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song could not approximate even one ten-thousandth? It is because they have a method of cultivating the mind as their foundation.

The Sagely Founder once instructed his attendant ministers: “The human mind is empty and numinously perceptive; it comes and goes with the workings of vital energy. To grasp and preserve it is difficult.” His Majesty likewise once discussed the principles of good government with his chief ministers and composed the Admonition on Reverent Oneness (Jingyi zhen) to admonish himself. In the purity of their learning of the mind, His Majesty and the Sagely Founder follow the same standard, successor and predecessor alike. His Majesty’s reverent oneness is precisely the Sagely Founder’s grasping and preserving the mind: both are governed by refinement and singleness. When minds are the same, the Way is the same; when the Way is the same, their writings are the same. Is this why enlightened sagely discernment flourishes [?], and both original composition and the transmission of inherited teachings prosper together?

Yet I have ventured to say that a founder is concerned only [?] that his civil accomplishments are insufficient, while a ruler who preserves an established realm fears only that his martial power has not been fully asserted. Our…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖祖偃武而復綏之以文今
聖上敷文而且
拳拳於修攘之略蓋文武兼備
帝王之全用也識其勢而緩急之
帝王之所以善其用也爾者南夷北虜尚未蕩
平則嚴武備而敷文德寧不上厪
宵旰之憂乎雖然以堯舜之世而尚不免於
三苗猾夏則玆又何足爲
盛世累哉昔湯之造商也制事制心乃能代
夏而成允殖之功數傳而有高宗内服諸
侯外平荊楚故商道燦然復興衍而爲六
百年之商武王之造周也敬勝義勝乃能
代商而成永清之治數傳而有宣王北伐
玁狁南定蠻荊故周道燦然復興衍而爲
八百年之周我
聖上中興之盛視高宗宣王爲遠邁焉特
敬一之心運諸上惟見人文化成太和洋溢
四夷率俾蠢玆夷虜亦何足慮哉
punctuated: 聖祖偃武而復綏之以文。今聖上敷文，而且拳拳於修攘之略。蓋文武兼備，帝王之全用也；識其勢而緩急之，帝王之所以善其用也。爾者南夷北虜尚未蕩平，則嚴武備而敷文德，寧不上厪宵旰之憂乎？雖然，以堯舜之世而尚不免於三苗猾夏，則玆又何足爲盛世累哉？昔湯之造商也，制事制心，乃能代夏而成允殖之功。數傳而有高宗，内服諸侯，外平荊楚，故商道燦然復興，衍而爲六百年之商。武王之造周也，敬勝義勝，乃能代商而成永清之治。數傳而有宣王，北伐玁狁，南定蠻荊，故周道燦然復興，衍而爲八百年之周。我聖上中興之盛，視高宗、宣王爲遠邁焉。特敬一之心運諸上，惟見人文化成，太和洋溢，四夷率俾，蠢玆夷虜亦何足慮哉？
translation_en:
…the Sagely Founder laid down arms and further brought peace through civil cultivation. Now His Majesty spreads civil cultivation and also devotes earnest attention to strategies for strengthening internal government and repelling external enemies. Possessing both civil and military capacities gives an emperor the full range of means; discerning circumstances and deciding what can wait and what requires urgency enables him to employ those means well. Of late, the southern barbarians and northern raiders have yet to be completely pacified. Surely the need to strengthen military preparedness while spreading civil virtue must burden His Majesty with cares from before dawn until late at night? Yet even the age of Yao and Shun could not escape the Sanmiao bringing disorder to the central lands. How, then, could these troubles blemish an age of flourishing rule?

When Tang founded Shang, he regulated affairs and disciplined his mind, and thus was able to replace Xia and achieve truly flourishing rule. Several reigns later came Gaozong, who secured the submission of the regional lords within and pacified Jing and Chu beyond. Thus the Way of Shang rose again in splendor, extending the dynasty to a span of six hundred years. When King Wu founded Zhou, he prevailed through reverence and righteousness, and thus was able to replace Shang and establish enduring peace. Several reigns later came King Xuan, who campaigned north against the Xianyun and subdued the Man peoples of Jing in the south. Thus the Way of Zhou rose again in splendor, extending the dynasty to a span of eight hundred years.

The splendor of the restoration under our present Majesty far surpasses that of Gaozong and King Xuan. With his mind of reverent single-mindedness directing affairs from above, we shall see transformation accomplished through civil cultivation, supreme harmony overflowing, and the peoples of all four quarters obediently submitting. What cause for concern, then, could these unruly barbarians and raiders present?

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
文謨武烈於
聖祖赫然宣重光矣書曰以覲文王之耿光以
揚武王之大烈愚敢借是爲
聖上頌
第二問
張炳
同考試官教諭吳　批〔好古而不泥蓋究心于禮而得其本者〕
同考試官教諭周　批〔讀此作則古禮之不可無與諸儒纂輯之功犂然具見且言以時爲大雖三代損益不過如此可謂達禮之本矣〕
===
考試官侍讀陳　批〔足爲議禮斷案〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔窮本知變蓋達禮者〕
先王之禮有本焉有文焉本也者義也古
今之所相沿而不能以少異者也文也者
數也古今之所損益而不能以必同者也
人見古之禮日趨于密今之禮日趨于簡
則謂古禮若無用于今者不知聖人所以
punctuated:
文謨武烈，於聖祖赫然宣重光矣。《書》曰：「以覲文王之耿光，以揚武王之大烈。」愚敢借是爲聖上頌。

第二問
張炳
同考試官教諭吳批〔好古而不泥，蓋究心于禮而得其本者。〕
同考試官教諭周批〔讀此作，則古禮之不可無與諸儒纂輯之功犂然具見。且言以時爲大，雖三代損益，不過如此，可謂達禮之本矣。〕
考試官侍讀陳批〔足爲議禮斷案。〕
考試官侍讀瞿批〔窮本知變，蓋達禮者。〕

先王之禮，有本焉，有文焉。本也者，義也，古今之所相沿而不能以少異者也；文也者，數也，古今之所損益而不能以必同者也。人見古之禮日趨于密，今之禮日趨于簡，則謂古禮若無用于今者，不知聖人所以
translation_en:
…In civil counsels and martial achievements, the brilliance of the sagely ancestor has been splendidly renewed. The Book of Documents says: “To display King Wen’s radiant light and exalt King Wu’s great achievements.” I venture to borrow these words in praise of His Majesty.

Second Question
Zhang Bing

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: 〔He cherishes antiquity without being bound by it. He has surely devoted himself to ritual and grasped its foundations.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: 〔Reading this composition, one sees with perfect clarity both the indispensability of ancient rites and the achievements of the scholars who compiled them. Moreover, he says that adapting to the times is paramount. Even the modifications made under the Three Dynasties went no further than this. He may be said to understand the foundations of ritual.〕

Comment by Examiner Chen, Reader-in-waiting: 〔This suffices as an authoritative judgment in discussions of ritual.〕

Comment by Examiner Qu, Reader-in-waiting: 〔He probes the foundations and understands change. He surely comprehends ritual.〕

The rites of the former kings have foundations and outward forms. Their foundations are moral principles, transmitted from antiquity to the present without admitting the slightest alteration. Their outward forms are prescribed particulars, subject to subtraction and addition from antiquity to the present, and not necessarily remaining identical. People see that ancient rites grew increasingly elaborate, while present-day rites grow increasingly simple, and therefore claim that ancient rites seem to have no use today. They do not understand the means by which the sages…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
承天道治人情而立羣動之紀者萬世不
可易也綢繆其制度繁縟其文章皆有精
義存其間非苟以爲密也後之君子先求
禮之本于吾心至文之所在與其過而棄
之寧過而存之竝爲肄習以爲議禮之資
則其有益于人治夫豈小哉執事發策以
三禮爲問蓋有感于古禮之僅存而欲求
夫情文之衷也愚何足以知之昔歐陽子
嘗曰三代而上治出于一而禮樂達于天
===
下三代而下治出于二而禮樂徒爲虛文
夫古之所謂禮者非特宗伯所掌已也自
其辨方正位體國經野設官分職皆所以
習民于禮約之等級度數以潛消其慢易
之心故民皆曉然知禮之不可踰而凌犯
不生淫佚不作後之所謂禮者其制度已
非三代之舊然惟藏之禮官肄之太常朝
會饗祀時一陳之以爲觀美而已故雖傳
士弟子亦有不識其名物度數者况望其
punctuated: 承天道、治人情而立羣動之紀者，萬世不可易也。綢繆其制度，繁縟其文章，皆有精義存其間，非苟以爲密也。後之君子，先求禮之本于吾心，至文之所在，與其過而棄之，寧過而存之，竝爲肄習，以爲議禮之資，則其有益于人治，夫豈小哉？執事發策，以三禮爲問，蓋有感于古禮之僅存，而欲求夫情文之衷也。愚何足以知之？昔歐陽子嘗曰：「三代而上，治出于一，而禮樂達于天下；三代而下，治出于二，而禮樂徒爲虛文。」夫古之所謂禮者，非特宗伯所掌已也。自其辨方正位、體國經野、設官分職，皆所以習民于禮，約之等級度數，以潛消其慢易之心。故民皆曉然知禮之不可踰，而凌犯不生，淫佚不作。後之所謂禮者，其制度已非三代之舊，然惟藏之禮官，肄之太常，朝會饗祀，時一陳之，以爲觀美而已。故雖傳士弟子，亦有不識其名物度數者，况望其
translation_en:
…that whereby they accorded with the Way of Heaven, ordered human feelings, and established guiding principles for all human activity cannot be changed for ten thousand generations. The intricacy of their institutions and the richness of their ceremonial forms all embodied subtle principles; they were not made elaborate merely for elaboration’s sake. Gentlemen of later ages should first seek the foundation of ritual in their own hearts. As for its outward forms, rather than err by discarding them, they should err by preserving them, studying and practicing them all as resources for deliberating on ritual. Could their benefit to human governance then be slight? You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question concerning the Three Ritual Classics, presumably moved by the scant survival of ancient ritual and wishing to find the proper balance between human feelings and ceremonial forms. How could I, in my ignorance, adequately understand this?

Master Ouyang once said: “From the Three Dynasties and earlier, governance issued from a single source, and rites and music reached throughout the realm. After the Three Dynasties, governance issued from two sources, and rites and music became mere empty forms.” What the ancients called ritual was not confined to the responsibilities of the Minister of Rites. Determining directions and establishing proper positions, laying out the capital and demarcating the countryside, establishing offices and allocating duties—all served to accustom the people to ritual and restrain them through distinctions of rank and prescribed measures, imperceptibly dispelling their arrogance and disrespect. Thus the people all understood clearly that ritual boundaries must not be crossed: encroachment and transgression did not arise, nor did licentiousness and indulgence.

As for what later ages called ritual, its institutions were already unlike those of the Three Dynasties. Yet it was merely preserved by ritual officials and rehearsed in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, displayed occasionally at court assemblies, ceremonial banquets, and sacrifices, simply to furnish a pleasing spectacle. Thus even among scholars and students [?], some did not recognize its terminology, ritual objects, or prescribed measures. How much less could one hope that it would…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
達于閭巷漸于海隅共興揖讓之治乎此
論者所以有思于古禮也執事謂古之祝
史猶能知禮之數後之儒者顧有不知非
智有不逮蓋時有升降禮有廢興誠不素
講之過也今古禮之存于世者三禮而已
士所習儀禮周禮禮記者是也儀禮之獲
傳也蓋自高堂生始也后蒼明之戴氏慶
氏繹之鄭玄傳小戴之學而始爲之註是
儀禮之所以至今不泯也周禮之獲傳也
===
蓋自劉歆始也杜子春受之馬融繹之鄭
玄傳馬融之學而復爲之註是周禮之所
以至今不泯也禮記之獲傳也蓋自二戴
始也劉向所校繁多大戴刪之爲篇八十
五小戴復刪之爲篇四十六至馬融益之
以月令明堂位樂記爲四十九篇是禮記
之所以至今不泯也鄭夾漈乃曰秦火焚
書而書存漢儒窮經而經絶噫古禮之存
于今者多康成之功而可輕訾之哉惟康
punctuated:
達于閭巷，漸于海隅，共興揖讓之治乎？此論者所以有思于古禮也。執事謂古之祝史猶能知禮之數，後之儒者顧有不知，非智有不逮，蓋時有升降，禮有廢興，誠不素講之過也。

今古禮之存于世者，三禮而已，士所習《儀禮》《周禮》《禮記》者是也。《儀禮》之獲傳也，蓋自高堂生始也。后蒼明之，戴氏、慶氏繹之，鄭玄傳小戴之學，而始爲之註，是《儀禮》之所以至今不泯也。《周禮》之獲傳也，蓋自劉歆始也。杜子春受之，馬融繹之，鄭玄傳馬融之學，而復爲之註，是《周禮》之所以至今不泯也。《禮記》之獲傳也，蓋自二戴始也。劉向所校繁多，大戴刪之爲篇八十五，小戴復刪之爲篇四十六，至馬融益之以《月令》《明堂位》《樂記》，爲四十九篇，是《禮記》之所以至今不泯也。

鄭夾漈乃曰：「秦火焚書而書存，漢儒窮經而經絶。」噫！古禮之存于今者，多康成之功，而可輕訾之哉？惟康
translation_en:
…to reach the village lanes, permeate the distant coastal regions, and bring all together in establishing government marked by deference and courtesy? This is why those who discuss the matter long for the ancient rites. You observe that even the invocators and scribes of antiquity understood the prescribed details of ritual, whereas some later Confucian scholars did not. This was not because their intelligence fell short: times have their rises and declines, and rites fall into disuse and flourish again. It was indeed the fault of failing to study them regularly.

The ancient rites that survive in the world today are contained only in the Three Ritual Classics: the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili), Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), and Record of Rites (Liji), which scholars study. The transmission of the Ceremonies and Rites began with Gaotang Sheng. Hou Cang elucidated it, the Dai and Qing masters expounded it, and Zheng Xuan transmitted the learning of the Younger Dai and first supplied it with a commentary. This is how the Ceremonies and Rites has survived to the present. The transmission of the Rites of Zhou began with Liu Xin. Du Zichun received it, Ma Rong expounded it, and Zheng Xuan transmitted Ma Rong’s learning and likewise supplied it with a commentary. This is how the Rites of Zhou has survived to the present. The transmission of the Record of Rites began with the two Dai masters. The materials collated by Liu Xiang were extensive; the Elder Dai abridged them into eighty-five chapters, and the Younger Dai further abridged them into forty-six. Ma Rong then added the Monthly Ordinances, Positions in the Hall of Enlightenment, and Record of Music, making forty-nine chapters. This is how the Record of Rites has survived to the present.

Yet Zheng Jiaji said: “Qin’s fires burned the books, yet the books survived; Han scholars exhaustively studied the classics, yet the classics were lost.” Alas! Much of the survival of ancient ritual down to the present is due to Kangcheng [Zheng Xuan]. Can one lightly disparage him? Yet Kang…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
成以讖緯之書而釋經以秦漢之事而擬
三代天帝之辨緯書之荒誕也封禪之讖
秦漢之侈心也而以釋郊祀明堂之禮升
中于天之義則亦不得爲無外此所以遺
譏後世也至宋儒朱子作古禮經傳通解
則以儀禮爲經禮記爲傳如冠禮之與冠
義昏禮之與昏義各以類從而盡削夫迂
僻蔓衍之說使學者不棄經而信傳不忘
本而逐末蓋以救康成之失然非朱子一
===
人之私書也黄榦楊復相繼討論蓋實共
成之者也元儒吳澂作三禮考註則欲以
周官之全正周禮之誤且謂冬官之文未
嘗亡而實散見于五官之中使學者緣文
尋意以考之參諸經籍以證之蓋以辨考
工記之不類然非吳澂一人之私言也俞
庭椿王次點丘葵各有論著蓋有所受之
者也自今觀之誠有愈于漢儒矣然創始
者難爲力而潤色者易爲工漢之諸儒以
punctuated: 成以讖緯之書而釋經，以秦漢之事而擬三代。天帝之辨，緯書之荒誕也；封禪之讖，秦漢之侈心也。而以釋郊祀明堂之禮、升中于天之義，則亦不得爲無外，此所以遺譏後世也。至宋儒朱子作《古禮經傳通解》，則以《儀禮》爲經，《禮記》爲傳，如《冠禮》之與《冠義》、《昏禮》之與《昏義》，各以類從，而盡削夫迂僻蔓衍之說，使學者不棄經而信傳，不忘本而逐末，蓋以救康成之失。然非朱子一人之私書也，黄榦、楊復相繼討論，蓋實共成之者也。元儒吳澂作《三禮考註》，則欲以《周官》之全正《周禮》之誤，且謂冬官之文未嘗亡，而實散見于五官之中，使學者緣文尋意以考之，參諸經籍以證之，蓋以辨《考工記》之不類。然非吳澂一人之私言也，俞庭椿、王次點、丘葵各有論著，蓋有所受之者也。自今觀之，誠有愈于漢儒矣。然創始者難爲力，而潤色者易爲工，漢之諸儒以
translation_en:
…Kangcheng used books of prophecy and apocrypha to interpret the classics, and used the affairs of the Qin and Han to draw analogies with the Three Dynasties. The distinction between Heaven and the Supreme Deity belongs to the absurdities of the apocryphal writings; the prophecies concerning the feng and shan sacrifices express the extravagant ambitions of the Qin and Han. To use these to explain the rites of suburban sacrifice and the Hall of Light, and the meaning of reporting accomplishments to Heaven, cannot be considered free of extraneous elements [?]. This is why he left himself open to criticism by later generations.

When the Song scholar Master Zhu composed the Comprehensive Explanation of the Classics and Commentaries on Ancient Rites, he treated the Ceremonies and Rites as the classic and the Record of Rites as its commentary. He grouped passages by subject, pairing, for example, “Capping Rites” with “The Meaning of Capping,” and “Marriage Rites” with “The Meaning of Marriage.” He removed all strained, eccentric, and rambling explanations, so that students would neither abandon the classic in favor of its commentary nor forget the root in pursuit of the branches. His purpose was to remedy Kangcheng’s errors. Yet this was not a book produced by Master Zhu alone: Huang Gan and Yang Fu successively examined and discussed it, and in fact shared in bringing it to completion.

When the Yuan scholar Wu Cheng composed the Critical Annotations on the Three Ritual Classics, he sought to correct errors in the Rites of Zhou by restoring the completeness of the Offices of Zhou. He further maintained that the text concerning the Winter Offices had never been lost, but was actually scattered among the other five offices. He encouraged students to follow the wording in search of its meaning, examine it, and compare it with the other classics to substantiate their findings. His purpose was to distinguish the Record of Artificers as a text of a different kind. Yet this was not an argument advanced by Wu Cheng alone: Yu Tingchun, Wang Cidian, and Qiu Kui each wrote discussions of the matter, and his views had sources from which they were derived.

Viewed from the present, these scholars certainly surpassed the Han scholars in some respects. Yet those who initiate an undertaking face difficulties in carrying it out, while those who refine it can more easily achieve excellence. The scholars of the Han, with …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
籍去經焚之餘而先後肆習使後世獲見
先王之遺文後儒得有所據以考訂焉則
其功亦多矣惡可以夾漈之言而少之哉
昔王通氏之續經朱子嘗病其僭今通解
之作所編邦國王朝禮多取周禮禮記所
載天子之禮以備儀禮之闕非誠若王通
氏之擬經也特曰禮之義疏云耳漢時有
古禮經出于魯淹中漢儒無能傳之者班
固志藝文獨深取之謂多天子諸侯卿大
===
夫之制雖不能備猶愈倉等推士禮而致
于天子自今觀之士一也天子之士與諸
侯之士不同上大夫與下大夫不同等而
上之信有可推者然十七篇非皆士禮也
冠昏喪祭士禮也鄉飲射朝聘燕射朝聘
非士禮也無待于推也孟堅之意蓋慮儀
禮之未備而幸互見于古經當並肆而存
之也今淹中所出已不可考而周禮禮記
所載有明及于天子之制不待于推而致
punctuated:
籍去經焚之餘，而先後肆習，使後世獲見先王之遺文，後儒得有所據以考訂焉，則其功亦多矣。惡可以夾漈之言而少之哉？
昔王通氏之續經，朱子嘗病其僭。今《通解》之作，所編邦國王朝禮，多取《周禮》《禮記》所載天子之禮，以備《儀禮》之闕，非誠若王通氏之擬經也，特曰禮之義疏云耳。漢時有古《禮經》出于魯淹中，漢儒無能傳之者。班固志藝文，獨深取之，謂多天子諸侯卿大夫之制，雖不能備，猶愈倉等推士禮而致于天子。自今觀之，士一也，天子之士與諸侯之士不同，上大夫與下大夫不同，等而上之，信有可推者。然十七篇非皆士禮也。冠昏喪祭，士禮也；鄉飲射朝聘燕射，朝聘非士禮也，無待于推也。孟堅之意，蓋慮《儀禮》之未備，而幸互見于古經，當並肆而存之也。今淹中所出已不可考，而《周禮》《禮記》所載，有明及于天子之制，不待于推而致
translation_en:
…working with the remnants left after the removal of books and the burning of the classics [?], they devoted themselves, generation after generation, to study. They enabled later ages to see the surviving writings of the former kings and gave later scholars a basis for examination and correction. Their contribution was therefore considerable. How could one belittle them on the strength of Jiaji’s words?
Master Zhu once criticized Wang Tong’s continuation of the classics as presumptuous. But in compiling the Comprehensive Explanation (Tongjie), the sections on the rites of the regional states and the royal court draw extensively on the Son of Heaven’s rites recorded in the Rites of Zhou and the Record of Rites, supplementing what is missing from the Ceremonies and Rites. This is not truly comparable to Wang Tong’s imitation of the classics; it is merely an explanatory commentary on ritual.
During the Han, an ancient Classic of Rites emerged at Yanzhong in Lu, but none of the Han scholars could transmit it. Ban Gu, in his bibliographical treatise, alone esteemed it highly. He said that it contained many institutions concerning the Son of Heaven, regional lords, ministers, and grand masters. Though incomplete, it was still better than Cang and the others extrapolating from the rites of service gentlemen to apply them to the Son of Heaven. Viewed from the present, although service gentlemen share a single designation, those serving the Son of Heaven differ from those serving regional lords; senior grand masters differ from junior grand masters. Ascending through the ranks, there are indeed matters that can be inferred by extension. Yet the seventeen chapters are not all rites for service gentlemen. Capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice are rites for service gentlemen. Village drinking, archery, court audiences, diplomatic visits, banquets, and archery—court audiences and diplomatic visits are not rites for service gentlemen [?]; there is no need to infer them by extension.
Mengjian [Ban Gu] presumably feared that the Ceremonies and Rites was incomplete and was glad that complementary material appeared in the ancient classic: both should be studied and preserved together. Now the text that emerged at Yanzhong can no longer be examined, whereas the Rites of Zhou and the Record of Rites contain institutions expressly pertaining to the Son of Heaven, requiring no extrapolation to apply them…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之者以類編輯以便觀覽以備天子議禮
之資則固無嫌于僭踰者孟堅在漢不得
爲純儒猶惓惓以古禮經爲意可以吾儒
而孟堅之不如哉此朱子之勤惓纂輯復
付之黃楊二子以畢其志者也后之議禮
者吾惑焉不以儀禮爲殘缺不可考之書
則以周禮爲瀆亂不經之書而疑周禮者
爲尤甚噫吾方憫古禮之幾泯于天下而
僅見于三禮之存也猶幸古禮之未泯于
===
天下而時見于三禮之存也世世之好議者
何言之易也鄭衛迭奏而僅聞韶濩之音
瓦缶竝陳而忽覩敦彝之器見者以非今
所尚必欲掊擊而棄之亦過矣昔韓退之
嘗苦儀禮難讀然又以文武周公之制幸
在于是而覩爲註釋且恨不得揖讓進退
其間則退之亦知其可以正人心而厚風
俗也唐太宗嘗嘆周禮眞聖人作後雖不
行然以世業授民以府衛治兵則亦周禮
punctuated:
之者，以類編輯，以便觀覽，以備天子議禮之資，則固無嫌于僭踰者。孟堅在漢，不得爲純儒，猶惓惓以古禮經爲意，可以吾儒而孟堅之不如哉？此朱子之勤惓纂輯，復付之黃楊二子以畢其志者也。
后之議禮者，吾惑焉：不以儀禮爲殘缺不可考之書，則以周禮爲瀆亂不經之書，而疑周禮者爲尤甚。噫！吾方憫古禮之幾泯于天下，而僅見于三禮之存也，猶幸古禮之未泯于天下，而時見于三禮之存也。世世之好議者，何言之易也！鄭衛迭奏，而僅聞韶濩之音；瓦缶竝陳，而忽覩敦彝之器。見者以非今所尚，必欲掊擊而棄之，亦過矣！
昔韓退之嘗苦儀禮難讀，然又以文武周公之制幸在于是，而覩爲註釋，且恨不得揖讓進退其間，則退之亦知其可以正人心而厚風俗也。唐太宗嘗嘆周禮眞聖人作，後雖不行，然以世業授民，以府衛治兵，則亦周禮
translation_en:
…such provisions, compiled by category to facilitate consultation and furnish materials for the Son of Heaven’s deliberations on ritual, would surely carry no suspicion of overstepping one’s station. Mengjian, who lived under the Han, cannot be counted a wholly orthodox Confucian scholar, yet he remained deeply concerned with the ancient ritual classics. Can we Confucian scholars allow ourselves to fall short of Mengjian? This is why Master Zhu devoted such care to compiling them and then entrusted the work to the two scholars Huang and Yang to fulfill his purpose.
I am perplexed by later commentators on ritual: they either regard the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) as a fragmentary book that cannot be reliably investigated, or regard the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) as a confused and disorderly book lacking canonical authority. Their doubts about the Rites of Zhou are especially severe. Alas! I lament that ancient ritual has almost vanished from the world and can scarcely be found except in the surviving Three Ritual Classics; yet I am thankful that it has not vanished altogether and can still be encountered from time to time in those surviving works. How readily those fond of disputation in every generation pronounce their judgments! While the music of Zheng and Wei plays in succession, one barely hears the strains of the Shao and Hu; amid an array of earthenware jars, one suddenly catches sight of venerable ritual vessels. For observers to insist on smashing and discarding these simply because they are not currently esteemed is surely excessive!
Han Tuizhi once found the Ceremonies and Rites difficult to read. Yet, considering it fortunate that the institutions of Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou survived therein, he undertook to annotate it [?]. He also regretted that he could not himself perform its bows, deferential gestures, advances, and withdrawals. Thus Tuizhi too understood that it could rectify people’s hearts and enrich their customs. Emperor Taizong of the Tang once exclaimed that the Rites of Zhou was truly the work of a sage. Although he did not subsequently put it into practice, his allocation of hereditary livelihoods to the people and his administration of troops through military prefectures and guards likewise reflected the Rites of Zhou…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之遺意太宗亦知其足以經邦國而治萬
民也昔人有言周禮一書不徒彌亮天地
和洽神人而監詛譏伐所以待衰世者無
不備不徒檢柅君身防絶禍患而米鹽絲
枲所以任賤役者無不及則惡在其爲瀆
亂而可廢也其言古禮也粗在應對進退
之間精在道德性命之要始于童幼之習
而終于聖人之歸則惡在其爲殘闕而可
棄也且儀禮誠不備今以其殘闕而并廢
===
之則先王之彝章典則必盡亡滅而後可
也自秦不師古禮法蕩棄更漢世而箕踞
誶語之習猶多秦風此賈誼董仲舒所爲
惓惓于更化也欲更化善治則古禮之復
其要也是尚可以輕議而棄之乎後之君
子疑周禮之煩瑣而難行者若林孝存氏
何休氏蘇潁濱氏胡五峯氏皆疑其非聖
人之書惟馬端臨氏之言差得其中亦謂
古今異宜而難行大意謂自周以前封建
punctuated:
之遺意。太宗亦知其足以經邦國而治萬民也。昔人有言：「周禮一書，不徒彌亮天地、和洽神人，而監詛譏伐，所以待衰世者無不備；不徒檢柅君身、防絶禍患，而米鹽絲枲，所以任賤役者無不及。」則惡在其爲瀆亂而可廢也？其言古禮也，粗在應對進退之間，精在道德性命之要，始于童幼之習，而終于聖人之歸，則惡在其爲殘闕而可棄也？且儀禮誠不備，今以其殘闕而并廢之，則先王之彝章典則必盡亡滅而後可也。
自秦不師古，禮法蕩棄，更漢世而箕踞誶語之習猶多秦風，此賈誼、董仲舒所爲惓惓于更化也。欲更化善治，則古禮之復其要也，是尚可以輕議而棄之乎？後之君子疑周禮之煩瑣而難行者，若林孝存氏、何休氏、蘇潁濱氏、胡五峯氏，皆疑其非聖人之書。惟馬端臨氏之言差得其中，亦謂古今異宜而難行。大意謂自周以前，封建
translation_en:
…a surviving intention of that work. Taizong, too, understood that it was sufficient for ordering the states and governing the myriad people. Someone in former times said: “The Rites of Zhou does more than assist Heaven and Earth [?] and bring spirits and people into harmony: in its provisions for oversight, imprecations, scrutiny, and punitive expeditions, it supplies everything needed to deal with an age of decline. It does more than restrain the ruler’s person and forestall calamities: in its provisions concerning grain, salt, silk, and hemp, it encompasses everything involved in assigning humble services.” How, then, can it be considered confused and disorderly, and fit to be abolished? In its exposition of ancient ritual, the elementary aspects concern responding to others and advancing and withdrawing; the refined aspects concern the essentials of the Way, virtue, human nature, and destiny. It begins with childhood practice and culminates in the attainment of sagehood. How, then, can it be considered fragmentary and fit to be discarded? Moreover, the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) is indeed incomplete. But if we now abolish it altogether because of its fragmentary state, must the former kings’ enduring institutions and canonical standards all be utterly destroyed before we are satisfied?
From the Qin onward, antiquity was no longer taken as a model, and ritual and law were swept aside. Even into the Han, habits such as sitting with legs splayed and speaking abusively retained much of the Qin manner. This is why Jia Yi and Dong Zhongshu were so earnestly concerned with reforming moral influence. To achieve such reform and good government, restoring ancient ritual is essential. Can it still be lightly criticized and discarded? Among later scholars who doubted the practicality of the Rites of Zhou because of its troublesome detail, Lin Xiaocun, He Xiu, Su Yingbin, and Hu Wufeng all doubted that it was a sage’s book. Only Ma Duanlin’s remarks came somewhat close to a balanced judgment; yet he, too, said that differing circumstances in antiquity and the present made it difficult to put into practice. His general contention was that, in the Zhou and earlier, the system of enfeoffment…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
制行人皆私上子人故教養之法貴密而
人不以爲擾自秦以後郡縣制行守令遷
代不常故教養之法貴簡而人更以爲適
然則古禮果無用于今而諸儒之纂輯亦
好古之過哉蓋禮有義有數而以時爲大
故先王之禮有得與時變革者禮之數也
有不得與時變革者禮之義也數之所在
雖古之帝王不相沿襲義之所在則遞相
守之以爲經不可易也如周之教民先德
===
行而後文藝故士多賢能周之養民授之
產而薄其征故人多富庶此其精義寓于
良法之中豈以古今異時而不可用哉好
古君子誠師其意而用之則六官之遺文
十七篇之遺制皆後世修政立教之資在
善擇而用之耳昔孔子嘗曰虞夏之文不
勝其質殷周之質不勝其文又曰虞夏之
道寡怨于民殷周之道不勝其弊則孔子
之心固欲損周之文以從虞夏之質矣朱
punctuated: 制行，人皆私上子人，故教養之法貴密，而人不以爲擾。自秦以後，郡縣制行，守令遷代不常，故教養之法貴簡，而人更以爲適。然則古禮果無用于今，而諸儒之纂輯亦好古之過哉？蓋禮有義有數，而以時爲大。故先王之禮，有得與時變革者，禮之數也；有不得與時變革者，禮之義也。數之所在，雖古之帝王不相沿襲；義之所在，則遞相守之，以爲經，不可易也。如周之教民，先德行而後文藝，故士多賢能；周之養民，授之產而薄其征，故人多富庶。此其精義寓于良法之中，豈以古今異時而不可用哉？好古君子誠師其意而用之，則六官之遺文、十七篇之遺制，皆後世修政立教之資，在善擇而用之耳。昔孔子嘗曰：「虞夏之文不勝其質，殷周之質不勝其文。」又曰：「虞夏之道，寡怨于民；殷周之道，不勝其弊。」則孔子之心，固欲損周之文，以從虞夏之質矣。朱
translation_en:
…the system was in force, people regarded their superiors as their own, and [rulers] treated the people as their children [?]. Thus, methods of educating and nurturing the people prized close attention to detail, yet the people did not find them intrusive. After the Qin, the system of commanderies and counties came into force, and prefects and magistrates were transferred and replaced at irregular intervals. Thus, methods of educating and nurturing the people prized simplicity, which the people found more congenial. Does this mean that ancient ritual truly has no use today, and that the compilations of the various scholars are merely the excesses of their love of antiquity?

Ritual has both underlying principles and prescribed forms, but responsiveness to the times is paramount. Thus, those aspects of the former kings’ ritual that may change with the times are its prescribed forms; those that may not change with the times are its underlying principles. In matters of prescribed forms, even the emperors and kings of antiquity did not simply follow their predecessors. In matters of principle, however, they upheld these in succession as unalterable norms. For example, in educating the people, the Zhou put virtuous conduct before literary accomplishments, and thus its gentlemen were largely worthy and capable. In nurturing the people, the Zhou granted them productive property and kept levies light, and thus the people were largely prosperous. Here, essential principles were embodied in sound institutions. How could these be unusable merely because ancient and modern times differ? If gentlemen who love antiquity truly take its intent as their guide and put it into practice, then the surviving writings on the Six Offices and the institutions preserved in the Seventeen Chapters will all furnish resources for later ages to reform government and establish instruction. It is simply a matter of choosing well and putting them to use.

Confucius once said: “The refinement of Yu and Xia did not surpass their substance; the substance of Yin and Zhou did not surpass their refinement.” He also said: “The ways of Yu and Xia occasioned little resentment among the people; the ways of Yin and Zhou could not overcome their attendant abuses.” Confucius’s intention, then, was surely to reduce Zhou refinement and follow the substance of Yu and Xia. Zhu…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
子之論祭禮亦謂後世有作必不一一如古
禮之繁則朱子之好古亦豈徒愼守其數
不敢損益以持王公如荀卿氏之言哉然
則學禮者當柰何亦曰自吾心始吾心之
恭儉莊敬爲禮之所自出猶之規矩準繩
爲方圓平直之所自出也先王之遺文蓋
亦方圓平直之迹非所以爲方圓平直也
故學禮者始于習其數終于達其義以心
會義則先王之遺文竝存之以詔後可也
===
損益之以趨時可也雖先王未之有以義
起焉亦可也此之謂得禮之本而文有不
拘者也此非愚之言也記曰忠信之人可
以學禮宋儒張子亦曰禮儀三百威儀三
千無一事而非仁也皆言禮之本于心也
若無得于心而徒曰數易陳也義難知也
數不必習也則吾恐其如晉之縱淸談而
蔑禮教是禮之賊也不知執事以爲何如
第三問
punctuated:
子之論祭禮，亦謂後世有作，必不一一如古禮之繁。則朱子之好古，亦豈徒愼守其數，不敢損益以持王公，如荀卿氏之言哉？然則學禮者當柰何？亦曰：自吾心始。吾心之恭儉莊敬，爲禮之所自出，猶之規矩準繩爲方圓平直之所自出也。先王之遺文，蓋亦方圓平直之迹，非所以爲方圓平直也。故學禮者始于習其數，終于達其義。以心會義，則先王之遺文竝存之以詔後可也，損益之以趨時可也，雖先王未之有，以義起焉亦可也。此之謂得禮之本而文有不拘者也。此非愚之言也。記曰：「忠信之人，可以學禮。」宋儒張子亦曰：「禮儀三百，威儀三千，無一事而非仁也。」皆言禮之本于心也。若無得于心，而徒曰：「數易陳也，義難知也，數不必習也。」則吾恐其如晉之縱淸談而蔑禮教，是禮之賊也。不知執事以爲何如？

第三問
translation_en:
…Master Zhu, in discussing sacrificial rites, likewise said that if anyone in later ages were to establish rites anew, they would certainly not reproduce every complexity of ancient ritual. Could Master Zhu’s love of antiquity, then, have meant merely guarding its prescribed forms scrupulously, daring neither to subtract nor to add, and using them to constrain kings and dukes, as Xun Qing said?

How, then, should those who study ritual proceed? The answer is simply: begin with one’s own heart. The humility, restraint, gravity, and reverence of our hearts are the source from which ritual issues, just as compasses, squares, levels, and marking lines are the source of roundness, squareness, levelness, and straightness. The forms bequeathed by the former kings are likewise the traces of these shapes and alignments, rather than the means by which they are produced. Thus, studying ritual begins with learning its prescribed forms and culminates in comprehending their underlying meaning. If one apprehends that meaning in one’s heart, one may preserve all the forms bequeathed by the former kings to instruct posterity; one may subtract from or add to them to suit the times; and one may even institute practices unknown to the former kings, provided they arise from what is right. This is what it means to grasp the root of ritual without being bound by every outward form.

These are not merely my own humble words. The Book of Rites says: “A person of loyalty and trustworthiness can learn ritual.” The Song Confucian Master Zhang also said: “Of the three hundred ceremonial rules and three thousand rules of deportment, not one is other than humaneness.” Both speak of ritual as rooted in the heart. But if someone has gained no understanding in the heart and merely says, “The prescribed forms are easy to set out, while their meaning is difficult to know; there is no need to learn the forms,” I fear that this would resemble the indulgence in pure conversation during the Jin dynasty, which treated ritual teaching with contempt. This is to be a destroyer of ritual. I wonder what you, sir, think of this?

Third Question

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
張璽
同考試官教諭魏　批〔正統之說觀之春秋已有定論子能以折羣疑且知朱子書法之嚴〕
已具引而不發之意不使方氏蒙好異之疑讀
之灑然矣
同考試官教諭邵　批〔評隲眾論而折以春〕
秋蓋深於史學者
考試官侍讀陳　批〔明切〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔精確〕
===
明於春秋之義而後可與言正統明于正
統之義而後可與言史法夫事有常變故
史法有正例有變例正例者所以經夫事
之常也變例者所以揆夫事之變也事莫
大于國統之離合絕續而正不正恒存乎
其間如不明乎春秋之義徒以其一天下
而謂之正統則得之正而常者謂之統之
正可也得之不正而變者謂之統之正不
可也雖其事之核足以信天下亦何以懲
punctuated:
張璽

同考試官教諭魏批〔正統之說，觀之春秋，已有定論。子能以折羣疑，且知朱子書法之嚴〕，已具引而不發之意，不使方氏蒙好異之疑，讀之灑然矣。

同考試官教諭邵批〔評隲眾論，而折以春〕秋，蓋深於史學者。

考試官侍讀陳批〔明切〕。

考試官侍讀瞿批〔精確〕。

明於春秋之義，而後可與言正統；明于正統之義，而後可與言史法。夫事有常變，故史法有正例，有變例。正例者，所以經夫事之常也；變例者，所以揆夫事之變也。事莫大于國統之離合絕續，而正不正恒存乎其間。如不明乎春秋之義，徒以其一天下而謂之正統，則得之正而常者，謂之統之正可也；得之不正而變者，謂之統之正不可也。雖其事之核足以信天下，亦何以懲
translation_en:
Zhang Xi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor: “On the question of legitimate dynastic succession, the Spring and Autumn Annals already provides a settled judgment. You can use it to resolve the many doubts, and you also understand the rigor of Master Zhu’s manner of writing history. Your answer already conveys the intention of drawing the bow without releasing the arrow—suggesting a conclusion without stating it outright—and does not leave Master Fang under suspicion of seeking novelty. Reading it is refreshing.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor: “He evaluates the various arguments and adjudicates them by reference to the Spring and Autumn Annals. Here is someone deeply versed in historical scholarship.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Reader-in-Waiting: “Clear and incisive.”

Comment by Examiner Qu, Reader-in-Waiting: “Precise and accurate.”

Only with someone who understands the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals can one discuss legitimate dynastic succession; only with someone who understands the principles of legitimate dynastic succession can one discuss the methods of historical writing. Events have both regular and exceptional forms; hence historical writing has both regular and exceptional rules. Regular rules govern events in their ordinary course; exceptional rules assess events that depart from that course. No events are more momentous than the division and unification, interruption and continuation of dynastic rule, and the distinction between legitimacy and illegitimacy is always present within them. If, without understanding the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals, one calls a dynasty legitimate merely because it unified all under Heaven, then where rule was acquired legitimately and in accordance with the regular course, it is permissible to call that succession legitimate; but where rule was acquired illegitimately and through exceptional circumstances, it is impermissible to call that succession legitimate. Even if the factual accuracy of such a history suffices to win the trust of all under Heaven, how could it serve to deter…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
嗟乎世衰哉執事以正統之論入人殊
而求折衷之論此非末學所及也雖然亦
嘗聞之矣論正統于三代之上則其論易
定論正統于三代之下則其論難一三代
而上唐虞之受禪天下之大公也湯武之
放伐天下之大義也其爲正統雖三尺童
子能決之以其爲天下萬世之所共予也
三代而下欺孤寡而奪之位猶假名於受
禪奮詐力而篡其國猶假名于放伐其爲
===
正統雖宗工鉅儒猶難之以其僞定一時
而非天下萬世之所共予也如執事所稱
諸說之同異是也然則孰從而定之語曰
衆言淆亂折諸聖請折之春秋則其得失
可知也春秋之時周室微諸侯橫周天子
特寄空名于六合之上當時吳楚皆已稱
王觀其諸侯威震上國如以其稱王而王
之則何以爲訓故春秋于周王必稱天王
于歲首必書春王正月于吳楚則稱人稱
punctuated: 嗟乎，世衰哉！執事以正統之論入人殊，而求折衷之論，此非末學所及也。雖然，亦嘗聞之矣。論正統于三代之上，則其論易定；論正統于三代之下，則其論難一。三代而上，唐虞之受禪，天下之大公也；湯武之放伐，天下之大義也。其爲正統，雖三尺童子能決之，以其爲天下萬世之所共予也。三代而下，欺孤寡而奪之位，猶假名於受禪；奮詐力而篡其國，猶假名于放伐。其爲正統，雖宗工鉅儒猶難之，以其僞定一時，而非天下萬世之所共予也。如執事所稱諸說之同異是也。然則孰從而定之？語曰：「衆言淆亂，折諸聖。」請折之《春秋》，則其得失可知也。《春秋》之時，周室微，諸侯橫，周天子特寄空名于六合之上。當時吳楚皆已稱王，觀其諸侯威震上國，如以其稱王而王之，則何以爲訓？故《春秋》于周王必稱天王，于歲首必書「春王正月」，于吳楚則稱人、稱
translation_en:
Alas, how the age has declined! You, sir, observing that opinions on legitimate dynastic succession differ from person to person [?], seek a judgment that reconciles them. This lies beyond the reach of a scholar of such slight learning as myself. Nevertheless, I have heard something of the matter. When discussing legitimate succession in the Three Dynasties and earlier, a judgment is readily settled; when discussing it after the Three Dynasties, agreement is difficult. In the Three Dynasties and earlier, the acceptance of the throne by abdication under Tang and Yu exemplified the supreme impartiality of All under Heaven; the banishment and punitive conquest undertaken by Tang and Wu exemplified its supreme righteousness. Even a child three feet tall could determine that theirs was legitimate succession, because it received the common assent of All under Heaven for all ages. After the Three Dynasties, men deceived orphans and widows and seized their thrones, yet borrowed the name of accepting an abdication; they deployed deceit and force to usurp states, yet borrowed the name of banishment and punitive conquest. Even eminent ministers and great Confucian scholars find it difficult to judge whether such succession was legitimate, because its counterfeit claims were established for a time, rather than receiving the common assent of All under Heaven for all ages. Such are the agreements and disagreements among the various accounts you have cited, sir.

What, then, should we follow in settling the matter? As the saying goes, “When the many opinions are confused, adjudicate them by reference to the sage.” Let us adjudicate them by the Spring and Autumn Annals, and their merits and faults can be known. In the time of the Spring and Autumn Annals, the royal house of Zhou was weak, and the feudal lords acted without restraint. The Zhou Son of Heaven retained only an empty title over the realm. At that time, Wu and Chu had both already assumed the title of king. Consider how the might of their lords shook the central states: if they were recognized as kings simply because they called themselves kings, what instruction could this provide? Thus, the Spring and Autumn Annals invariably calls the king of Zhou “Heavenly King,” and at the beginning of the year invariably records “Spring, the king’s first month.” As for Wu and Chu, it calls them “men,” or calls them …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
子甚或擧其號以從夷狄之例春秋非故
沒吳楚之實而虛加周天子以正統之名
也凡以立勸戒爲世道計也正之所在卽
其勢之微且弱如東周而君子之所予者
恒在焉則人知正之可貴而有勸也
不正之所在卽其勢之强且大如吳楚而
君子之所奪者恒在焉則人知不正之可
賤而有懲也此春秋之義例非聖人
不惟修觀春秋則正統之論可定也歐陽
===
子之言曰正者所以正天下之不正也統
者所以合天下之不一也由不正與不一
而後正統之論作此論之正也又曰居天
下之正合天下于一斯正統矣堯舜周秦
漢唐是也始雖不得其正終合天下于一
以其合天下而其君之斯亦正統矣晉隋
是也此論之不得已者也夫以晉隋之得
國非正而復予之則正不正之說窮有以
啓章子霸統之說而無以折之于是蘇子
punctuated:
子，甚或擧其號，以從夷狄之例。《春秋》非故沒吳楚之實，而虛加周天子以正統之名也，凡以立勸戒，爲世道計也。正之所在，卽其勢之微且弱如東周，而君子之所予者恒在焉，則人知正之可貴而有勸也。不正之所在，卽其勢之强且大如吳楚，而君子之所奪者恒在焉，則人知不正之可賤而有懲也。此《春秋》之義例，非聖人不惟修。觀《春秋》，則正統之論可定也。
歐陽子之言曰：「正者，所以正天下之不正也；統者，所以合天下之不一也。由不正與不一，而後正統之論作。」此論之正也。又曰：「居天下之正，合天下于一，斯正統矣。堯舜周秦漢唐是也。始雖不得其正，終合天下于一，以其合天下而其君之，斯亦正統矣。晉隋是也。」此論之不得已者也。夫以晉隋之得國非正而復予之，則正不正之說窮，有以啓章子霸統之說，而無以折之。于是蘇子
translation_en:
…“viscount,” or even simply records their designation, following the conventions used for the Yi and Di peoples. The Spring and Autumn Annals does not deliberately suppress the actual standing of Wu and Chu and groundlessly confer the name of legitimate succession upon the Zhou Son of Heaven. Its purpose throughout is to establish encouragements and admonitions for the sake of moral order in the world. Wherever legitimacy resides, even if its power is as slight and weak as that of Eastern Zhou, the gentleman consistently grants it recognition. People thereby understand that legitimacy is worthy of esteem and are encouraged. Wherever legitimacy is absent, even if its power is as strong and great as that of Wu and Chu, the gentleman consistently withholds recognition. People thereby understand that illegitimacy is contemptible and are admonished. These are the principles and conventions of the Spring and Autumn Annals, which none but a sage could establish [?]. By examining the Spring and Autumn Annals, one can settle the question of legitimate succession.
Master Ouyang said: “Legitimacy is that by which what is illegitimate in All-under-Heaven is rectified; succession is that by which what is divided in All-under-Heaven is united. It is only because illegitimacy and disunity exist that discussion of legitimate succession arises.” This is the correct formulation of the argument. He also said: “To occupy the legitimate position in All-under-Heaven and unite All-under-Heaven as one constitutes legitimate succession. Yao, Shun, Zhou, Qin, Han, and Tang exemplify this. Even if legitimacy was not secured at the outset, if All-under-Heaven was ultimately united as one, then, because they united All-under-Heaven and ruled it [?], this too constitutes legitimate succession. Jin and Sui exemplify this.” This formulation is a concession made out of necessity. Now, if Jin and Sui acquired their realms illegitimately yet are nevertheless accorded recognition, the distinction between legitimacy and illegitimacy reaches an impasse. This opens the way for Master Zhang’s theory of hegemonic succession, while leaving no means of refuting it. Thereupon Master Su…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
乃爲之說曰正統云者特有天下之名云
爾賢不肖之辨非所以施之也輕以與
人貴而重以與人賢則雖晉隋與之正統
不爲嫌而堯舜三代之得國亦不嫌于美
惡之同辭嗚呼使正統之名而可輕予則
春秋之于吳楚將進而王之矣且歐陽子
之論正統猶重與之名故于秦則進之于
梁則斥之若如蘇子之說則凡强大而得
志于當時如曹魏如元魏如朱梁皆將進
===
之矣是何見與歐陽子異哉夫蘇子之論
無復評矣司馬溫公作資治通鑑朱子因
之作通鑑綱目其立例間有異同非朱子
之求異也綱目爲萬世修義所未安固不
嫌于少異也溫公帝曹魏而寇蜀漢朱子
則以昭烈紹漢統以昭烈帝室之胄曹魏
固不得而加之也溫公帝朱梁而寇河東
朱子則正河東爲敵國以河東亦角立之
維朱梁固不得而臣之也且秦嘗一天下
punctuated:
乃爲之說曰：「正統云者，特有天下之名云爾，賢不肖之辨非所以施之也。輕以與人貴，而重以與人賢，則雖晉隋與之正統不爲嫌，而堯舜三代之得國亦不嫌于美惡之同辭。」嗚呼！使正統之名而可輕予，則春秋之于吳楚，將進而王之矣。且歐陽子之論正統，猶重與之名，故于秦則進之，于梁則斥之。若如蘇子之說，則凡强大而得志于當時，如曹魏，如元魏，如朱梁，皆將進之矣。是何見與歐陽子異哉？夫蘇子之論，無復評矣。
司馬溫公作《資治通鑑》，朱子因之作《通鑑綱目》，其立例間有異同，非朱子之求異也。《綱目》爲萬世修，義所未安，固不嫌于少異也。溫公帝曹魏而寇蜀漢，朱子則以昭烈紹漢統，以昭烈帝室之胄，曹魏固不得而加之也。溫公帝朱梁而寇河東，朱子則正河東爲敵國，以河東亦角立之維，朱梁固不得而臣之也。且秦嘗一天下
translation_en:
…Master Su then advanced this explanation: “What is called the legitimate succession is merely the designation for possessing all under Heaven; distinctions between the worthy and the unworthy do not apply to it. If we readily accord people exalted status but are cautious about according them worthiness, then there is no objection to granting even Jin and Sui a place in the legitimate succession. Nor is there any objection to using the same term for the good and the bad when speaking of how Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties acquired the realm.” Alas! If the designation of legitimate succession could be bestowed lightly, then the Spring and Autumn Annals would have elevated Wu and Chu and recognized their rulers as kings. Moreover, in discussing the legitimate succession, Master Ouyang still attached weight to granting this designation: thus he admitted Qin but rejected Liang. If we followed Master Su’s explanation, all those who were powerful and achieved their ambitions in their own times—such as Cao Wei, Yuan Wei, and Zhu Liang—would be admitted. What view is this, so different from Master Ouyang’s? As for Master Su’s argument, it merits no further discussion.
Sima Guang, Duke of Wen, composed the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, and Master Zhu drew upon it to compose the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror. Their editorial principles sometimes agree and sometimes differ; this was not because Master Zhu sought to be different. The Outline and Details was compiled for all generations, and wherever its principles would otherwise have been unsatisfactory, there was certainly no objection to a slight departure. The Duke of Wen treated Cao Wei’s rulers as emperors and Shu Han as rebels. Master Zhu, however, held that Zhaolie continued the Han succession: since Zhaolie was a descendant of the imperial house, Cao Wei assuredly could not be placed above him. The Duke of Wen treated Zhu Liang’s rulers as emperors and Hedong as rebels. Master Zhu, however, correctly classified Hedong as a state of equal standing: Hedong was also an independently established rival power [?], and Zhu Liang assuredly could not treat it as a subject. Moreover, Qin once unified all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
矣晉隋亦嘗一天下矣曹魏未梁未嘗一
天下則帝魏者魏之臣子可矣固不可強
天下而帝魏也帝梁者亦梁之臣子可矣
固不可強天下而帝梁也且當時人心猶
不肯帝魏帝梁何后世乃忽于魯仲連之
義而輕帝之也哉此朱子之立義雖少異
于溫公而不以為嫌也獨其以周秦漢晉
隋唐為正統未一天下者為無統蓋本歐
陽子之說近世方氏乃謂天下有正統有
===
變統正統之說立而後人君之位尊變統
之名立而後正統之義明如方氏之說其
未合天下于一者不論也即合天下于一
而得之不以正皆當歸之變統而不得與
正統竝噫愽雅如歐陽子亦無以尚矣精
義如朱子亦無可議矣而方氏猶置辨不
已者豈好異哉方氏固憂天下之變將日
甚思嚴其法以懲之也且歐陽子言正統
之絕續其可疑者有三一曰周秦之際二
punctuated: 矣。晉隋亦嘗一天下矣，曹魏未梁未嘗一天下，則帝魏者，魏之臣子可矣，固不可強天下而帝魏也；帝梁者，亦梁之臣子可矣，固不可強天下而帝梁也。且當時人心猶不肯帝魏、帝梁，何后世乃忽于魯仲連之義而輕帝之也哉？此朱子之立義，雖少異于溫公，而不以為嫌也。獨其以周秦漢晉隋唐為正統，未一天下者為無統，蓋本歐陽子之說。近世方氏乃謂天下有正統、有變統。正統之說立，而後人君之位尊；變統之名立，而後正統之義明。如方氏之說，其未合天下于一者不論也，即合天下于一，而得之不以正，皆當歸之變統，而不得與正統竝。噫！愽雅如歐陽子，亦無以尚矣；精義如朱子，亦無可議矣。而方氏猶置辨不已者，豈好異哉？方氏固憂天下之變將日甚，思嚴其法以懲之也。且歐陽子言正統之絕續，其可疑者有三：一曰周秦之際，二
translation_en: …had indeed done so. Jin and Sui, too, once unified all under Heaven. Cao Wei and [Zhu] Liang [?] never unified all under Heaven. Thus, it was permissible for Wei’s own subjects to recognize its ruler as emperor, but certainly impermissible to compel all under Heaven to do so. Likewise, it was permissible for Liang’s own subjects to recognize its ruler as emperor, but certainly impermissible to compel all under Heaven to do so. Moreover, even people at the time were unwilling to recognize the rulers of Wei and Liang as emperors. Why, then, should later generations disregard the righteous principle upheld by Lu Zhonglian and lightly accord them imperial status? This is why Master Zhu did not regard it as objectionable that the principles he established differed somewhat from those of the Duke of Wen, Sima Guang. Yet his classification of Zhou, Qin, Han, Jin, Sui, and Tang as the legitimate succession, and of periods when all under Heaven was not unified as having no succession, was evidently based on Master Ouyang’s account. In more recent times, Master Fang argued that there are both a legitimate succession and an irregular succession. Only once the doctrine of legitimate succession is established is the ruler’s position exalted; only once the designation of irregular succession is established does the meaning of legitimate succession become clear. According to Master Fang’s account, those who failed to unite all under Heaven need not be discussed. Even those who did unite it, if they acquired it by illegitimate means, must all be assigned to the irregular succession and may not rank alongside the legitimate succession. Ah! For breadth and refinement of learning, none could surpass Master Ouyang; for precision in discerning moral principles, Master Zhu likewise seems beyond criticism. Yet Master Fang continued to dispute their views. Was this merely a fondness for differing from others? Master Fang was surely concerned that disorders throughout the realm would grow worse by the day, and sought to make the standards stricter in order to restrain them. Furthermore, in discussing the interruption and continuation of the legitimate succession, Master Ouyang identified three doubtful junctures: first, the transition from Zhou to Qin; second…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
曰東晉後魏之際三曰五代之際謂後之
作史者溺于非聖之學五運之說故其論
曲而不公夫五運之說起于鄒衍非帝王
之所以受命君子不道也然仁暴之迹逆
順之辨人心是非之公不容掩焉則人之
以秦爲閏以梁爲僞或有微意未可知也
東晉雖偏安猶正朔之餘後魏雖强盛乃
夷狄之雄也固不當如南北史之相詆自
君子觀之其去取亦當有辨也歐陽子進
===
秦繢周且謂秦之得國其初無異湯武則
湯武果利天下而殘酷不仁者哉此以正
統予秦方氏終不敢以爲安也秦不可以
爲正統則晉隋可知也朱子之敘正統蓋
亦沿歐陽子之說不得已而予秦晉隋耳
方氏之言變統有三曰簒奪也女后也夷
狄也書法所加必嚴加貶絶而不得與正
統並今觀朱子于魏晉之受禪而書其自
立所以討簒賊也于武后之光宅而削其
punctuated:
曰東晉後魏之際，三曰五代之際。謂後之作史者溺于非聖之學、五運之說，故其論曲而不公。夫五運之說起于鄒衍，非帝王之所以受命，君子不道也。然仁暴之迹、逆順之辨，人心是非之公，不容掩焉。則人之以秦爲閏、以梁爲僞，或有微意，未可知也。東晉雖偏安，猶正朔之餘；後魏雖强盛，乃夷狄之雄也。固不當如南北史之相詆，自君子觀之，其去取亦當有辨也。歐陽子進秦繢周，且謂秦之得國，其初無異湯武，則湯武果利天下而殘酷不仁者哉？此以正統予秦，方氏終不敢以爲安也。秦不可以爲正統，則晉隋可知也。朱子之敘正統，蓋亦沿歐陽子之說，不得已而予秦晉隋耳。

方氏之言變統有三，曰簒奪也，女后也，夷狄也。書法所加，必嚴加貶絶，而不得與正統並。今觀朱子于魏晉之受禪而書其自立，所以討簒賊也；于武后之光宅而削其
translation_en:
…[second] is the transition between Eastern Jin and Later Wei; third is the period of the Five Dynasties. He says that later historians became immersed in teachings contrary to those of the sages and in the theory of the Five Phases’ successive ascendancy, so that their judgments were distorted and impartiality lost. This theory originated with Zou Yan; it is not the basis upon which emperors and kings receive the Mandate, and the gentleman does not speak of it. Yet the evidence of benevolence or brutality, the distinction between rebellion and rightful obedience, and the impartial judgment of right and wrong in people’s hearts cannot be concealed. Thus, those who treat Qin as an intercalary dynasty and Liang as illegitimate may have subtle reasons for doing so; we cannot be certain. Although Eastern Jin held only a regional refuge, it still preserved the remnants of legitimate calendrical authority. Although Later Wei was powerful, it was a hegemon among the barbarians. Certainly one should not engage in mutual disparagement as do the histories of the southern and northern dynasties; yet from a gentleman’s perspective, acceptance and rejection must still rest upon distinctions. Master Ouyang elevates Qin as Zhou’s successor [?], and even says that Qin’s acquisition of the realm was initially no different from that of Tang and Wu. But were Tang and Wu really men who coveted the realm and were cruel and inhumane? Master Fang could never feel comfortable with thus granting Qin legitimate succession. If Qin cannot be considered legitimate, the implications for Jin and Sui are clear. Master Zhu’s account of legitimate succession presumably also follows Master Ouyang’s argument, granting legitimacy to Qin, Jin, and Sui only because he felt compelled to do so.

Master Fang identifies three forms of aberrant succession: usurpation, female rulers, and barbarians. Wherever the conventions of historical writing apply, these must be sternly condemned and excluded, and must not be placed alongside legitimate succession. Now consider how Master Zhu records the rulers of Wei and Jin as having established themselves when they received the throne through abdication: this is his means of condemning usurpers. In the case of Empress Wu’s Guangzhai reign, he deletes her…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
紀年所以絶女后也于克用之舉兵而著
其沙陀所以別夷狄也雖合天下于一如
秦人天下有惡其暴而首事者不以爲叛
而以爲起兵其書法之嚴亦猶方氏之意
則方氏變統之說亦朱子之意亦歐陽子
正不正之意也特其憂之也切故其辨之
也詳不嫌于少異耳由周以來國統之離
合絶續不常而不正之徒恒以智力攘奪
其間民生其時者何不幸也晉也隋也皆
===
簒奪之賊也後魏也後唐也皆夷狄之雄
也使簒奪而可以與正統則人之負恩于
紀者將益奔走矣使夷狄而可以與正統
則夷之亂夷猾夏者將益充斥矣夫其智
力可以僞定一時而終不能奪萬世是非
之公庶後世之人猶知所畏而不敢肆也
可徒以其一天下而槩予之乎且晉隋雖
得之不正然猶中國也后魏后唐雖夷狄
然猶未一天下也變猶未甚也至胡元之
