punctuated: 紀年，所以絶女后也；于克用之舉兵而著其沙陀，所以別夷狄也。雖合天下于一，如秦人，天下有惡其暴而首事者，不以爲叛，而以爲起兵。其書法之嚴，亦猶方氏之意。則方氏變統之說，亦朱子之意，亦歐陽子正不正之意也。特其憂之也切，故其辨之也詳，不嫌于少異耳。由周以來，國統之離合絶續不常，而不正之徒恒以智力攘奪其間。民生其時者，何不幸也！晉也，隋也，皆簒奪之賊也；後魏也，後唐也，皆夷狄之雄也。使簒奪而可以與正統，則人之負恩于紀者將益奔走矣；使夷狄而可以與正統，則夷之亂夷猾夏者將益充斥矣。夫其智力可以僞定一時，而終不能奪萬世是非之公。庶後世之人猶知所畏，而不敢肆也。可徒以其一天下而槩予之乎？且晉隋雖得之不正，然猶中國也；后魏后唐雖夷狄，然猶未一天下也。變猶未甚也。至胡元之
translation_en:
…reign-year designations, thereby excluding female rulers; in recording Keyong’s raising of troops, he identifies him as Shatuo, thereby distinguishing the non-Chinese peoples. Even when a dynasty united All under Heaven, as Qin did, if someone in the realm detested its tyranny and initiated resistance, he described this as raising troops, not as rebellion. The severity of his historical wording likewise accords with Master Fang’s intention. Thus Master Fang’s theory of aberrant dynastic succession also expresses Master Zhu’s intention, and Master Ouyang’s distinction between legitimate and illegitimate succession. It is simply that his concern was acute, so his distinctions were detailed; he did not shrink from minor differences.

Since Zhou, the dynastic succession has undergone unpredictable divisions and reunifications, interruptions and continuations, while illegitimate contenders have continually used cunning and force to seize power amid these changes. How unfortunate were the people born in those times! Jin and Sui were both usurping traitors; Later Wei and Later Tang were both powerful rulers among the non-Chinese peoples. If usurpers may be accorded legitimate succession, those who betray favors and violate the established order [?] will pursue their ambitions all the more eagerly. If non-Chinese rulers may be accorded legitimate succession, those among them who disorder the non-Chinese peoples and disrupt the Chinese realm [?] will proliferate all the more. Their cunning and force may establish a spurious settlement for a time, but ultimately cannot overturn the impartial judgment of right and wrong for all ages. One hopes that people of later generations will still know what to fear and dare not act without restraint. Can legitimate succession be granted indiscriminately merely because they united All under Heaven?

Moreover, although Jin and Sui acquired power illegitimately, they were still Chinese dynasties. Although Later Wei and Later Tang were non-Chinese, they had not united All under Heaven. The aberration was still not extreme. When it comes to the non-Chinese Yuan’s…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
入主中國舉中國之衣冠而左衽之舉中
國之俎豆而腥羶之且遲遲于百年之久
將胥天下而爲禽獸之歸變未有甚于此
者也尚可以其一天下而予之乎如其不
予則吾予晉隋而不予元彼將有辭如其
予之則何以謹華夷之辨此方氏之言固
將爲萬世之坊而非苟以爲異也史法爲
萬世是非之公非一家之私言于義苟安
雖異于先哲亦先哲之所許也況方氏之
===
言又與朱子相出入者哉我
國家受
天明命驅逐胡元復古帝王所自立之土宇敘
古帝王所世守之彝倫日月于是乎貞明
乾坤于是乎再闢
得國之正雖湯武之放伐有慚德焉真有以
陋漢唐宋于不居而秦晉隋不足言矣天
下臣民沐浴
膏澤歌詠
punctuated:
入主中國，舉中國之衣冠而左衽之，舉中國之俎豆而腥羶之，且遲遲于百年之久，將胥天下而爲禽獸之歸，變未有甚于此者也。尚可以其一天下而予之乎？如其不予，則吾予晉隋而不予元，彼將有辭；如其予之，則何以謹華夷之辨？此方氏之言，固將爲萬世之坊，而非苟以爲異也。史法爲萬世是非之公，非一家之私言。于義苟安，雖異于先哲，亦先哲之所許也。況方氏之言，又與朱子相出入者哉！
我國家受天明命，驅逐胡元，復古帝王所自立之土宇，敘古帝王所世守之彝倫。日月于是乎貞明，乾坤于是乎再闢。得國之正，雖湯武之放伐有慚德焉。真有以陋漢唐宋于不居，而秦晉隋不足言矣。天下臣民沐浴膏澤，歌詠
translation_en:
…entered and ruled China, making all China’s people fasten their robes to the left and tainting all China’s ritual vessels with the rank smell of meat. Moreover, they lingered for as long as a century, threatening to bring the entire realm down to the condition of birds and beasts. Never had there been a more extreme upheaval. Can we still accord them legitimate succession merely because they unified the realm? If we do not, then, since we accord it to Jin and Sui but deny it to Yuan, their defenders will have grounds for objection. If we do accord it to them, how can we rigorously maintain the distinction between Chinese and barbarians? Master Fang’s statement was surely intended as a bulwark for all ages, not merely as an attempt to be different. The principles of historical writing embody the impartial judgment of right and wrong for all ages, not the private opinion of a single school. If a position accords with righteousness, then even if it differs from the earlier sages, those sages themselves would approve it. How much more so when Master Fang’s statement is broadly consonant with Master Zhu’s!
Our dynasty received Heaven’s luminous mandate, expelled the barbarian Yuan, restored the territory in which the ancient sage emperors and kings had established their rule, and set in order the enduring human relationships that those rulers had upheld generation after generation. Thus the sun and moon regained their constant brightness, and Heaven and Earth were opened anew. Such was the legitimacy with which our dynasty acquired the realm that even Tang and Wu, who banished or attacked their sovereigns, would have cause for shame by comparison. It truly so far surpasses Han, Tang, and Song as to render them insignificant; Qin, Jin, and Sui are scarcely worth mentioning. The officials and people throughout the realm bathe in its gracious bounty and sing praises …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
道化未嘗不在生斯時也若夫
保一統□□而綿綿無疆之曆則
聖天子方與□□公卿默運于鈞陶之上草莽賤
臣又何能測焉
第四問
同考試官教諭安　批〔人物一志甚有助於觀人擇材之法子能詳究而復加折衷其亦稽古而有得者耶〕
王之翰
===
考試官侍讀陳　批〔明確〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔蓋亦傚潞公之忠者〕
人君以用賢爲急而用賢以知人爲要天
生人而賦之性性無不一而材固不得而
強同也君擇人而任之事事雖不一而人
則有難於求備也天之生材有偏全而君
之任用有小大用各適宜則天下無不可
用之材材各勝任則天下無不可成之事
顧在人君知人何如耳知此則劉邵人物
punctuated:
道化，未嘗不在生斯時也。若夫保一統□□而綿綿無疆之曆，則聖天子方與□□公卿默運于鈞陶之上，草莽賤臣又何能測焉？

第四問
同考試官教諭安　批〔人物一志，甚有助於觀人擇材之法。子能詳究而復加折衷，其亦稽古而有得者耶？〕
王之翰
考試官侍讀陳　批〔明確〕
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔蓋亦傚潞公之忠者〕

人君以用賢爲急，而用賢以知人爲要。天生人而賦之性，性無不一，而材固不得而強同也。君擇人而任之事，事雖不一，而人則有難於求備也。天之生材有偏全，而君之任用有小大。用各適宜，則天下無不可用之材；材各勝任，則天下無不可成之事。顧在人君知人何如耳。知此，則劉邵人物
translation_en:
…the transforming influence of the Way, never failing to rejoice [?] in being born in this age. As for preserving unified rule □□ and a succession of years extending endlessly without limit, the sagely Son of Heaven is now, together with □□ the dukes and ministers, silently directing affairs from above, like a potter shaping clay. How could your lowly servant, dwelling among the common people, fathom this?

Fourth Question
Associate Examiner An, Instructor, comments: 〔The Treatise on Personalities greatly assists the methods of assessing people and selecting talent. You have examined it thoroughly and further weighed its judgments. Are you not also someone who has gained insight through investigating antiquity?〕
Wang Zhihan
Examiner Chen, Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔Clear and precise.〕
Examiner Qu, Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔He too seems to emulate the loyalty of the Duke of Lu.〕

A ruler regards employing the worthy as urgent, and discerning people is the key to employing the worthy. Heaven brings people into being and endows them with their nature. Their nature is invariably the same, but their talents certainly cannot be forced into uniformity. A ruler selects people and entrusts them with tasks. Although tasks differ, it is difficult to demand every accomplishment of any one person. The talents Heaven produces may be partial or comprehensive, and the responsibilities a ruler assigns may be small or great. If each appointment is appropriate, there is no talent under Heaven that cannot be put to use; if each person’s talents fit the responsibilities assigned, there is no undertaking under Heaven that cannot be accomplished. It depends solely on how well the ruler discerns people. Understanding this, then Liu Shao’s Treatise on Personalities…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
志雖其中洞意少疵而鑒別之當商確之
詳固有足多者請得而復明悶可乎且天
以是理賦於人而人得之以爲性無智愚
賢不肖一也特發見而爲才有偏有全若
是其不同矣惟至哲爲能隨材而授任因
人以器使故尚書序堯舜命官之美自禹
稷益契以降所命典司不踰一職登之創
大廈者棟梁榱桷之材所畢集成大車者
輪轅衡軏之用無所遺鑒別於始授不責
===
之以不能委任於既用不撓之以所守專
極其理人盡其材功烺當時名施後世迨
其失也取舍違則好惡乖正使人不量其
器與人不由其誠或付任逾涯而不思其
所不及或責望過高而不恕其所不能職
日以曠而治因以舛自古理亂之由槩然
可考矣魏明帝時詔博求衆賢散騎侍郎
夏侯惠薦劉卲曰深忠篤思體周於數凡
所錯綜源流弘遠群材大小咸取所同而
punctuated: 志，雖其中洞意少疵，而鑒別之當、商確之詳，固有足多者。請得而復明悶，可乎？且天以是理賦於人，而人得之以爲性，無智愚賢不肖，一也。特發見而爲才，有偏有全，若是其不同矣。惟至哲爲能隨材而授任，因人以器使。故《尚書》序堯舜命官之美，自禹稷益契以降，所命典司，不踰一職。登之，創大廈者，棟梁榱桷之材所畢集；成大車者，輪轅衡軏之用無所遺。鑒別於始授，不責之以不能；委任於既用，不撓之以所守。專極其理，人盡其材，功烺當時，名施後世。迨其失也，取舍違則，好惡乖正，使人不量其器，與人不由其誠。或付任逾涯，而不思其所不及；或責望過高，而不恕其所不能。職日以曠，而治因以舛。自古理亂之由，槩然可考矣。魏明帝時，詔博求衆賢，散騎侍郎夏侯惠薦劉卲曰：「深忠篤思，體周於數，凡所錯綜，源流弘遠，群材大小，咸取所同而
translation_en:
…Treatise on Human Character (Renwu zhi): although some of its ideas have minor flaws [?], its sound discrimination and detailed deliberation certainly deserve considerable praise. May I elaborate further to clarify the doubts [?]? Heaven endows human beings with this principle, and they receive it as their nature. Whether wise or foolish, worthy or unworthy, all are alike in this respect. Only when it manifests itself as ability do some possess partial and others comprehensive capacities, differing so greatly from one another. Only the wisest can assign responsibilities according to ability and employ people according to their capacities. Thus, when the Book of Documents recounts the excellence of Yao and Shun in appointing officials, from Yu, Ji, Yi, and Xie onward, each was entrusted with responsibility for no more than one office. By analogy [?], someone constructing a great hall assembles all the timber needed for ridgepoles, beams, and rafters; someone making a great carriage omits none of the functions supplied by wheels, shafts, crossbars, and yoke-pins. Distinguish people’s abilities when first appointing them, without demanding what they cannot do; once they are employed, entrust them with responsibility without obstructing them in carrying out their charge. Each fully attends to his particular responsibilities, and everyone exhausts his abilities. Their achievements shine in their own time [?], and their fame extends to later generations.
When this practice breaks down, selection and rejection depart from proper standards, and likes and dislikes stray from what is right. People are employed without their capacities being assessed, and supported without regard to their sincerity. Some are entrusted with responsibilities beyond their limits, without consideration for what lies beyond their reach; others face excessively high expectations, without allowance for what they cannot accomplish. Official duties are increasingly neglected, and government consequently goes awry. The causes of order and disorder since antiquity can broadly be discerned from this.
During the reign of Emperor Ming of Wei, an edict ordered a broad search for worthy men. Xiahou Hui, Gentleman Attendant of Cavalier Service, recommended Liu Shao, saying: “Profoundly loyal and earnest in thought, he comprehensively grasps methods and principles. In everything he analyzes and brings together, his understanding of origins and developments is broad and far-reaching. Of the various talents, great and small, he takes what they have in common and…”

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
斟酌焉史臣陳壽亦曰邵該覽學籍文質
周洽故宋臣文彥博於熈寧之時援劉邵
人物志進說蓋以邵之書主於詳察人物
於任官擇材之法有可觀焉其言曰人之
質量中和最貴中和之質必平淡無味故
能調成五材變化應節是以觀人察質必
先察其平淡而後求其聰明此觀物之則
也但天之生人兼材常少而偏材寔多故
主治於上者非兼材則無以獨運分任於
===
下者雖偏材亦各有所長今考其志人流
之業十二有清節家有法家有術家有國
體有器能有臧否有伎倆有智意有文章
有儒學有口辨有雄傑論其人則延陵晏
嬰爲清節家管仲商鞅爲法家范蠡張良
爲術家伊尹呂望爲國體子產西門豹爲
器能子夏之徒爲臧否張敞趙廣漢爲伎
倆陳平韓安國爲智意司馬遷班固爲文
章毛公貫公爲儒學樂毅曹丘生爲口辨
punctuated:
斟酌焉。史臣陳壽亦曰：「邵該覽學籍，文質周洽。」故宋臣文彥博於熈寧之時，援劉邵《人物志》進說，蓋以邵之書主於詳察人物，於任官擇材之法有可觀焉。其言曰：「人之質量，中和最貴。中和之質，必平淡無味，故能調成五材，變化應節。是以觀人察質，必先察其平淡，而後求其聰明，此觀物之則也。」但天之生人，兼材常少，而偏材寔多，故主治於上者，非兼材則無以獨運；分任於下者，雖偏材亦各有所長。
今考其志，人流之業十二：有清節家，有法家，有術家，有國體，有器能，有臧否，有伎倆，有智意，有文章，有儒學，有口辨，有雄傑。論其人，則延陵、晏嬰爲清節家，管仲、商鞅爲法家，范蠡、張良爲術家，伊尹、呂望爲國體，子產、西門豹爲器能，子夏之徒爲臧否，張敞、趙廣漢爲伎倆，陳平、韓安國爲智意，司馬遷、班固爲文章，毛公、貫公爲儒學，樂毅、曹丘生爲口辨，
translation_en:
…and weighs and assesses them. The historian Chen Shou also said: “Shao read scholarly writings comprehensively and was thoroughly accomplished in both refinement and substance.” Thus Wen Yanbo, a minister of the Song, drew upon Liu Shao’s Treatise on Human Types (Renwu zhi) when presenting his views during the Xining era. This was because Shao’s book chiefly concerns the close examination of human character and offers insights into methods of appointing officials and selecting talent. It says: “Among people’s inherent qualities and capacities, balance and harmony are most valuable. A balanced and harmonious disposition must be bland and without distinctive flavor; thus it can harmonize the five constituent qualities and adapt to change in due measure. Therefore, in observing people and examining their dispositions, one must first examine their blandness and only afterward seek their intelligence and discernment. This is the rule for observing things.” Yet among the people Heaven produces, those with comprehensive talents are always few, while those with specialized talents are indeed numerous. Thus those who preside over government above cannot direct affairs independently unless their talents are comprehensive; those who share responsibilities below each have their strengths, even if their talents are specialized.
Examining his Treatise, we find twelve fields of endeavor corresponding to types of people: those of pure integrity; experts in law; experts in statecraft; those embodying the capacities of a statesman; capable administrators; appraisers of merit and fault; resourceful practitioners; discerning planners; literary writers; Confucian scholars; skilled speakers; and outstanding heroes. As for their exemplars, Yanling and Yan Ying represent pure integrity; Guan Zhong and Shang Yang, expertise in law; Fan Li and Zhang Liang, expertise in statecraft; Yi Yin and Lü Wang, the capacities of a statesman; Zichan and Ximen Bao, administrative ability; the followers of Zixia, appraisal of merit and fault; Zhang Chang and Zhao Guanghan, practical resourcefulness; Chen Ping and Han Anguo, discerning planning; Sima Qian and Ban Gu, literary writing; Master Mao and Master Guan, Confucian scholarship; and Yue Yi and Cao Qiusheng, skill in speaking…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
白起韓信爲驍雄論其任則清節之德師
氏之任也法家之材司寇之任也術家之
材三孤之任也三材純備三公之任也三
材而微冢宰之材冢宰之任也□□之佐
也智意之材冢宰之佐也□□伎倆之材司空
之任也儒學之材安民之任也文章之材
國史之任也辨給之材行人之任也驍雄
之材將帥之任也凡此十二材分爲十二
任皆人臣之責也主德不與焉主德者聰
===
明平淡總達衆材而不以事自任者也是
謂王道得而臣道序官不易方而太平用
成矣卲之意蓋以流有十二則人材無不
盡任有十二則官職無不備即古人之已
行而分指爲專家見用當其材而事無不
舉於任官擇材之法誠有可觀者今夫偏
材之人皆一味之美故長於辦一官而短
於爲一國何者一官之任以一味協五味
一國之政以無味和五味故偏材治小則
punctuated:
白起、韓信爲驍雄。論其任，則清節之德，師氏之任也；法家之材，司寇之任也；術家之材，三孤之任也；三材純備，三公之任也；三材而微，冢宰之材，冢宰之任也，□□之佐也；智意之材，冢宰之佐也；□□伎倆之材，司空之任也；儒學之材，安民之任也；文章之材，國史之任也；辨給之材，行人之任也；驍雄之材，將帥之任也。凡此十二材，分爲十二任，皆人臣之責也，主德不與焉。主德者，聰明平淡，總達衆材而不以事自任者也。是謂王道得而臣道序，官不易方，而太平用成矣。
卲之意，蓋以流有十二，則人材無不盡；任有十二，則官職無不備。即古人之已行而分指爲專家，見用當其材，而事無不舉。於任官擇材之法，誠有可觀者。今夫偏材之人，皆一味之美，故長於辦一官而短於爲一國。何者？一官之任，以一味協五味；一國之政，以無味和五味。故偏材治小則
translation_en:
…Bai Qi and Han Xin represent martial prowess. As for their appointments: the virtue of pure integrity suits the duties of the Preceptor; the talent of experts in law, those of the Minister of Justice; and the talent of experts in strategic methods, those of the Three Solitaries. Possessing all three talents in full purity suits the duties of the Three Dukes. Possessing the three talents in lesser degree constitutes the talent of the Minister of State and suits that office, serving as an assistant to □□ [?]. Talent in intelligent planning suits service as an assistant to the Minister of State. □□ Talent in practical skills suits the duties of the Minister of Works; talent in Confucian learning, the task of pacifying the people; literary talent, the duties of the State Historiographer; ready eloquence, those of the Messenger; and martial prowess, those of generals and commanders. These twelve talents are assigned to twelve kinds of responsibility, all of which are the obligations of ministers. The ruler’s virtue does not enter into this classification. The ruler’s virtue consists in perceptiveness and understanding, equanimity and freedom from partiality: comprehending all the various talents without personally assuming responsibility for particular affairs. This is what is meant by the ruler’s Way being realized and the ministers’ Way being ordered: officials do not depart from their proper spheres, and thereby great peace is achieved.
Shao’s meaning is presumably that, with twelve categories, every human talent is encompassed, and with twelve kinds of responsibility, every official function is covered. Taking what men of antiquity had already accomplished, he identifies them separately as specialists, showing that when their employment matched their talents, no business was left undone. His method of appointing officials and selecting talent certainly deserves consideration. Now, people of specialized talent all possess the excellence of a single flavor. Thus they are good at administering one office but deficient in governing an entire state. Why is this? The responsibility of a single office is to bring one flavor into accord with the five flavors; governing an entire state requires harmonizing the five flavors through the absence of a distinctive flavor. Thus, when specialized talent governs a small domain…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
相稱以之統大則非宜蓋任有小大材有
偏全不可得而强也偏材之人皆一流之
材故能識同體之善而或失異量之美何
者一流之人能識一流之善二流之人能
識二流之美故取同體也則接論而相得
取異體也雖歷久而不知蓋以我觀物而
不以物觀物惡在其知人也是故用人者
必量材授任不强其所不能觀人者必以
物觀物不執己以自是邵之論似亦當矣
===
然亦竊有可疑者焉以彊國富人爲法家
則桑孔言利之徒不必鄙矣以遭變用權
爲智意則蘇張縱横之術不必非矣謂能
傳聖人之業而不能幹事施政爲儒學則
吾儒顧有無用之學乎謂辯不入道而應
對資給爲口辯則佞者顧在所取乎英爲
智而雄爲膽則英雄兼備爲豪傑而曰英
可以爲相雄可以爲將豈可分爲二用乎
惡訐以爲直則訐直迹同而實異而曰直
punctuated:
相稱，以之統大則非宜。蓋任有小大，材有偏全，不可得而强也。偏材之人皆一流之材，故能識同體之善，而或失異量之美。何者？一流之人能識一流之善，二流之人能識二流之美。故取同體也，則接論而相得；取異體也，雖歷久而不知。蓋以我觀物，而不以物觀物，惡在其知人也？是故用人者必量材授任，不强其所不能；觀人者必以物觀物，不執己以自是。邵之論似亦當矣。
然亦竊有可疑者焉。以彊國富人爲法家，則桑孔言利之徒不必鄙矣；以遭變用權爲智意，則蘇張縱横之術不必非矣。謂能傳聖人之業而不能幹事施政爲儒學，則吾儒顧有無用之學乎？謂辯不入道而應對資給爲口辯，則佞者顧在所取乎？英爲智而雄爲膽，則英雄兼備爲豪傑，而曰英可以爲相，雄可以爲將，豈可分爲二用乎？惡訐以爲直，則訐直迹同而實異，而曰直
translation_en:
…they are well matched; to employ them in overseeing great affairs, however, is inappropriate. Responsibilities differ in scale, and talents may be specialized or comprehensive: one cannot force them beyond their capacities. People of specialized talent each possess the talent of a particular type. Thus they can recognize the merits of those of their own kind, yet may overlook the excellence of those whose capacities differ. Why? A person whose abilities embrace one type can recognize the merits of that type; one whose abilities embrace two types can recognize the excellence of both. Thus, when selecting someone of the same kind, they reach mutual understanding through conversation; when selecting someone of a different kind, they may remain unable to understand him even after a long acquaintance. This is judging others from one’s own standpoint rather than on their own terms. How can this amount to knowing people? Therefore, those who employ people must assess their talents and assign responsibilities accordingly, without forcing them to do what lies beyond their abilities. Those who appraise people must consider them on their own terms, without clinging to their own standpoint and assuming themselves correct. Shao’s argument, it would seem, is sound.
Yet I venture to find points open to doubt. If strengthening the state and enriching the people defines the category of experts in administrative methods, then profit-seeking men such as Sang and Kong need not be despised. If responding to changing circumstances with expedient measures defines strategic intelligence, then the arts of forming vertical and horizontal alliances practiced by Su and Zhang need not be condemned. If transmitting the undertaking of the sages while being unable to manage affairs and administer government defines Confucian learning, does our Confucian tradition really contain learning that is useless? If argument that does not accord with the Way, coupled with ready resources in answering, defines verbal eloquence, are glib flatterers really among those to be selected? If the outstanding possess wisdom and the mighty possess courage, then those who combine both qualities are men of exceptional ability. Yet he says that the outstanding may serve as chief councilors and the mighty as generals: can these really be separated into two distinct functions? We detest exposing others’ faults when it passes for uprightness; thus faultfinding and uprightness resemble each other outwardly but differ in substance. Yet he says that the upright…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
者亦訐訐者亦訐豈可混爲一塗乎孔子
謂上智與下愚不移而偏材則非下愚也
顧謂性不可轉移耶孟子謂仁者無不愛
而慈仁自無不愛也顧有不仁不恤耶其
合於聖賢之論則有矣觀其感變以知常
度即誠中形外而由外可以識中也觀其
所短以知所長則人各有短有長取其所
長而舍其所短也衆惡必察衆好必察信
耳而不信目是不審於毀譽者也而察譽
===
有偏頗之謬矣同弗與異弗非踈善而善
非是以已爲愛惡者也而接物有愛惡之
惑矣自漢以來儒者聞道甚鮮劉邵崛起
於魏固一時之選也然於聖賢之論亦未
悉聞故其言不能無純駁惟其意而不惟
其言取其大旨而略其小疵則邵之論亦
不可以盡少也今夫用材貴恕知人貴精
用天下之材必先知天下之人然知人亦
難矣聽言未可信其行觀貌未必察其心
punctuated:
者亦訐，訐者亦訐，豈可混爲一塗乎？孔子謂上智與下愚不移，而偏材則非下愚也，顧謂性不可轉移耶？孟子謂仁者無不愛，而慈仁自無不愛也，顧有不仁不恤耶？其合於聖賢之論則有矣。觀其感變以知常度，即誠中形外，而由外可以識中也。觀其所短以知所長，則人各有短有長，取其所長而舍其所短也。衆惡必察，衆好必察，信耳而不信目，是不審於毀譽者也，而察譽有偏頗之謬矣。同弗與，異弗非，踈善而善非，是以已爲愛惡者也，而接物有愛惡之惑矣。
自漢以來，儒者聞道甚鮮。劉邵崛起於魏，固一時之選也。然於聖賢之論亦未悉聞，故其言不能無純駁。惟其意而不惟其言，取其大旨而略其小疵，則邵之論亦不可以盡少也。今夫用材貴恕，知人貴精。用天下之材，必先知天下之人。然知人亦難矣，聽言未可信其行，觀貌未必察其心。
translation_en:
…the upright also expose others’ faults, and those who denounce others likewise expose faults—how can the two be lumped together? Confucius said that the highest in wisdom and the lowest in stupidity do not change; yet people of one-sided ability are not the lowest in stupidity. How, then, can one say that their nature cannot be changed? Mencius said that the benevolent love all things; those who are compassionate and benevolent naturally love all things. How, then, could they lack benevolence or concern?
There are, to be sure, points in his discussion that accord with the teachings of the sages and worthies. To observe how people respond to changing circumstances in order to discern their constant standards is to recognize that what is truly within manifests itself outwardly, and that the inward can therefore be known through the outward. To observe their shortcomings in order to know their strengths means that everyone has both shortcomings and strengths: one should employ their strengths and set aside their shortcomings. When everyone dislikes someone, one must investigate; when everyone likes someone, one must investigate. Trusting one’s ears rather than one’s eyes shows a failure to scrutinize disparagement and praise, and thus an error of partiality in assessing praise. One should neither endorse someone merely for agreeing nor condemn someone merely for differing. To estrange oneself from the good and approve what is wrong [?] is to make oneself the measure of likes and dislikes; thus, in dealing with others, one is led astray by these preferences.
Since the Han dynasty, very few Confucian scholars have heard the Way. Liu Shao rose to prominence in Wei and was certainly an outstanding man of his age. Yet he had not fully learned the teachings of the sages and worthies, so his statements inevitably mingle the sound with the unsound. If we attend to his intentions rather than merely his words, grasp his main purport, and overlook his minor flaws, Shao’s discussion cannot be dismissed altogether.
Now, in employing talent, generosity of judgment is essential; in understanding people, precision is essential. To employ the talent of the realm, one must first understand the people of the realm. Yet understanding people is difficult indeed. Hearing their words does not necessarily warrant confidence in their conduct; observing their appearance does not necessarily reveal their hearts…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
矯飾或疑於清節詭秘或疑於術家張大
或疑於國體權譎或疑於器能譏刺或疑
於臧否奇巧或疑於伎倆游詞或疑於文
章剛暴或疑於驍雄是非判於幾微情僞
伏於微曖苟非在我權度精切鮮有不惑
於此者是以人君用人必廣詢獨見詳察
愼擇非其人也則絕之必嚴無倖進之弊
如其才也則舉之不疑得彙征之吉事君
者度德量力重於始進而不自衒以求售
===
用人者因能授事審於任用而不責備以
過刻故曰臣以自任爲能君以用人爲能
臣以能言爲能君以能聽爲能臣以能行
爲能君以能賞罰爲能君臣各盡其能而
治功所由以成世道所由以泰也昔宋神
宗時君子小人雜進文彥博欲其鑒前古
治忽之由於人物更加詳察故援邵志以
進說耳蓋人材不一各有短長兼收並錄
乃克有濟是以人主不可偏好而必貴乎
punctuated:
矯飾或疑於清節，詭秘或疑於術家，張大或疑於國體，權譎或疑於器能，譏刺或疑於臧否，奇巧或疑於伎倆，游詞或疑於文章，剛暴或疑於驍雄。是非判於幾微，情僞伏於微曖。苟非在我權度精切，鮮有不惑於此者。是以人君用人，必廣詢獨見，詳察愼擇。非其人也，則絕之必嚴，無倖進之弊；如其才也，則舉之不疑，得彙征之吉。事君者度德量力，重於始進，而不自衒以求售；用人者因能授事，審於任用，而不責備以過刻。故曰：「臣以自任爲能，君以用人爲能；臣以能言爲能，君以能聽爲能；臣以能行爲能，君以能賞罰爲能。」君臣各盡其能，而治功所由以成，世道所由以泰也。
昔宋神宗時，君子小人雜進，文彥博欲其鑒前古治忽之由，於人物更加詳察，故援邵志以進說耳。蓋人材不一，各有短長，兼收並錄，乃克有濟。是以人主不可偏好，而必貴乎
translation_en:
… Affectation may be mistaken for unsullied integrity; secretive cunning for mastery of statecraft; grandiosity for the bearing of a statesman; expedient deceit for practical ability; sarcastic criticism for sound judgments of merit; clever ingenuity for skill; empty rhetoric for literary accomplishment; and violent obstinacy for martial prowess. Right and wrong are distinguished by the finest nuances, while sincerity and falsity lie hidden in obscurity. Unless one’s own standards of judgment are precise and exact, few can avoid being misled by these things. Thus, when employing men, a ruler must consult widely while judging independently, examine closely, and choose carefully. If a man is unsuitable, the ruler must firmly exclude him, preventing the abuse of advancement through mere good fortune. If a man has the requisite talent, the ruler must promote him without hesitation, securing the good fortune of worthy men advancing together. Those who serve a ruler should assess their virtue and measure their strength, attaching weight to their first entry into service rather than advertising themselves to secure employment. Those who employ men should assign duties according to ability and exercise care in appointments, rather than demand perfection with excessive severity. Hence it is said: “A minister’s ability lies in undertaking responsibilities himself; a ruler’s ability lies in employing others. A minister’s ability lies in speaking well; a ruler’s ability lies in listening well. A minister’s ability lies in acting effectively; a ruler’s ability lies in administering rewards and punishments.” When ruler and ministers each exercise their abilities fully, successful government is thereby achieved, and the world thereby enjoys peace.
Formerly, during the reign of Emperor Shenzong of the Song, gentlemen and petty men advanced into office together. Wen Yanbo wished the emperor to learn from the causes of order and disorder in antiquity and to scrutinize men more closely. It was simply for this reason that he cited Liu Shao’s Treatise on Personalities (Renwu zhi) in presenting his counsel. Human talents are diverse, and each person has weaknesses and strengths. Only by admitting and employing them together can results be achieved. Thus, a ruler must not indulge partial preferences, but must prize …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
淡之道以任材人有小才飭身干進非無
小忠小利以自效也然小忠爲大忠之賊
小利爲大利之殘是以人主必當哲於早
辨而務去小以取大愚甚有取於劉邵聰
明平淡之說焉曰聰明即書所謂克知灼
見曰平淡即書所謂休休有容蓋賢才之
不用每始於不知而見忌惟不知也故賢
才多遺佚之患惟見忌也故賢才多沮抑
之虞必聖人公明兼主者乃克徧舉而恕
===
用焉伊訓曰與人不求備斯言寔用賢之
要是以伊尹雖列於國體而國體實兼乎
衆流得伊尹則衆流皆可以器使也蓋嘗
聞之人君勞於求賢而逸於任人然豈能
人人而任之哉誠得伊尹者而專之則求
賢之勞責諸彼而得賢之逸享於上將見
徧材皆得以效用而野無隱伏登崇不及
於匪人而朝無倖濫賢才輔而天下治邪
正辨而泰道隆自古堯舜所以致雍熈之
punctuated: 淡之道以任材。人有小才，飭身干進，非無小忠小利以自效也。然小忠爲大忠之賊，小利爲大利之殘，是以人主必當哲於早辨，而務去小以取大。愚甚有取於劉邵聰明平淡之說焉。曰聰明，即《書》所謂克知灼見；曰平淡，即《書》所謂休休有容。蓋賢才之不用，每始於不知而見忌。惟不知也，故賢才多遺佚之患；惟見忌也，故賢才多沮抑之虞。必聖人公明兼主者，乃克徧舉而恕用焉。《伊訓》曰：「與人不求備。」斯言寔用賢之要。是以伊尹雖列於國體，而國體實兼乎衆流；得伊尹，則衆流皆可以器使也。蓋嘗聞之，人君勞於求賢，而逸於任人。然豈能人人而任之哉？誠得伊尹者而專之，則求賢之勞責諸彼，而得賢之逸享於上。將見徧材皆得以效用，而野無隱伏；登崇不及於匪人，而朝無倖濫。賢才輔而天下治，邪正辨而泰道隆。自古堯舜所以致雍熈之
translation_en: …the way of equanimity in employing talent. Men of limited talent cultivate their conduct and seek advancement; they are not without minor acts of loyalty or small benefits through which to demonstrate their usefulness. Yet petty loyalty undermines greater loyalty, and small benefits impair greater benefits. Thus the ruler must exercise discernment in distinguishing them early, and strive to discard the lesser in favor of the greater. In my humble view, there is much to commend in Liu Shao’s teaching on perceptiveness and equanimity. Perceptiveness is what the Book of Documents calls “being able to know and see clearly”; equanimity is what it calls “being magnanimous and accommodating.” The failure to employ worthy and talented men commonly begins with their going unrecognized or becoming objects of suspicion. Because they go unrecognized, worthy men often suffer neglect; because they arouse suspicion, they often risk obstruction and suppression. Only a sage who combines impartiality and discernment can recommend them all and employ them with forbearance. The Instructions of Yi states: “In dealing with others, do not demand perfection.” These words express the essential principle of employing the worthy. Thus, although Yi Yin is classified among those who embody the state, this category in fact encompasses all the various kinds of talent. If one obtains a Yi Yin, all kinds can be employed according to their capacities. I have heard that a ruler toils in seeking worthy men but enjoys ease in entrusting responsibilities to others. Yet how could he personally appoint every individual? If he truly obtains a man like Yi Yin and grants him undivided responsibility, the toil of seeking worthy men can be charged to that man, while the ruler above enjoys the ease that comes from obtaining them. Then talents of every kind will be able to render service, and none will remain hidden in the countryside; promotion to high office will not extend to the unworthy, and the court will be free of those who advance through undeserved favor or indiscriminate appointments. With worthy and talented men assisting, the realm will be well governed; with the perverse distinguished from the upright, the way of peace and prosperity will flourish. The means by which Yao and Shun of antiquity brought about the flourishing of harmony and prosperity…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
盛者亦不外此要之致治之道莫先用材
而材有不一惟學可以成材而復性不然
是中人而小有才者也不幾於倖進而黷
治乎惟能以材索性而詳察邪正於未任
之先由是因人授職而咸茂熙績於旣用
之後精於鑒别而恕於任用寔聖人聰明
平淡兼備其材者乃克與能此伊尹所以
爲國體而人君不可不求君人而任之以
總其成也是劉邵序流業之本意故彥博
===
援之以進說於熙寧固以見愛君之念抑
以見取善之公蓋人臣之事君苟可以獻
納不必善之皆自己出也或掩美以上蔽
或掠美以自飾其□□彥博處心何如也即
此足以嘉彥博之忠而况立朝所可稱者
又未易悉數哉故用人者當以邵志折衷
而愛君者當以彥博取法謹對
第五問
王錫爵
punctuated:
盛者，亦不外此。要之，致治之道莫先用材，而材有不一，惟學可以成材而復性。不然，是中人而小有才者也，不幾於倖進而黷治乎？惟能以材索性，而詳察邪正於未任之先，由是因人授職，而咸茂熙績於旣用之後。精於鑒别而恕於任用，寔聖人聰明平淡兼備其材者乃克與能。此伊尹所以爲國體，而人君不可不求，君人而任之以總其成也。是劉邵序流業之本意，故彥博援之以進說於熙寧，固以見愛君之念，抑以見取善之公。蓋人臣之事君，苟可以獻納，不必善之皆自己出也。或掩美以上蔽，或掠美以自飾，其□□彥博處心何如也？即此足以嘉彥博之忠，而况立朝所可稱者，又未易悉數哉！故用人者當以邵志折衷，而愛君者當以彥博取法。謹對。

第五問
王錫爵
translation_en:
…such flourishing prosperity likewise depended on nothing beyond this. In sum, nothing takes precedence over employing talent as the means of achieving good government. Yet talents differ, and only learning can perfect talent and restore one’s original nature. Otherwise, such a person is merely someone of middling character with a little ability. Would this not come close to advancement through undeserved favor and the corruption of government? One must discern a person’s nature through his talents and carefully distinguish the upright from the crooked before appointing him. Then, by assigning offices according to the individual, all can achieve splendid results after entering service. Penetrating in discernment yet forbearing in employing others: only a sage whose capacities encompass both perspicacity and calm impartiality can accomplish this. This is why Yi Yin embodied the substance of the state, and why a sovereign must seek such a man and, as ruler, entrust him with overall responsibility for achieving results.

This was Liu Shao’s original intention in setting out the various types of men and their occupations. Thus Yanbo cited him when presenting his views during the Xining reign period. This certainly showed his concern for his ruler, but also demonstrated his impartiality in adopting what was good. For a minister serving his ruler, if something is worthy of presentation, its merits need not all originate with himself. Some conceal others’ merits and thereby keep their superiors in ignorance; others appropriate those merits to embellish themselves. How do their [two illegible characters] compare with Yanbo’s intentions [?]? This alone suffices to commend Yanbo’s loyalty. How much more was there to praise in his service at court—more than could readily be enumerated! Thus those who employ men should take Shao’s intent as their standard of judgment, while those who cherish their ruler should take Yanbo as their model. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fifth Question
Wang Xijue

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭戴　批〔鹽法一策具悉竅〕
〔進議始末且能斟酌經制蓋亦留心時務者錄〕
〔之非徒以其辭之文也〕
〔條歟〕
考試官侍讀陳　批〔其策可行殆亦識時務之俊〕
限而事之害財者無窮以無窮之用而責
其所以害財者而已矣夫民之生財也有
古今善理財者非能求財而益之也能去
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔議論該洽區畫亦審佳士也〕
===
諸民則民匱而國亦匱節無窮之用而寬
諸民則民足而國亦足故善計國者必慮
其始終權其取予寧去夫事之害財者而
不敢過爲操切之計非重于爲民而輕于
爲國也藏富于民固富國之大者也又何
慮夫財之不足而弊弊焉以求之哉執事
憂吏兵之難贍因有感于鹽法之變而求
善後之策此其念亦深矣愚請先陳鹽法
之始末而條及于經制之略可乎夫鹽筴
punctuated:
同考試官教諭戴　批〔鹽法一策，具悉竅〕〔進議始末，且能斟酌經制，蓋亦留心時務者，錄〕〔之非徒以其辭之文也。〕〔條歟？〕
考試官侍讀陳　批〔其策可行，殆亦識時務之俊。〕
限，而事之害財者無窮，以無窮之用而責其所以害財者而已矣。夫民之生財也有古今善理財者，非能求財而益之也，能去。
考試官侍讀瞿　批〔議論該洽，區畫亦審，佳士也。〕
諸民，則民匱而國亦匱；節無窮之用而寬諸民，則民足而國亦足。故善計國者，必慮其始終，權其取予，寧去夫事之害財者，而不敢過爲操切之計。非重于爲民而輕于爲國也，藏富于民，固富國之大者也。又何慮夫財之不足，而弊弊焉以求之哉？執事憂吏兵之難贍，因有感于鹽法之變，而求善後之策，此其念亦深矣。愚請先陳鹽法之始末，而條及于經制之略，可乎？夫鹽筴
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor, comments: “This policy essay on the salt administration thoroughly understands its workings [?] and the course of the proposals from beginning to end. It also weighs the established institutions. Its author evidently attends to contemporary affairs; his selection is not merely for the elegance of his writing.” A detached annotation reads: “Regulations, perhaps? [?]”
Examiner Chen, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: “His proposals are practicable. He is surely a talented man who understands contemporary affairs.”
[?] The opening lines of the essay appear out of order; their apparent sense is: “Those skilled in managing wealth, past and present, have not increased it by seeking more, but merely eliminated what depletes it. The people's capacity to produce wealth has limits, whereas the activities that consume it are endless. If unlimited expenditure is exacted…”
Examiner Qu, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: “The argument is comprehensive and well informed, and the planning is also judicious. An excellent scholar.”
“…from the people, the people will be impoverished, and the state will likewise be impoverished. If unlimited expenditure is restrained and the people's burdens eased, the people will have enough, and the state will likewise have enough. Thus those who plan well for the state must consider matters from beginning to end and weigh what is taken against what is given. They would rather eliminate activities that deplete wealth and dare not resort excessively to harsh exactions. This is not to give greater weight to serving the people and less to serving the state: keeping wealth among the people is itself a principal means of enriching the state. Why, then, worry that funds will be insufficient and toil anxiously to obtain them?
“You, sir, are concerned about the difficulty of supporting officials and soldiers. Consequently, prompted by changes in the salt administration, you seek a policy for dealing with their aftermath. This concern is indeed far-reaching. May I first set forth the history of the salt administration and then discuss, point by point, the broad outlines of its institutional arrangements? Now, as for the salt monopoly…”

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之征非古也在夏有鹽絺之貢在周有鹽
人之官未始征之以爲利也征之蓋自管
仲始后世若漢之桑弘羊孔僅唐之劉晏
皆祖之以裕國至于今不廢亦其法之不
可廢也蓋古之時其事簡其用易足故有
田賦而無山澤之稅後之時其事煩其用
難供故有田賦而復有征榷之利後世旣
不能如太古之無事則取諸商賈之饒以
寬三農之征亦時義之不可已者也在漢
===
之賢良文學魏之甄琛則以鹽利爲不可
榷是以公利爲心志乎古者也漢之大夫
魏之元勰則以鹽利爲不可罷是以足用
爲心急乎今者也惟胡寅氏折衷之曰盡
捐之民則縱末作資游惰盡收之官則奪
民日用不若官爲厲禁俾民取之而裁取
其稅嗚呼胡寅之言其萬世言鹽法者之
所必稽乎我
國家富有天下鹽筴之利不當常賦百一在
punctuated:
之征，非古也。在夏有鹽絺之貢，在周有鹽人之官，未始征之以爲利也。征之，蓋自管仲始。后世若漢之桑弘羊、孔僅，唐之劉晏，皆祖之以裕國，至于今不廢，亦其法之不可廢也。蓋古之時，其事簡，其用易足，故有田賦而無山澤之稅；後之時，其事煩，其用難供，故有田賦而復有征榷之利。後世旣不能如太古之無事，則取諸商賈之饒，以寬三農之征，亦時義之不可已者也。在漢之賢良文學、魏之甄琛，則以鹽利爲不可榷，是以公利爲心，志乎古者也。漢之大夫、魏之元勰，則以鹽利爲不可罷，是以足用爲心，急乎今者也。惟胡寅氏折衷之曰：「盡捐之民，則縱末作、資游惰；盡收之官，則奪民日用。不若官爲厲禁，俾民取之，而裁取其稅。」嗚呼！胡寅之言，其萬世言鹽法者之所必稽乎！
我國家富有天下，鹽筴之利不當常賦百一，在
translation_en:
…the levying of salt revenues was not an ancient practice. Under the Xia there was tribute of salt and fine ramie cloth; under the Zhou there was the office of Salt Officer. Yet salt was not then taxed for profit. Such taxation apparently began with Guan Zhong. In later ages, men such as Sang Hongyang and Kong Jin of the Han, and Liu Yan of the Tang, all followed his precedent to enrich the state. That the practice has continued to this day also shows that it cannot be abolished. In antiquity, affairs were simple and expenditure easily met; thus there was a land tax but no tax on mountains and marshes. In later times, affairs grew complex and expenditure became difficult to provide for; thus, alongside the land tax, there were revenues from taxation and monopolies. Since later ages cannot enjoy the freedom from affairs of remote antiquity, drawing upon merchants’ abundance to ease the levies on farmers is also something that the needs of the times make unavoidable.
The Worthies and Literati of the Han and Zhen Chen of the Wei held that profits from salt should not be monopolized. They took the public benefit to heart and aspired to antiquity. The Imperial Counselor of the Han and Yuan Xie of the Wei held that salt revenues could not be abolished. They took adequate provision for expenditure to heart and considered present needs urgent. Hu Yin alone reconciled these positions, saying: “To relinquish it entirely to the people would encourage secondary occupations and sustain the idle; to collect it entirely into official hands would deprive the people of their daily necessities. Better for the authorities to impose strict prohibitions, allow the people to obtain salt, and levy a measured tax upon it.” Ah! Surely Hu Yin’s words must be consulted by all who discuss salt administration for ages to come!
Our dynasty possesses all the wealth under Heaven, and the revenue from salt does not amount to one hundredth of regular tax receipts. As for that in …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
兩淮者則特甲天下蓋劉晏所賴以濟唐
中興者也自
國初以來法凡三變而議之者凡幾人矣其
在
國初令人輸粟于邊給之引目以次支給是
謂常股法之正也後以邊儲告急商人困
于守支不樂飛輓乃別儲以待開中是謂
存積法之變也最後屯政廢弛芻粟踊貴
商人難于中納乃乞中餘鹽不輸粟而輸
===
金則變之又變也自餘鹽興而正課微矣
正課微而邊儲匱矣議者欲變通鈔法使
流行如初則可以厚貧竈而收餘鹽一利
權而息私販是賅于名也欲盡復正課使
輸粟如故則可以省度支轉輸之勞增邊
人飽歌之氣是闇于時也且鈔法之難行
久矣漢之平準蓋執以取泉貨猶有本而
易售今之鈔法直執以爲泉貨則無本而
難施在正統時蓋有給米之
punctuated:
兩淮者則特甲天下，蓋劉晏所賴以濟唐中興者也。自國初以來，法凡三變，而議之者凡幾人矣。其在國初，令人輸粟于邊，給之引目，以次支給，是謂常股，法之正也。後以邊儲告急，商人困于守支，不樂飛輓，乃別儲以待開中，是謂存積，法之變也。最後屯政廢弛，芻粟踊貴，商人難于中納，乃乞中餘鹽，不輸粟而輸金，則變之又變也。自餘鹽興，而正課微矣；正課微，而邊儲匱矣。

議者欲變通鈔法，使流行如初，則可以厚貧竈而收餘鹽，一利權而息私販，是賅于名也。欲盡復正課，使輸粟如故，則可以省度支轉輸之勞，增邊人飽歌之氣，是闇于時也。且鈔法之難行久矣。漢之平準，蓋執以取泉貨，猶有本而易售；今之鈔法，直執以爲泉貨，則無本而難施。在正統時，蓋有給米之
translation_en:
…that of Lianghuai ranks foremost in the empire. It was indeed what Liu Yan relied upon to sustain the Tang restoration. Since the founding of our dynasty, the regulations have undergone three changes, and how many people have debated them! At the dynasty’s beginning, merchants were required to deliver grain to the frontier; they were issued salt certificates and received their allotments in sequence. This was called the regular quota system (changgu), the proper form of the regulations. Later, frontier reserves became critically low. Merchants, burdened by waiting to collect their salt, were unwilling to undertake rapid grain transport. Separate salt reserves were therefore established to meet subscriptions for salt rights in exchange for grain deliveries. This was called the reserve system (cunji), a modification of the regulations. Finally, the administration of military agricultural colonies fell into neglect, and fodder and grain became exceedingly expensive. Merchants found it difficult to fulfill their grain-delivery obligations, so they petitioned to purchase rights to surplus salt, paying money instead of delivering grain. This was a further change upon the earlier change. Once the surplus-salt system arose, regular-quota receipts dwindled; as those receipts dwindled, frontier reserves were depleted.

Some who discuss the matter wish to reform the paper-currency system so that the notes circulate as they did initially. They claim that this would improve the livelihood of impoverished salt producers and bring surplus salt under official collection, concentrate control over profits, and end illicit trading. This is to be confined to nominal forms [?]. Others wish to restore the regular quota in full and require grain deliveries as before. They claim that this would spare the fiscal administration the burden of transporting supplies and enable frontier people to sing in the contentment of full stomachs. This is to be ignorant of present circumstances. Moreover, the paper-currency system has long been difficult to put into practice. Under the Han price-equalization system, the authorities held goods with which to obtain money: there was still underlying stock, readily sold. In the present paper-currency system, the notes themselves are simply treated as money; without underlying stock, the system is difficult to implement. During the Zhengtong reign, there was already a provision for issuing rice …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
令矣不議行此而惟欲變通鈔法吾恐無以
惠貧竈而處之終于無術也屯政之廢弛
久矣當烽堠希警田穀布野輕變而折銀
誠罪也今邊城晝閉地多不耕乃強而輸
粟非情也以所輸之銀歸常平爲糴本亦
可得芻粟之用今不議此而欲盡復正課
吾恐正課不可必復而坐失餘鹽之利也
今之鹽法正課與餘鹽相權而竝行其始
議曰多不爲功少不爲嫌無抑勒以取盈
===
蓋亦知今之餘鹽非眞山海之藏有盈溢
特恐妨鹽法之正而姑爲之名使上不失
國初實邊之意而下亦從商人之便耳然事
有召釁而法有啓奸宋人之初刺義勇也
約以不守邊未幾而發之守邊且涅其手
矣宋人之初置義倉也約以不輸郡未幾
而發之輸郡且恣鞭撻矣今法正課與餘
鹽竝行安知後之人不以多爲功而抑勒
以取盈乎此則草茅之所深慮也且
punctuated:
令矣。不議行此，而惟欲變通鈔法，吾恐無以惠貧竈，而處之終于無術也。屯政之廢弛久矣。當烽堠希警，田穀布野，輕變而折銀，誠罪也。今邊城晝閉，地多不耕，乃強而輸粟，非情也。以所輸之銀歸常平爲糴本，亦可得芻粟之用。今不議此，而欲盡復正課，吾恐正課不可必復，而坐失餘鹽之利也。
今之鹽法，正課與餘鹽相權而竝行。其始議曰：「多不爲功，少不爲嫌，無抑勒以取盈。」蓋亦知今之餘鹽，非眞山海之藏有盈溢，特恐妨鹽法之正，而姑爲之名，使上不失國初實邊之意，而下亦從商人之便耳。然事有召釁，而法有啓奸。宋人之初刺義勇也，約以不守邊，未幾而發之守邊，且涅其手矣。宋人之初置義倉也，約以不輸郡，未幾而發之輸郡，且恣鞭撻矣。今法正課與餘鹽竝行，安知後之人不以多爲功，而抑勒以取盈乎？此則草茅之所深慮也。且
translation_en:
…an order to that effect had been issued. If we do not consider implementing this, but wish only to modify the paper-currency system, I fear we shall have no means of benefiting impoverished salt producers and ultimately find no way to deal with their plight. The administration of military agricultural colonies has long fallen into neglect. When alarms at the beacon posts were rare and grain covered the fields, rashly changing the system to commute grain payments into silver was indeed culpable. But now, when frontier cities keep their gates shut even by day and much land lies uncultivated, compelling deliveries of grain is unreasonable. If the silver paid in were assigned to the Ever-Normal Granaries as capital for purchasing grain, it could likewise provide the means to obtain fodder and grain. If we do not consider this now, but instead wish to restore the regular salt quota in full, I fear that its restoration cannot be assured, while we needlessly forfeit the benefits of surplus salt.
Under the present salt system, the regular quota and surplus salt operate side by side, each balancing the other. The initial proposal stated: “A larger amount shall not count as merit, nor a smaller amount as grounds for reproach; there shall be no coercion to exact the full amount.” This surely also recognized that today’s ‘surplus salt’ does not represent a genuine overflowing abundance of the resources of mountains and seas. Rather, fearing interference with the regular salt system, they provisionally adopted this designation, so that those above would preserve the dynasty’s original intention of provisioning the frontier, while those below would also accommodate the convenience of merchants. Yet undertakings can invite trouble, and laws can open the way to abuse. When the Song first tattooed men enrolled in the Volunteer Militia, they promised that these men would not have to defend the frontier. Before long, however, they dispatched them to frontier duty and even tattooed their hands. When the Song first established the Charitable Granaries, they promised that the grain would not be transported to the prefecture. Before long, however, they ordered it transported there and even resorted to unrestrained flogging. Under the present regulations, the regular quota and surplus salt operate side by side. How can we know that future administrators will not count larger receipts as merit and use coercion to exact the full amount? This is what deeply concerns me, a man outside official service. Moreover…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
國初之優竈户者至矣給鈔給米之
令可考也優商人者至矣每引輸銀八分之
令可考也惟時正課蓋三十萬引耳後變爲
七十萬則倍之矣今餘鹽至三百餘萬則
數倍矣竈户之採辦日益多而不恤其私
商人之中納日益難而不償其直雖嚴刑
督之安能使課入之必充哉昔劉晏理財
以養民爲先此晏之賢所以異于桑孔也
自有海寇以來商人困于焚掠竈户逼于
===
屠戮失業者不知其幾矣愚謂今之鹽法
當以優恤商竈爲先優恤既至則人知所
歸異日課入之充羨雖日倍于昔如晏之
在兩淮可也此鹽法始末之可議者也愚
嘗思之司計之臣所爲皇皇焉日憂夫財
之不足者非不知愛民也凡以夷狄盜賊
之憂無以處之也蓋自殘胡雲擾于西北
倭夷飈發于東南守臣不足以制變于是
有員外之置額兵不足以禁□□是□□
punctuated:
國初之優竈户者至矣，給鈔給米之令可考也。優商人者至矣，每引輸銀八分之令可考也。惟時正課蓋三十萬引耳，後變爲七十萬，則倍之矣；今餘鹽至三百餘萬，則數倍矣。竈户之採辦日益多，而不恤其私；商人之中納日益難，而不償其直。雖嚴刑督之，安能使課入之必充哉？昔劉晏理財，以養民爲先，此晏之賢所以異于桑孔也。自有海寇以來，商人困于焚掠，竈户逼于屠戮，失業者不知其幾矣。愚謂今之鹽法，當以優恤商竈爲先。優恤既至，則人知所歸，異日課入之充羨，雖日倍于昔，如晏之在兩淮可也。此鹽法始末之可議者也。
愚嘗思之，司計之臣所爲皇皇焉日憂夫財之不足者，非不知愛民也，凡以夷狄盜賊之憂無以處之也。蓋自殘胡雲擾于西北，倭夷飈發于東南，守臣不足以制變，于是有員外之置；額兵不足以禁□□，是□□
translation_en:
…At the founding of the dynasty, salt-producing households received the utmost favorable treatment: the orders granting them paper currency and grain can be consulted. Merchants likewise received the utmost favorable treatment: the order requiring payment of eight fen of silver for each salt certificate can be consulted. At that time, the regular salt quota amounted to only some 300,000 certificates. Later it became 700,000, more than twice as much; now surplus salt amounts to over three million certificates, several times that figure. Salt-producing households must procure ever more, yet no consideration is given to their own needs; merchants find it increasingly difficult to make the payments required to obtain salt certificates, yet receive no adequate return for their outlay. Even if they are driven on with harsh punishments, how can the full receipt of salt revenues be assured? In former times, Liu Yan put sustaining the people first in managing public finances. This was the virtue that distinguished him from Sang Hongyang and Kong Jin. Since the maritime raiders appeared, merchants have suffered burning and plunder, and salt-producing households have faced slaughter. Countless people have lost their livelihoods. In my humble opinion, the salt administration today should give priority to favorable treatment and relief for merchants and salt producers. Once such care is fully extended, people will know where to turn. Thereafter, salt revenues may become abundant and yield a surplus—even growing day by day to twice their former level, as under Liu Yan in Lianghuai. These are the matters concerning the development of the salt administration that merit discussion.
I have often reflected on this: the officials responsible for public finances are so anxious, worrying daily that funds will be insufficient, not because they do not know to care for the people, but because they have no means of dealing with the troubles caused by foreign peoples and bandits. Since the remaining Hu forces have swarmed turbulently in the northwest and the Japanese raiders have risen like a whirlwind in the southeast, the officials charged with defending those regions have proved unable to contain these emergencies, and appointments beyond the authorized establishment have consequently been made. The regular troop establishment has proved insufficient to suppress [illegible], and [illegible; the wording is uncertain] [?]…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
發之兵經費之領于司農者始皇皇無以
爲計矣愚則以爲固國之本在恤民恤民
之實在省賦省賦之實在治軍治軍之實
在擇吏今之置吏溢于舊額者多矣不惟
其賢而惟其多則官多祗以爲擾也今之
置兵溢于舊額者亦多矣不惟其精而惟
其多則兵多祗以階亂也且賊之入寇也
或近在百里之内而我之調兵也乃望救
于千里之外是祗以勤民而何及于事也
===
賊之深入也各持必死之志而我之禦之
也多嬰以内顧之民是祗以資賊而何益
于守禦也故曰養兵十萬則五萬之費可
去也屯兵十年則五年之費可去也此今
財用之所以詘而事不立也爲今之計亦
惟稍假督撫以事權俾之訓練士兵爲持
久不可動之計而已矣自有寇盗以來練
兵之
令數下而奉行鮮有效者亦以兵未易練而
punctuated: 發之兵，經費之領于司農者，始皇皇無以爲計矣。愚則以爲，固國之本在恤民，恤民之實在省賦，省賦之實在治軍，治軍之實在擇吏。今之置吏溢于舊額者多矣，不惟其賢而惟其多，則官多祗以爲擾也。今之置兵溢于舊額者亦多矣，不惟其精而惟其多，則兵多祗以階亂也。且賊之入寇也，或近在百里之内，而我之調兵也，乃望救于千里之外，是祗以勤民，而何及于事也？賊之深入也，各持必死之志，而我之禦之也，多嬰以内顧之民，是祗以資賊，而何益于守禦也？故曰：養兵十萬，則五萬之費可去也；屯兵十年，則五年之費可去也。此今財用之所以詘而事不立也。爲今之計，亦惟稍假督撫以事權，俾之訓練士兵，爲持久不可動之計而已矣。自有寇盗以來，練兵之令數下，而奉行鮮有效者，亦以兵未易練而
translation_en: …the troops dispatched, and those drawing funds for their regular expenses from the Ministry of Revenue, have consequently become alarmed, with no means of making provision. In my humble opinion, the foundation of securing the state lies in caring for the people; genuinely caring for the people lies in reducing taxation; reducing taxation lies in putting the army in order; and putting the army in order lies in selecting officials. Many officials are now appointed beyond the former quotas. If attention is paid only to their numbers, rather than their worthiness, more officials merely cause more harassment. Many troops are likewise now established beyond the former quotas. If attention is paid only to their numbers, rather than their quality, more troops merely pave the way for disorder. Moreover, when bandits invade, they may be close at hand, within a hundred li, yet in mobilizing troops we look for relief from a thousand li away. This merely burdens the people: how can it meet the emergency in time? When bandits penetrate deep into our territory, each is resolved to die, while in resisting them we are often encumbered with men anxious about their families. This merely supplies the bandits with resources: how does it help our defense? Thus I say: of the expense of maintaining a hundred thousand troops, that for fifty thousand could be eliminated; of the expense of stationing troops for ten years, that for five years could be eliminated. This explains why financial resources are now exhausted while nothing is accomplished. The present remedy is simply to grant the supreme commanders and grand coordinators somewhat greater authority over affairs, enabling them to train the soldiers and establish an enduring, unshakable defense. Since the onset of banditry, orders to train troops have repeatedly been issued, yet those implementing them have seldom achieved results. This too is because troops cannot readily be trained, and…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
敵患已逼故不得不倚夫調發之兵也愚
以爲土兵之當練者有二在武衛之世襲
則有專任而練之也易在郡縣之數遷則
無常任而練之也難今郡邑之練兵旣格
于守令之數遷而武衛之舉行者亦鹵莽
甚矣誠嚴比試之法如
國初使武衛皆得其人乃使聯其什伍而肄
之以戰陣之法督撫時閱其精否而行賞
罰有不精者則罰必行嚴贓吏之法如
===
國初使守令皆得其人乃使擇民壯勇而肄
之以都試之法督撫時閱其精否而行賞
罰有不精者則罰必行仍撫之以恩愛而
饑寒困苦有必恤示之以節制而亂行失
伍有必誅使所練之兵無事則樂耕而和
于國有事則樂戰而和于軍而督撫之勤
于事者時特
褒奬增秩賜金久任以責其成則兵不外借
財不外出即有夷狄盜賊之憂亦可坐制
punctuated: 敵患已逼，故不得不倚夫調發之兵也。愚以爲土兵之當練者有二：在武衛之世襲，則有專任而練之也易；在郡縣之數遷，則無常任而練之也難。今郡邑之練兵旣格于守令之數遷，而武衛之舉行者亦鹵莽甚矣。誠嚴比試之法如國初，使武衛皆得其人，乃使聯其什伍，而肄之以戰陣之法，督撫時閱其精否而行賞罰，有不精者則罰必行；嚴贓吏之法如國初，使守令皆得其人，乃使擇民壯勇，而肄之以都試之法，督撫時閱其精否而行賞罰，有不精者則罰必行。仍撫之以恩愛，而饑寒困苦有必恤；示之以節制，而亂行失伍有必誅。使所練之兵無事則樂耕而和于國，有事則樂戰而和于軍。而督撫之勤于事者，時特褒奬，增秩賜金，久任以責其成，則兵不外借，財不外出，即有夷狄盜賊之憂，亦可坐制
translation_en:
…the threat from the enemy is already pressing, so there is no choice but to rely on troops mobilized from elsewhere. In my humble view, there are two categories of local troops that ought to be trained. In the military guards, where offices are hereditary, responsibility is vested in designated officers, making training easy; in the prefectures and counties, where officials are frequently transferred, there is no continuity of responsibility, making training difficult. At present, training troops in the prefectures and counties is obstructed by the frequent transfer of prefects and magistrates, while the military guards also conduct it with extreme carelessness.

If the rules for competitive military examinations were truly enforced as strictly as at the founding of the dynasty, ensuring that the military guards were all staffed by suitable men, these officers could then be directed to organize their troops into squads of ten and five and drill them in battlefield formations. Supreme commanders and grand coordinators should periodically inspect their proficiency and administer rewards and punishments; wherever proficiency is lacking, punishment must invariably follow. If the laws against corrupt officials were enforced as strictly as at the founding of the dynasty, ensuring that all prefects and magistrates were suitable men, they could then be directed to select strong and courageous men from among the people and drill them according to the methods of the general military muster. Supreme commanders and grand coordinators should periodically inspect their proficiency and administer rewards and punishments; wherever proficiency is lacking, punishment must invariably follow.

They should also care for the troops with kindness and affection, invariably providing relief when they suffer hunger, cold, or hardship; and they should instruct them in military discipline, invariably executing those who disrupt the ranks or abandon their units. Thus, the trained troops would gladly cultivate the land and live harmoniously within the realm in peacetime, and gladly fight and serve harmoniously within the army in wartime. Supreme commanders and grand coordinators who diligently attend to their duties should from time to time receive special commendations, promotions in rank, and monetary gifts, and should be retained in office for long terms so that they may be held accountable for achieving results. Then troops need not be borrowed from elsewhere, nor funds sent outside the region. Even if threats arose from foreign peoples or bandits, they could be kept under control with ease…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而無橫決之患夫然後財賦之節省可議
也昔人謂害財之大者莫大于冗吏冗兵
國初之征商甚薄而用常有餘者亦以其設
官制兵之有節而無浮冗之蠹耳今之財
用誠急矣獨不可求
國初之故而調停消息以處夫吏兵之冗乎
誠使擇吏必賢而任職者皆牧民馭衆之
才則員外之置可漸省也員外之置省則
廪祿之省當不止一二也練兵必精而在
===
營者皆有勇知方之士則調發之兵可漸
省也調發之兵省則餽餉之省當亦不止
一二也費出有經則賦可寬征斂有藝則
民可裕民心欣悅則邦本益固夷狄盜賊
之憂必且消弭而不足以勤執政之慮太
倉之儲亦且貫朽粟陳不可勝用而鹽筴
之多寡固有不足言者矣此則經制之略
昔人所謂萬世之計者是也如使二冗不
去惟財用之急而抑勒以取盈雖使管仲
punctuated: 而無橫決之患。夫然後財賦之節省可議也。昔人謂害財之大者，莫大于冗吏、冗兵。國初之征商甚薄，而用常有餘者，亦以其設官制兵之有節，而無浮冗之蠹耳。今之財用誠急矣，獨不可求國初之故，而調停消息，以處夫吏兵之冗乎？誠使擇吏必賢，而任職者皆牧民馭衆之才，則員外之置可漸省也。員外之置省，則廪祿之省當不止一二也。練兵必精，而在營者皆有勇知方之士，則調發之兵可漸省也。調發之兵省，則餽餉之省當亦不止一二也。費出有經，則賦可寬；征斂有藝，則民可裕。民心欣悅，則邦本益固，夷狄盜賊之憂必且消弭，而不足以勤執政之慮。太倉之儲亦且貫朽粟陳，不可勝用，而鹽筴之多寡固有不足言者矣。此則經制之略，昔人所謂萬世之計者是也。如使二冗不去，惟財用之急，而抑勒以取盈，雖使管仲
translation_en:
…and there would be no danger of their breaking loose unchecked. Only then could economies in public revenue and expenditure be considered. Men of former times said that nothing harmed the public finances more than superfluous officials and superfluous troops. At the founding of the dynasty, commercial taxes were very light, yet funds regularly exceeded expenditure. This was simply because official appointments and military establishments were kept within limits, without the drain of unnecessary personnel. The present need for funds is indeed pressing. Yet could we not investigate the practices of the dynasty’s founding and make appropriate adjustments to deal with these excess officials and troops?

If officials were invariably chosen for their worth, and all who held office possessed the ability to govern the people and direct the multitude, appointments beyond the established complement could gradually be reduced. Once such appointments were reduced, the savings in stipends would certainly be considerable. If troops were invariably trained to proficiency, and all those in the camps were men of courage who understood right conduct, the troops mobilized from elsewhere could gradually be reduced. Once those mobilizations were reduced, the savings in military provisions and pay would likewise be considerable.

With expenditure governed by regular standards, taxes could be lightened; with fixed limits on exactions, the people could prosper. When the people were content, the foundation of the state would grow firmer. The troubles caused by foreign peoples and bandits would surely subside and no longer burden those conducting affairs of government. The stores of the Grand Granary would likewise become so abundant that the strings of cash would rot and the grain grow old before they could all be used. The amount of revenue from the salt monopoly would then scarcely merit discussion. This is the outline of a lasting institutional arrangement—what men of former times called a plan for ten thousand generations. If, however, these two kinds of superfluous personnel were not eliminated, and the pressing need for funds led only to coercive exactions to make up the required amount, then even if Guan Zhong were entrusted with the task…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
爲之亦難以善其後矣仲之相齊也進賢
有賞蔽明有罰一時所與若高傒鮑叔甯
戚之徒皆齊國之良則仲之設官亦有節
不多取庸懦以充位也其作內政也居則
相親戰則相赴三軍之衆可使相爲用如
左右手故能以三萬人而方行天下則仲
之制兵亦有節不多取老弱以充數也夫
是以吏易祿兵易贍而齊稱富疆也鹽筴
之征仲亦不専恃之以爲國也今之經國
===
者顧可出管仲之下哉愚也溺所聞而昧
時務然效忠之意亦耿耿久矣敢陳固陋
若言之可採與否則未敢知也惟執事教
焉
punctuated: 爲之，亦難以善其後矣。仲之相齊也，進賢有賞，蔽明有罰。一時所與，若高傒、鮑叔、甯戚之徒，皆齊國之良，則仲之設官亦有節，不多取庸懦以充位也。其作內政也，居則相親，戰則相赴，三軍之衆可使相爲用，如左右手，故能以三萬人而方行天下，則仲之制兵亦有節，不多取老弱以充數也。夫是以吏易祿，兵易贍，而齊稱富疆也。鹽筴之征，仲亦不専恃之以爲國也。今之經國者，顧可出管仲之下哉？愚也溺所聞而昧時務，然效忠之意亦耿耿久矣。敢陳固陋，若言之可採與否，則未敢知也。惟執事教焉。
translation_en:
…were to undertake it, even he would find it difficult to bring matters to a satisfactory conclusion. When Guan Zhong served as chief minister of Qi, he rewarded those who advanced worthy men and punished those who obscured men of ability. Those with whom he worked at the time, such as Gao Xi, Bao Shu, and Ning Qi, were all outstanding men of Qi. Thus Guan Zhong exercised restraint in establishing offices: he did not recruit numerous mediocre and timid men merely to fill positions. In organizing domestic government, he ensured that men were close to one another in daily life and came to one another’s aid in battle. The hosts of the Three Armies could thus support one another like the left and right hands. For this reason, he could march unimpeded throughout the realm with thirty thousand men. Thus Guan Zhong also exercised restraint in organizing the army: he did not recruit numerous old and weak men merely to fill the ranks. Consequently, officials were easy to remunerate and soldiers easy to provision, and Qi was renowned for its wealth and strength. Even Guan Zhong did not rely exclusively on revenue from the salt monopoly to govern his state. Can those who manage the state today really allow themselves to fall below Guan Zhong?

I am immersed in what I have learned and ignorant of current affairs; nevertheless, my desire to serve loyally has long burned bright. I venture to set forth these ill-informed views, though I dare not presume to know whether my words merit adoption. I ask only that you, honored examiners, instruct me.

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄後序
嘉靖戊午秋八月天下復當
選士於鄉應天府臣循例預
請
上命〔臣景淳臣陞〕往典試事旣取士
如式疏名梓文以
獻〔臣陞〕職宜有序〔臣〕嘗讀菁莪
棫樸成周孕毓賢俊在於岐
豐而綱紀作人實惟壽考以
基之則知
===
今日南畿才賢之盛是
高皇帝開先文教而
聖天子久道作人之功也維茲
聖祖肇跡一時佐
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄後序

嘉靖戊午秋八月，天下復當選士於鄉。應天府臣循例預請，上命〔臣景淳臣陞〕往典試事。旣取士如式，疏名梓文以獻。〔臣陞〕職宜有序。〔臣〕嘗讀《菁莪》《棫樸》，成周孕毓賢俊在於岐、豐，而綱紀作人，實惟壽考以基之，則知今日南畿才賢之盛，是高皇帝開先文教，而聖天子久道作人之功也。維茲聖祖肇跡，一時佐
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the wuwu year of Jiajing [1558], the time had again come to select men throughout the empire through the Provincial Examination. The officials of Yingtian Prefecture submitted their advance request according to precedent, and His Majesty commanded [your servants Jingchun and Sheng] to go and preside over the examination. Having selected the men in accordance with the prescribed procedures, we listed their names in a memorial and printed their examination essays for presentation to the throne. It falls within the duties of [your servant Sheng] to provide a postface.

[Your servant] has read “Luxuriant Mugwort” (Jing E) and “The Oaks” (Yu Pu). The flourishing Zhou nurtured its worthy and outstanding men in Qi and Feng; yet the ordering and cultivation of men rested fundamentally upon the ruler’s longevity. Thus we know that the present abundance of talented and worthy men in the Southern Metropolitan Region is the achievement of Emperor Gao, who inaugurated its literary instruction, and of our sagely Son of Heaven, whose enduring adherence to the Way has cultivated its men. When our sagely dynastic founder first rose to prominence, those who assisted him at that time …

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
命元勲雲蒸風從多出其地嗣
是諸儒碩亦彬彬然後先相
望故人士視海內獨繁殆豐
芑之遺也我
皇上統真斯文嘉惠庠序每屢
明詔崇雅黜浮士忻忻軼于古
卽疏逖阻深猶祗承
===
德意烝耀光明矧是
畿甸首善拭觀向邇者乎
甄陶鼓鑄已逾三紀于茲淪入
浸漬含生之類莫不革心矧
於多士乎夫周南化始西北
漸於江漢維時兔罝之士尚
任干城腹心況此由來衣被
punctuated:
命元勲，雲蒸風從，多出其地。嗣是諸儒碩亦彬彬然，後先相望，故人士視海內獨繁，殆豐芑之遺也。我皇上統真斯文，嘉惠庠序，每屢明詔，崇雅黜浮，士忻忻軼于古。卽疏逖阻深，猶祗承德意，烝耀光明，矧是畿甸首善，拭觀向邇者乎？
甄陶鼓鑄，已逾三紀于茲，淪入浸漬，含生之類莫不革心，矧於多士乎？夫周南化始西北，漸於江漢，維時兔罝之士尚任干城腹心，況此由來衣被
translation_en:
…the meritorious founding ministers who assisted in establishing the dynasty rose like clouds and followed like the wind; many came from this region. Thereafter, eminent Confucian scholars likewise appeared in cultivated abundance, succeeding one another in an unbroken line. Thus, compared with the rest of the realm, this region has been uniquely rich in learned men—surely a surviving legacy of the luxuriant millet celebrated in the Odes, an image of nurturing talent. Our Emperor presides over this cultural tradition [?] and graciously favors the schools. Through repeated explicit edicts, he honors refinement and rejects superficiality; scholars rejoice and surpass those of antiquity. Even in remote places separated by formidable barriers, people reverently receive his benevolent intentions and shine with their radiance. How much more must this be so in the metropolitan region, foremost in moral example, among those who look toward him from nearby [?]?
His shaping and nurturing of men has now continued for more than three twelve-year cycles. Its influence has penetrated and steeped them so thoroughly that none among the living fail to reform their hearts—how much more, then, the multitude of scholars? The transforming influence celebrated in the Southern Zhou section of the Odes began in the northwest and spread to the Jiang and Han rivers. Even the men celebrated in “The Rabbit Net” could then serve as shields and walls of the state and as trusted intimates. How much more these men, who have long been clothed in…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
文教比
皇上垂意留都根本裁成樂育每
先列服士游歌鼓舞選善不
知其
道化所涵濡固有行誼文學之
彥出而翊贊
宸謨若
===
神武明作則必有隨世建義之雋
騈然竝出爲
國家宣力效勞奮庸熈載樹屛
翰寄封疆以輸忠於內外者
始臣膺
□□□謂玆才賢之藪庶幾得人
□□
punctuated:
文教，比皇上垂意留都根本，裁成樂育，每先列服。士游歌鼓舞，選善不知其道化所涵濡，固有行誼文學之彥出而翊贊宸謨。若神武明作，則必有隨世建義之雋，騈然竝出，爲國家宣力效勞，奮庸熈載，樹屛翰，寄封疆，以輸忠於內外者。
始臣膺□□□，謂玆才賢之藪，庶幾得人□□
translation_en:
…cultural instruction. Of late, His Majesty has devoted attention to the foundational importance of the auxiliary capital. In shaping and gladly nurturing talent, he has consistently given it precedence over the other regions. The scholars sing at their leisure and dance with joy, choosing goodness [?], unaware of how his moral transformation has permeated and nourished them. Among them there are assuredly men distinguished in conduct and literary learning who will come forward to assist in imperial deliberations. When divine martial prowess is illustriously displayed, outstanding men who establish righteous undertakings suited to the times will surely emerge together in abundance. They will exert themselves in service to the state, displaying their abilities and bringing its affairs to prosperity; they will stand as its protective bulwarks and be entrusted with its frontiers, offering their loyalty both within and beyond the court.
When I, your servant, first received [three illegible characters], I thought that here, in this gathering place of talented and worthy men, we might hope to obtain suitable men [two illegible characters]…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖明疇咨至意而臣偲偲然恐無
以稱塞
任使亦或藉此少紓萬一乃與
同事者胥飭胥慫夙夜殫竭
心力縱觀多士之文類能深
嘶并包誦說稱引閎而肆淵
而達彪曄而有則渢渢洋洋
===
天下之鉅麗備焉正如鍾山
石城多雄偉峭拔之狀而青
冥秀鬱不可攬結又如長江
大海渾溢浩蕩而驚濤迅湍
下上掩抑令人望而却焉臣
於是竦嘆曰猗休哉信人文
之炳蔚矣然臣猶有懼焉文
punctuated: 聖明疇咨至意，而臣偲偲然恐無以稱塞任使，亦或藉此少紓萬一。乃與同事者胥飭胥慫，夙夜殫竭心力。縱觀多士之文，類能深嘶并包，誦說稱引，閎而肆，淵而達，彪曄而有則，渢渢洋洋，天下之鉅麗備焉。正如鍾山、石城，多雄偉峭拔之狀，而青冥秀鬱，不可攬結；又如長江、大海，渾溢浩蕩，而驚濤迅湍，下上掩抑，令人望而却焉。臣於是竦嘆曰：「猗休哉！信人文之炳蔚矣！」然臣猶有懼焉，文
translation_en: …Your enlightened Majesty’s earnest intention in seeking worthy men through consultation. Yet I, your servant, anxiously feared that I could not adequately discharge the commission entrusted to me; through this, perhaps, that anxiety might be relieved in some small measure. Thus my colleagues and I admonished and encouraged one another, exhausting our mental and physical powers day and night. Surveying the candidates’ compositions, I found that most displayed depth [?] and breadth of comprehension. In their exposition and citation, they were expansive and unrestrained, profound yet lucid, brilliantly ornamented yet governed by rules. Rich and overflowing, they embodied all the grandeur and beauty under Heaven. They were just like Zhongshan and Shicheng, with their many majestic, steeply soaring forms, their verdant heights luxuriant in the blue distance, impossible to grasp and gather in; or like the Changjiang and the great ocean, surging full and vast, with startling waves and swift currents rising and falling, overtaking and pressing one another down, making the beholder recoil. At this I exclaimed in awed admiration: “How splendid! Truly, human culture shines here in flourishing brilliance!” Yet I still harbored a fear: literary refinement…

title: 嘉靖三十七年應天府鄉試錄
text:
與質迭爲興廢昔先王之制
治以質文相救但自質而趨
文也易自文而復質也難吳
故文盛之地而惟恐質之不
勝也力變而歸質茲非其時
乎邇嵗吳茲蔓於吳武備日
嚴而文不加少固將啓多士
===
以收蕩平者定之功耳夫文
武交資而成能是以吉甫功
焯當時聲施後世誠得若人
而舉之天下之真士也第今
所據者文而已孰能預卜他
日之真似哉彼惑於似士者
而失於真士是黎丘丈人之
punctuated: 與質迭爲興廢。昔先王之制治，以質文相救。但自質而趨文也易，自文而復質也難。吳故文盛之地，而惟恐質之不勝也。力變而歸質，茲非其時乎？邇嵗吳茲蔓於吳，武備日嚴，而文不加少，固將啓多士以收蕩平者定之功耳。夫文武交資而成能，是以吉甫功焯當時，聲施後世。誠得若人而舉之，天下之真士也。第今所據者文而已，孰能預卜他日之真似哉？彼惑於似士者而失於真士，是黎丘丈人之
translation_en:
…and substance alternate in their ascendancy and decline. In establishing good government, the former kings used substance and refinement to remedy one another’s deficiencies. Yet it is easy to move from substance toward refinement, and difficult to return from refinement to substance. Wu has long been a place where literary refinement flourishes; the concern is that substance may not be strong enough. Is this not the time to strive for change and return to substance? In recent years, [something] has spread through Wu [?]. Military preparations have grown more stringent by the day, yet literary activity has not diminished. Surely this will inspire the many scholars to achieve the work of pacification and stabilization [?].
Civil and military accomplishments draw upon one another to produce capability. Thus Jifu’s achievements shone in his own day, and his fame spread to later generations. If we could indeed find and promote such a man, he would be a true scholar of the realm. Yet at present, all we have to judge by is writing. Who can foretell whether someone will later prove genuine or merely a semblance? To be deceived by those who resemble true scholars and thereby overlook true scholars is the old man of Liqiu’s…
